# dsh-cleaner

English | [中文](README-zh.md)

[![ci](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-cleaner/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-cleaner/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-none-brightgreen)
![build step](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-none-brightgreen)
![dsh](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh-0.2.2--rc.1-blue)

> Deletes stored logs, never a live session.

A DeepSeek Harness profile bundle for the one thing the product does not do: remove a session's log. It
lists what is still on disk, waits while a person decides, deletes exactly the ids they approve, and
reports the bytes reclaimed. No schedule, no age threshold, no background sweep, and **no need to archive
first** — archiving is how the sidebar hides a session, not a permission to delete one.

[github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-cleaner](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-cleaner)

## Status

- Current version: v0.2.8.
- **Exercised in a real profile on this machine** (2026-11-13): installed from this directory, both
  tools appeared, `list_session_logs` reported the six logs, and `delete_session_logs`
  removed exactly those six directories — 4,169,349 bytes reclaimed, 0 failed, 0 refused. The mounted
  `sessionPersistence` backend confirmed it no longer lists them, a second listing reported zero
  candidates with all six explained as already gone, and an independent directory count agreed: 36
  session directories before, 30 after, with the running session untouched.
- **Checked with the Host's own schema validator**, taken out of the installed `0.2.2-rc.1` asar: both
  output schemas pass `assertSupportedJsonSchema`, the check `tools.register()` runs before a tool exists
  at all; both parameter schemas pass the stricter object-root assertion and accept exactly the argument
  shapes the tools document (an invented argument, a string where an array belongs, or a missing required
  field is rejected); and both real results pass `validateJsonSchemaValue` against the output schema they
  declare. The schema check alone is not activation — the live run above is what proves that.
- **Not covered yet**: a deletion that fails partway, a link inside a real session directory, and a
  Harness build whose storage layout differs from `0.2.2-rc.1`. The first two are fixture-tested; the
  third fails safely (zero candidates) and is described in [docs/design.md](docs/design.md) §8.
- `scripts/check.mjs` never loads the Harness, and it is not meant to: activation is what a profile
  shows, not what a repository can prove.
- Release list: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Mechanism and state matrix:
  [docs/design.md](docs/design.md). Decisions: [the ADRs](docs/adr/).

## The contract

Archiving a session in DeepSeek Harness only hides it: the log stays on disk forever. Nothing in the
product removes it, and the official persistence seam cannot — `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence`
documents "No deletion or retention API — pruning stored sessions is out-of-band backend maintenance"
as a known limitation, and its JSONL backend states it plainly: "Nothing deletes session files — logs
accumulate under root until removed externally." This bundle is that external removal, and it obeys one
rule:

**Deletion is an act somebody asked for, never a schedule.** There is no timer, no interval, no age
threshold and no background sweep in this plugin, and a profile cannot configure one into it. Removal
happens only inside a tool call, after a person has seen the list.

The two tools are the three steps:

| Step | Tool | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| list | `list_session_logs` | Lists the sessions whose logs are on disk, with each one's bytes, file count, last write and whether it is archived. No argument, no side effect — calling it can never be a mistake. |
| confirm | — | The person reads the list and approves ids. Nothing happens during this step. |
| delete | `delete_session_logs` | Takes the approved ids by name, removes those session directories, and reports the bytes reclaimed. |

`delete_session_logs` requires the ids, so nothing is ever deleted by default and a subset can be
approved. Archived and unarchived sessions are both deletable; what it refuses, and reports instead of
failing, is:

- the session running the command, and any session whose agent is **busy** (the refusal names the status);
- an id that is no longer on disk;
- a session directory the plugin will not touch: a link, or one holding anything but regular files.

The same operation is a **human command**, so a deletion does not need a model turn. Its name is `clean`,
and it is typed with a leading slash:

```
/clean                     → the listing, as text in the transcript
/clean <id> <id> …         → deletes exactly those, and reports the bytes
```

It runs through the host's command registry (`ctx.remote.commands.execute`), which resolves the command
and runs it *without* sending anything to the model: no turn, no request, no context window spent on a
decision you have already made. Both callers end in one implementation, so a person typing and a model
calling cannot disagree ([ADR 0011](docs/adr/0011-one-operation-two-callers.md)).

A session's own **⋯ menu** carries the same thing as one row — *删除会话* / *Delete session*, in the window's
language, drawn in the same red as 删除工作区, with the trash glyph the product registers for it, sorted last of every session action. It is a data
contribution to the menu, not a renderer: the bundle supplies the label, the icon key and the click, and the
sidebar draws it like its own actions. The row appears only when the host really has the `clean` command —
the window half reloads with the page and the host half only with the process, and a row whose command the
host has never heard of turns a click into ordinary text, which reads as a failure that never happened.

## Install

The profile links to a directory, so the clone is what runs — put it somewhere it can stay:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-cleaner.git ~/code/dsh-cleaner
```

Then install that absolute path into the profile you use. In the desktop app, ask for it: the model calls
`plugin_manager` with `install_bundle` and the path — the route this repository was verified with. A
profile the CLI owns (`web`, `headless`, `sdk`) takes the same path through `dsh plugin`, which forwards
to pnpm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ~/code/dsh-cleaner
```

There is no build step, no dependency and no install script: `index.js` and `engine.js` use only `node:`
builtins and each other.

**Updating** is `git pull` in that clone and a restart of the app: the host reads the bundle when it
starts, so a running window keeps the code it loaded. **Removing** is `plugin_manager` with
`remove_bundle`, or `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-cleaner` on a CLI profile; the clone, the
store, and every deletion already made are untouched.

After installing, the card in the plugin list reads **Cleaner** — `Deletes stored logs, never a live
session.` If the card is there with its switch on, the bundle loaded.

## First use

There is no interface to open: you ask in ordinary language and the model calls the tools. One real
exchange, from the live run recorded in [Status](#status):

```
> Which sessions are still taking space?

list_session_logs {}
← Session logs on disk: 6, 4169349 bytes (3.98 MiB) (6 of them archived).
  The session store holds 36 directories, 94607680 bytes (90.22 MiB) in all.
    "导入 Claude Code 聊天记录"  session-36560858-…  182051 bytes (177.8 KiB)  3 files  archived  last write 2026-11-02T07:39:15.053Z
    "询问模型身份"  session-177a4f1f-…  2475067 bytes (2.36 MiB)  1 file  archived  last write 2026-11-03T02:14:07.060Z    …
  Nothing was deleted. Show this list to the person and call delete_session_logs with the ids
  they approve — archived or not.

> Delete the six you listed. Keep nothing.

delete_session_logs { session_ids: ["session-36560858-…", "session-177a4f1f-…", …] }
← Deleted 6 session directories: 4169349 bytes (3.98 MiB) reclaimed.
    "导入 Claude Code 聊天记录"  session-36560858-…  182051 bytes (177.8 KiB)  3 files    …
  The workspace records dropped them (6 detached): an archived session is hidden by the sidebar, so
  the rows are gone from every open window without a reload.
  The session persistence backend no longer lists any of them.
```

## What it never does

- Never touches a session that is running the command, or one whose agent is **busy** — the refusal names
  the status, so "wait for its work" is distinguishable from "the plugin refused for a reason you cannot
  see". An agent the host merely keeps in memory does not block a deletion
  ([ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-busy-not-resident.md)).
- Never deletes anything nobody named. The store is the index — every session whose log is on disk is a
  candidate, archived or not — and the deleting tool only ever receives ids the listing printed.
- Never follows a link. Symlinked project and session directories are skipped rather than entered, a
  session directory holding anything but regular files is refused and reported rather than removed,
  every candidate is resolved under the session storage root before a byte is unlinked, and files are
  unlinked one at a time instead of handing a recursive delete a whole tree.
- Never opens a session log, reads an event or rewrites a line. The unit of removal is the session's
  own directory, whole — no session format is parsed, so no future format can be misread.

## Where it works

`DSH_HOME` (default `~/.dsh`), and under it the two paths the engine takes as arguments:

- `<DSH_HOME>/sessions/<project-key>/<session-id>/` — the session's own directory, as
  `dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` lays it out (`session.vN.jsonl.zstd` generations inside it). The
  directory name is the backend's own escaping of the id, reproduced in `engine.js`; every generation
  in the directory is part of the same session and goes with it.
- `<DSH_HOME>/storages/workspace.json` — read only, for `global.archivedSessionIds`: the archive flag a
  listing shows, and the ids an earlier deletion may have left behind. It is not a gate — a session
  without an archive entry is a candidate like any other.
- `<DSH_HOME>/storages/session_projcache/sessions/<id>.json` — read only, for one row: the session's
  title, shown beside the id so a list of ids can be matched against the sessions someone remembers by
  name. A missing, older or unreadable file costs the title and changes nothing else.

The workspace file is never written, and neither is the project's session list: the plugin **asks** the
registry to detach the deleted ids from their project and to archive them, which is what makes the row go
away ([ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-detach-by-asking.md)). Archiving is the lever, not a tidiness step: the
sidebar draws no archived session, and the registry publishes the change to every open window, so **the row
disappears at once — no reload, no restart, no sort switch**
([ADR 0012](docs/adr/0012-archive-never-unarchive.md)). Never unarchiving is the point: that call belongs
to a restore, and it is what used to put a deleted session's row back on screen. The one copy no host event
reaches is the window's own persisted sidebar view, and the bundle's browser half prunes it at every page
load ([ADR 0007](docs/adr/0007-browser-half-prunes-the-view.md)).

## What it does not do

- **No unarchive, no re-archive, no pinning.** It removes logs and nothing else, then asks for the two
  record changes that make the row disappear: detach it from its project, archive it. The second one is
  why a deletion needs no reload — an archived session is never drawn
  ([ADR 0012](docs/adr/0012-archive-never-unarchive.md)). The plugin writes no workspace record itself
  ([ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-detach-by-asking.md)).
- **Never a session whose work is running.** The session executing the command is always kept, and so is
  any session whose agent is busy; the refusal names the status (`a live agent holds this session (status:
  running)`) so the reason is something to act on. An agent that is merely resident — archived work has
  stopped, the harness still keeps the object in memory — does not block the deletion
  ([ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-busy-not-resident.md)).
- **No projection cache eviction.** The harness keeps per-session projections under
  `storages/session_projcache/`, and this plugin reads one row from them — the title it shows beside an
  id — and writes nothing: a deleted session may keep a stale row and its cache file until the runtime
  rewrites or drops it. Derived data, self-healing, and cheaper than parsing a log to find a name.
- **No attachment cleanup.** Images and files a session carried live in a content-addressed store
  (`attachments/v1/objects`), not in the session directory: one object can belong to several sessions,
  and finding a session's references would mean parsing its log, which this plugin refuses to do. That
  store is 54 MiB on the machine this was written on, and it is left alone.
- **No schedule, no retention policy, no size cap.** Deleting is a decision, not a rule.
- **No proof that a person approved the list.** The ids make the approved set explicit in the
  conversation and the refusals bound the damage, but a model could still name an id nobody looked at.
  See [ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-two-tools-with-explicit-ids.md).
- **No log repair.** A corrupt or unreadable log is still deleted when its session is named: this
  plugin is the cleanup path of last resort, so it must not depend on the log being parseable.

## Where this fits

Three ways to make a session's log go away, and what each one actually refuses to do. The middle column
was read from `dsh-session-cleaner` v1.0.2's published code, not from its summary.

| | this plugin | `dsh-session-cleaner` | doing it by hand |
|---|---|---|---|
| surface | two model-facing tools | a web UI menu item and an HTTP route | a shell |
| what it will delete | any session log on disk, named by a person | any session with no attached agent | whatever the glob matches |
| the running session | refused by id, always | refused while its agent is running | not refused — the glob does not know |
| what it reports | candidates, bytes, last write, store total, per-id result | detach / workspace / file counts | nothing |
| writes the workspace records | asks the registry to detach the deleted session; never edits the store | yes, it detaches the session | no |
| survives a wrong id | refuses it and says why | n/a — it takes one id from a menu | deletes the wrong session |

Neither tool is a superset of the other: `dsh-session-cleaner` reaches its deletion through a menu item
and an HTTP route, so a person clicks instead of naming ids. This plugin's whole design is about being
unable to delete anything nobody printed in a listing — and since v0.2.0 it does delete unarchived
sessions too, so the "already hidden" restriction is gone from the list of differences.

## Questions

**I archived a session by mistake — is it gone?**
Not until something is deleted. This plugin never writes the archive list, so unarchiving still works
while the files are there, and a session restored between the listing and the deletion is refused by
name.

**Does it work while the harness is running?**
Yes: it reads the workspace file and unlinks session directories, and holds no handle to the session
store. The session running the command is always refused, and so is any session a live agent holds. A
deleted session's row may linger in the UI until the runtime refreshes — see the projection cache note
above.

**Will it delete sessions that are not archived?**
Yes. Archiving is the product's way to hide a session, not this plugin's permission to delete one: the
store is the index, so an unarchived session is a candidate and can be deleted by id like any other. The
listing shows each session's archive state because it tells you whether the row is already hidden.

**Can a deletion be undone?**
No. Each session's directory is unlinked file by file, and there is no trash to restore from: the
workspace record stays, but the log behind it does not. That is the whole reason the surface is "list,
then name ids" — the listing is the only preview there is.

**Why does the listing show a last-write time?**
It is the newest file's write time in that session directory — the last time the session appended
anything. That is the fact that turns "delete all six" into a decision: of the six in the exchange
above, the oldest last wrote on 2026-11-02 and the newest on 2026-11-12, and nothing else in the output
separates them.

**Where does the title in the listing come from?**
The projection cache the harness keeps beside the store — the same name the sidebar shows. It is read
from that file and never written, no log is opened to find it, and a session without one is listed by id
alone.

**How does it know how big the store is?**
It walks every project directory under `sessions/` once per listing. That walk is also what makes an
archived id with no directory visible as `already_gone`, which is the state a second run finds.

## Troubleshooting

**The model does not offer the tool.**
The bundle is not loaded in this profile. The plugins page should show the **Cleaner** card and the
profile's `package.json` should list `dsh-cleaner`; if both are true and the tools are still missing,
restart the app — a window keeps the plugin list it booted with.

**It lists nothing, and the disk is still full.**
The listing reports the size of the whole store next to what it found: nothing listed against a 90 MiB
store means the sessions are gone and the space is held by something this plugin does not remove — the
projection cache and the attachment store.

**A refusal names a reason I do not understand.**
The reasons are: `a live agent holds this session (status: …)` — its work is still running, so wait for
it; `no session directory is stored under that id` — a second call with the same ids, or a session
deleted from another window; and `its directory is not a candidate: …`, where the reason after the colon
names the shape this plugin refuses to touch (a link, or a directory holding something that is not a
file).

**A deletion says `Partially removed`.**
A file could not be unlinked — usually a lock held by an indexer or an antivirus. The answer names the file
and the bytes freed so far, the directory stays, and the id is still a candidate, so the same call can
simply be run again.

**The card still shows an older description after an update.**
The host reads the bundle when it starts: `git pull` updates the files, but a running window keeps the code
and the locale it loaded. Restart.

**A deleted session is still in the sidebar.**
It should not be: the plugin archives the session as part of the deletion, and the sidebar never draws an
archived session, so the row goes the moment the registry change reaches the window — that is a live
stream, not a reload. What is left is a record, not a row: the archive set names an id with no directory,
which the listing reports as `already_gone`, and which appears only if you switch the archived filter to
*show* or *only*. If a row really is still drawn, the window kept a copy from before the change: a page
load also prunes the window's own persisted view, and a restart rebuilds the client's session list. One
case is stated rather than fixed: a session the host still holds in memory keeps its *name* in that list
until the host releases it (a restart does; no plugin API can), and the answer says so when it happens
(`the host holds that session in memory`).

## Compatibility

- **DSH**: verified against the installed `0.2.2-rc.1` desktop build. The storage layout and the id
  escaping in `engine.js` were read from that build's `app.asar`
  (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence` and its JSONL backend), not from memory. A later build that
  renames either is the one change this plugin cannot absorb by itself — and it fails safely: zero
  candidates, every archived id reported as already gone (`docs/design.md` §8).
- **Session format**: one directory per session with `session.vN.jsonl.zstd` generations inside. No
  format is parsed, so every released generation, and any later one, is covered by construction.
- **Node**: `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. CI runs `npm test` on both majors and all three platforms (Linux,
  macOS, Windows); the flag that puts the suites in one process is spelled per major, and
  `scripts/test.mjs` chooses it from the running version, so the same command works on each.

## Security

What the plugin trusts, what it can be made to delete, and what it cannot touch:
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Verify

```sh
node scripts/check.mjs     # manifest, dependency surface, schemas, locales, patch, documents
node --check index.js      # the bundle entry parses as ESM
node --check engine.js
npm test                   # the fixture tests, one process on purpose
```

The suites share one process deliberately: the default runner spawns one process per test file, and a
confined sandbox refuses that spawn. Node 24 spells the flag `--test-isolation`, Node 22
`--experimental-test-isolation`, so `scripts/test.mjs` picks the spelling for the running major rather
than repeating it in package.json, CI and here. CI runs that same `npm test` on both majors and all
three platforms, which is what makes the spelling and the platform green rather than claimed.

No test touches a real `DSH_HOME`. The engine takes the session storage root and the workspace storage
file as arguments, every engine test passes fixture paths, and the entry tests point `DSH_HOME` at a
fixture. A dry run against the real store is a separate, deliberate act:

```sh
node -e "import('./engine.js').then(async (m) => console.log(JSON.stringify(await m.planCleanup({
  sessionsRoot: process.env.DSH_HOME + '/sessions',
  workspaceFile: process.env.DSH_HOME + '/storages/workspace.json',
}), null, 2)))"
```

`planCleanup` only reads: it is safe to run at any time, and it is the same call `list_session_logs`
makes. It never deletes; `applyCleanup` is the only function that does.

| Why two tools, and why explicit ids? | [ADR 0003](docs/adr/0003-two-tools-with-explicit-ids.md) |
| Why are links and irregular directories refused? | [ADR 0004](docs/adr/0004-refuse-links.md) |
| Why is a plan checked again when it is executed? | [ADR 0005](docs/adr/0005-re-verify-at-execution.md) |
| Why does it detach a deleted session instead of editing the workspace file? | [ADR 0006](docs/adr/0006-detach-by-asking.md) |
| Why does the bundle carry a browser half? | [ADR 0007](docs/adr/0007-browser-half-prunes-the-view.md) |
| Why does a busy agent block a deletion, and a resident one not? | [ADR 0008](docs/adr/0008-busy-not-resident.md) |

# dsh-team

English | [中文](README-zh.md)

[![ci](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-team/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-team/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue)
![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-none-brightgreen)
![build step](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-none-brightgreen)

> Only the person changes, not the work.

A DeepSeek Harness profile bundle for the one thing the shipped agent-team roster cannot do: let a member
go. A Lead can retire one, restore it from a trash it controls, or replace it with a successor that
inherits the assignment, the work still in flight, and a pointer to the Lead's own task board. It owns
the roster and has no browser half.

[github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-team](https://github.com/FrozenYty/dsh-team)

## Status

- Current version: v0.41.4.
- **Exercised in a real profile on this machine.** Retirement, restore, message, stop, a replacement whose
  successor finished the predecessor's work, the trash cap and its refusal at load, the handoff template,
  spawn options and the forwarded route, the task board and its transfer, the three host hooks, and the
  one-shot sweep with the consent gate — recorded field by field in `PROGRESS.md`'s 2026-11-13 entry. The
  plugin's own state move is no longer a plan: this profile's roster is a file, `<workspace>/.agents/team/
  roster.json`, imported from the storage domain with a marker beside it, and the migration ran against
  that live data — **110 records, 20 artifacts moved, 4,913,598 bytes verified at the destination, 46
  tombstones reconciled to `pruned`, 44 left alone by reason, 0 refused.** The backup manifest and the
  destination directory agree on the byte total, `4,913,598` both ways across 20 files, which is the only
  reason the word "verified" is used here.
- **Checked with something stronger than a reading.** **247 tests** pass and `scripts/check.mjs` prints
  `check passed`; between them they cover the write-time caps, a retirement during an in-flight spawn,
  overlapping roster writes, the route fallbacks, the definition chain, the member-scope read, and the
  lifetime sweep and consent gate. The defect this release fixed was also **reproduced live before it was
  fixed**: for a record whose bytes the retention cap had deleted, `restore_member` answered
  `reason: "pruned"`, and for a spawned one it answered `trash-missing` with **no `reason` field at all**.
  Both answers are in `PROGRESS.md`, and the trash held 20 directories before and after each probe.
- **Asked the Host's own validator, out of the installed archive.** `scripts/schema-check.mjs` extracts
  `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` 0.2.2-rc.1 from the asar and runs the functions the registry itself runs:
  `assertSupportedJsonSchema` accepted **11 of 11 output schemas**, `validateJsonSchemaValue` accepted
  **13 real results**, and the Host rejected nothing. Three parameter schemas use `maxLength`, which is
  outside the Host's keyword subset — and the check established *why* that survives rather than merely
  that it does: `register()` asserts `output.schema` only and projects parameters to the model unasserted,
  so a cap is enforced by the action when the value arrives, not at the schema boundary. It is a local
  check and not a CI gate, because CI has no Harness.
- **Not covered yet**: activation in anyone else's profile — `scripts/check.mjs` never loads the Harness,
  so no repository can prove that; a Harness build whose services or storage layout differ from the
  installed one; and the `rename` fast path of the trash move, which this machine never took, because its
  data roots sit on different volumes and every move was the verified copy path (`EXDEV`) instead. The
  archive bound is in the same position: it runs on the first write after a reload and never on a read, so
  this profile's roster has not flushed yet — a tombstone leaving for `archive.jsonl` past the retention
  window is covered by the suite, not yet by a live observation here.
- Release list: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Append-only history: [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md).

## Install and verify

```
plugin_manager  install_bundle  target: <absolute path to this repository>
```

The install links this directory into the profile rather than copying it, so what runs is this working
tree and there is no build step. Verification afterwards is live calls, not `check.mjs` output:

- the patch row activates with `application: applied` and no warnings;
- `list_members` is callable from a Lead session, reports context pressure for a resident member, and
  answers `host_hooks` with `panel_filter`, `roster_filter` and `slot_credit` as `"installed"` and a
  non-zero `stripped_ids` once this Lead has retired someone — a hook that never installed reads
  `"absent"` and its `message` names the service it waited for;
- `retire_member` returns `trashed: true` and a `trash_path` for a session that has an artifact, and
  `spawn_member` with `replace` returns `predecessor_retired: true` with the successor at the next
  generation, reporting `transferred` with the task ids when the predecessor owned open work;
- a plain `spawn_member` answers `started_with.route_source: "plugin"` in a profile whose Session route
  is readable, and the member's own Session `request/header` names that same provider and model;
- `wait_members` answers `no_progress` when nothing is running, and returns a member's target when a
  message you sent it ends its turn;
- a Lead's tool list holds this plugin's tools and none of `spawn_teammate`, the shipped `wait_agent` or
  `team_task_*` — while `list_agents`, `send_message` and `interrupt_agent` remain, because they come
  from the shipped service row this patch keeps mounted;
- the shipped **成员** panel lists a member started here, and after `retire_member` the row is gone rather
  than relabelled; the **子智能体** picker and the shipped `list_agents` lose the same member.

## First use

There is no interface to open: you ask in ordinary language and the model calls the tools, so the roster
is managed by conversation. One real exchange — a member is spawned with an assignment, then replaced:

```
> Give the sum to a helper and tell it to stand by.
spawn_member { name: "handoff-probe", label: …, prompt: …,
  assignment: "Compute 6 * 7 and reply with the single number, nothing else." }
← target: "handoff-probe", generation: 1, phase: "active", …

> I don't need it any more. Replace it with a successor and retire it.
spawn_member { replace: "handoff-probe", label: …, prompt: … }
← target: "handoff-probe-g2", generation: 2, predecessor_retired: true,
  assignment: "Compute 6 * 7 and reply with the single number, nothing else.", …

handoff-probe-g2, which never saw its predecessor, replies: 42
```

Three commands cover most of the surface: `spawn_member` starts a member — with `replace` it hands a role
over instead of growing the team — `list_members` shows every member the Lead controls with its live
state, and `retire_member` (or `restore_member`) ends a role or takes it back. Abridged from an
acceptance run recorded in [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md).

## Why the shipped roster is not enough

The shipped experimental Agent Teams roster cannot let a member go. It is a fold over the Lead Session's
append-only event log with closed phases `provisioning | active | failed`: the projection throws on any
transition out of a terminal phase and records that throw as a permanent failure, so a synthetic
"retired" record poisons the projection rather than failing safely. `maxMembers` (16) is checked against
a list that never shrinks, names are never reused, and upstream's redesign still defers deletion
(ADR 0001). This plugin supplies the missing half without forking the shipped roster: its own roster on
the Harness subagent substrate, a real `retired` phase, a reusable name at the next generation, and a
session trash that is a move rather than a deletion.

## The tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `spawn_member` | Starts a named member as a continuable child. `definition` starts it from a file, `spawn_options` gives it its own directory, route or preset, `replace` starts a successor and retires the predecessor in one call, and `lifetime` says whether the role is `standing` or `one-shot`. |
| `list_members` | Every member this Lead controls, with phase, generation, assignment, lifetime, route, live state and context pressure — and a sweep of finished one-shot members before it answers. |
| `wait_members` | Blocks this turn until a member's live status changes, or a bounded timeout expires. |
| `message_member` | Delivers one message to a live member, optionally replacing its recorded assignment. |
| `stop_member` | Cancels the member's current turn and keeps its activation and inbox. |
| `retire_member` | Ends a role: drain, tombstone, move the persisted Session to the trash, enforce the retention cap. A standing member that still carries something needs the person's answer first. |
| `restore_member` | Moves a trashed Session back to its recorded path and returns the record to `active`. |
| `compact_member` | Forces one compaction on a resident, idle member. |
| `handoff_template` | Reads, stores or clears the brief a successor receives. |
| `task_board` | This Lead's own work board: `create`, `list`, `update`, `release` or `delete` a task. |
| `list_my_tasks` | **A member's own read**, not the Lead's: the rows whose `owner` is that member. |

The authoritative table — every result field, every refusal, the consent gate, the workspace overlay —
is [docs/architecture-en.md](docs/architecture-en.md) §5; the model also sees each tool's own description
at call time. What that table does not answer is which model a member runs on: that is
[docs/routes-en.md](docs/routes-en.md).

## A member is a division of labour

`spawn_member` asks how long the member lives. `standing` (the default) is a role you expect to use
again: never retired automatically, and ending it is the person's decision. `one-shot` is the fan-out
case — a member built for one piece of work, which the sweep retires by itself once it has run, stopped
and owns no open task. Messaging a one-shot member re-opens it rather than converting it, and the plugin
never converts one on its own count.

Ending a `standing` member that still carries something — a recorded assignment, an open task, evidence
it was re-tasked — needs the person's answer, quoted verbatim; one that carries nothing is housekeeping
and retires on a stated reason. A member can also be a file on disk instead of a paragraph in a call:

```markdown
---
name: reviewer
label: Review the diff
assignment: Check every changed file for behaviour changes
model: a-cheaper-model
---
You review changes. Report only findings that change behaviour, with the file and the line.
```

The whole subject is [docs/member-lifecycle-en.md](docs/member-lifecycle-en.md) — the four phases, the
state matrix, the sweep's three conditions and the consent gate — with the file format in
[docs/architecture-en.md](docs/architecture-en.md) §6. Replacing a member is
[docs/handoff-en.md](docs/handoff-en.md) for the brief, and
[docs/task-board-en.md](docs/task-board-en.md) for the work it hands over.

## Limits and deliberate omissions

Five things this bundle does not do, each decided rather than forgotten.

- **One record per Lead, and no cross-process lock.** The roster and this Lead's board live in one JSON
  document — `roster.json` under `.agents/team/` in the Lead's workspace (ADR 0027). Nothing serializes
  two processes over it (ADR 0010), so two Harness processes over one workspace are last-writer-wins: if
  both write the same Lead, the later write replaces the earlier one and the update it never read is lost.
  That is correct for one running Harness, which is how subagents themselves work; the plugin adds no
  lock file, and the second writer is reported as `foreign_write_at` when this process next reads or
  writes.
- **No browser half of its own.** There is no plugin panel, HTTP bridge or client bundle.
  v0.3's Settings panel was never rendered in a real profile and its clicks did not work, so v0.4 deleted
  it rather than repairing it (ADR 0008). What the panel shows is overlaid at the host's session-list
  exit (ADR 0023): its **成员** section lists this plugin's live members, and a retired member leaves the
  panel rather than being marked. The overlay only reads: it can neither retire nor replace anything, and
  it cannot write the Session log, which is why the shipped fold's closed phases (ADR 0001) do not apply
  to it. Every operation remains a model-facing tool, and a future UI is a new decision that starts from
  the operations in `actions.js`.
- **The shipped `agent-team` service row stays mounted.** Adoption, the membership test and the
  projection filter read it, so the patch cannot disable it — and that service publishes three
  model-facing tools of its own, `list_agents`, `send_message` and `interrupt_agent`, which therefore
  remain in a Lead's tool list. The patch retires the shipped *tool* row (`tool-agent-team`); removing
  those three would take the service, and this plugin's adoption, with them (ADR 0017).
- **A pruned tombstone cannot be restored.** A retirement that moves an artifact in enforces the
  per-Lead trash cap and removes the oldest entries past it. The tombstone keeps its `trashDir` and
  records `trashState: pruned`, but the bytes are gone, so `restore_member` refuses with
  `reason: "pruned"` and never calls the workspace (ADR 0011, ADR 0028). Configure a larger cap before a
  long-lived team needs more than 20 recoverable sessions.
- **The task board is a handover channel, not a project tracker.** A task has an id, a title, a bounded
  body, `open`/`done` and an optional owner, and deliberately no priorities, dependencies, comments,
  sub-tasks or due dates (ADR 0017, ADR 0020). Dependencies would need a graph and an ordering rule, and a
  handover would then have to decide what to do with a task whose dependency is still open; that order
  stays the Lead's judgment. The board answers one question: what work does the successor carry now?

## Configuration

The plugin keeps its data under `.agents/team/` in the Lead's workspace — `roster.json`, and a `trash/`
holding retired sessions. A profile that sets `DSH_TEAM_DATA_DIR` (or the pre-rename
`DSH_TEAM_ROSTER_DATA_DIR`) uses that directory instead, and the frozen `~/.dsh/team-roster` is what a
Session with no workspace of its own falls back to, so every Session has somewhere to write and no write
falls through to the storage domain. A new root with no roster file reads its records once from the file
`DSH_TEAM_SEED` names — this plugin's own shape or a storage-domain dump — and a seed that is configured
and unusable is reported rather than quietly ignored. The storage domain answers no read; it is opened
once more, for one release, only to migrate a profile that has never bound a workspace (ADR 0014,
ADR 0027, ADR 0031).

One Lead's trash keeps at most **20** retired sessions. The cap is the `trashLimit` field of the bundle's
patch row, so a profile changes it in its own `cordis.patch.yml` by id:

```yaml
- id: team-roster
  config:
    trashLimit: 7
```

That `id` is frozen at `team-roster` while the package is `dsh-team`: it is the key a profile uses to
address this row, so renaming it would silently stop the override from matching (ADR 0014). The field
must be an integer of at least 1 — `0`, negatives, fractions, numeric strings, `NaN` and an explicit
`null` are refused at load, before any tool is registered, with a message that names the field, the value
and the minimum. The entry declares no `Config` **schema**, so the provider reports `include:dsh-team` as
`absent`: that is the schema projection rather than a statement about configurability, because only a
native Schemastery schema projects and a zero-import bundle (ADR 0002) cannot import one (ADR 0012).

## Requirements and compatibility

**To run**, the bundle needs the installed Harness and the shipped packages it reads — not npm
dependencies: it is linked into a profile and imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` package (ADR 0002), so what runs
is this working tree. It reads the subagent seam, the shipped `agent-team` service, `sessionController`
(the projection filter and the panel overlay; a host that never publishes it reports
`panel_filter: "absent"` instead of losing the hook silently), `agentTeams.listMembers`, the token meter,
the storage-domain facility, and the agent registry with its `agent/status` event. `compact_member` also
needs a mounted compaction backend, which the patch's `compaction-basic` entry enables. Every host-side
effect is capability-probed and installs only when the service it wraps exists, so a Harness whose shape
changed skips that effect and says so in `list_members` rather than failing the load. A profile that does
not mount the experimental team bundle has no `tool-agent-team` row to disable; the Loader warns about the
missing target and skips that entry.

## Development

```sh
node --check index.js actions.js roster.js definitions.js trash.js host-hooks.js
node --test --test-isolation=none tests/*.test.mjs
node scripts/check.mjs
```

The three commands are the whole local gate. `--test-isolation=none` is not optional: Node 22 spells it
`--experimental-test-isolation`, so the flag itself fixes the major version at Node 24, and the default
runner spawns one process per test file, which this machine's sandbox refuses. CI pins Node 24 and runs
the same command, so a local pass is the same statement as a green run. `scripts/check.mjs` cannot prove
the plugin works — it never loads the Harness.

## Repository layout

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `index.js` | Host plugin entry: tool definitions, argument validation, Lead-only authority check |
| `actions.js` | The roster operations behind the tools |
| `roster.js`, `trash.js` | Durable roster (phases, name generations, adoption, migration) and the session trash with its restore and retention cap |
| `definitions.js` | The definition layer: the flat-frontmatter parser, the scan across the definition chain and its caps, the team file's handoff template, and the working directories all are resolved from |
| `host-hooks.js` | Projection filter (strip retired ids, add this plugin's live members to the team panel), shipped roster-read filter, roster slot credit, and the deferred install of all three |
| `tests/`, `scripts/check.mjs` | Unit tests, and the repository checks CI runs |
| `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, `locale/`, `icon.svg`, `templates/`, `.github/` | The bundle, the five role templates it ships, its CI workflow and templates |
| `PLAN.md`, `PROGRESS.md`, `docs/` | Open tasks, the append-only change log, and the design documents (bilingual) with the ADRs |

## Where everything else lives

| Question | Document |
|---|---|
| How does a member move between phases, and what do a retirement and a replacement do in what order? | [docs/member-lifecycle-en.md](docs/member-lifecycle-en.md) |
| The work board, the handover, and why a board write cannot undo one | [docs/task-board-en.md](docs/task-board-en.md) |
| The brief a successor receives, and which template wins | [docs/handoff-en.md](docs/handoff-en.md) |
| The stored record, the trash and the retention cap | [docs/roster-storage-en.md](docs/roster-storage-en.md) |
| Layers, the Harness substrate, the full tool surface, the risks | [docs/architecture-en.md](docs/architecture-en.md) |
| Which model a member runs on, and what bills what | [docs/routes-en.md](docs/routes-en.md) |
| Upgrading from v0.13 or earlier | [docs/upgrading-en.md](docs/upgrading-en.md) |
| Why a decision is what it is | [docs/adr/](docs/adr/), indexed in [docs/INDEX-en.md](docs/INDEX-en.md) |
| What changed, release by release | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for the summary, [PROGRESS.md](PROGRESS.md) for the evidence |

[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) is for AI assistants; [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) covers branches, commits
and CI.

# 📦 @goodandready/dsh-russian-lang

Полная русская локализация, умная типографика и исправление раскладки клавиатуры для DeepSeek Harness

🇷🇺 Русский • 🇨🇳 中文说明 • 📐 Design Contract

⭐ Если вам нравится этот плагин, поставьте ему звезду на GitHub — это покажет мне, что плагин вам полезен, и будет мотивировать меня развивать его дальше.

🐛 Если вы нашли баг или хотите предложить новый функционал, создайте issue на GitHub на любом языке — я рассмотрю ваше предложение и реализую полезные идеи в одной из следующих версий плагина.
--- ## ⚡ Обзор **`dsh-russian-lang`** — официальный, всеобъемлющий пакет русской локализации для веб-интерфейса [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh). Пакет не просто переводит интерфейс ядра и всех популярных плагинов экосистемы, но и добавляет интеллектуальные функции для комфортной русскоязычной работы: **100% ручная вычитка терминов**, **грамматические формы множественного числа (plural)**, автоматическую **расстановку экранной типографики** («ёлочки», длинные тире, неразрывные пробелы) и **исправление ошибочно набранного текста** на неверной раскладке по горячей клавише Alt+L. ```mermaid graph LR subgraph DSHCore [Ядро DeepSeek Harness] DSH[Web UI Интерфейс] --> Loader[Загрузчик локализации dsh-russian-lang] end subgraph TranslationLayer [Слой перевода и адаптации — 10 432 ключей / 100% вычитано] Loader --> CoreDict[58 Пространств имён ядра DSH / 2 442 ключа] Loader --> PluginDict[43 Пространства имён плагинов DSH / 7 781 ключа] Loader --> PluralEngine[Движок грамматических Plural-форм: 1/2/5] end subgraph SmartFeatures [Интеллектуальные модули] Loader --> Typo[Модуль типографики: кавычки-«ёлочки» и длинные тире] Loader --> LayoutFix[Детектор неверной раскладки + Hotkey Alt+L] Loader --> Spell[Активация русской проверки орфографии] Loader --> Overrides[Пользовательские переопределения ключей] end subgraph Result [Результат] CoreDict --> NativeUI[Нативный русский интерфейс] PluginDict --> NativeUI PluralEngine --> NativeUI Typo --> NativeUI LayoutFix --> NativeUI Spell --> NativeUI Overrides --> NativeUI end style DSHCore fill:#1e1e2e,stroke:#89b4fa,stroke-width:2px,color:#cdd6f4 style TranslationLayer fill:#181825,stroke:#cba6f7,stroke-width:2px,color:#cdd6f4 style SmartFeatures fill:#11111b,stroke:#a6e3a1,stroke-width:2px,color:#cdd6f4 style Result fill:#181825,stroke:#f38ba8,stroke-width:2px,color:#cdd6f4 ``` --- ## ✨ Полный обзор возможностей ### 1. 🌐 100% покрытие ядра DSH (58 пространств имён, 2 442 ключа) * **Диалоги и переписка (`conversation`)**: лента сообщений, ветки обсуждений, карточки вызова инструментов, статус генерации и рассуждений (thinking traces). * **Модели и провайдеры (`settings.models`)**: каталог моделей, параметры инференса, управление токенами и ключами API. * **Трейсы рассуждений (`trajectory`)**: детальные шаги, параметры вызовов инструментов, временные метки и визуализация размышлений модели. * **Настройки ядра (`settings`, `common`, `settings.theme`)**: параметры подключения, горячие клавиши, системные уведомления, масштабирование шрифтов, модальные окна и подтверждения. * **Рабочие области (`workspace`, `subagent`)**: дерево файлов, управление контекстом, запуск и координация субагентов. * **Планировщик и инвентарь (`schedule.catalog`, `settings.pluginInventory`, `settings.plugins`)**: фоновые задания, периодичность, фильтры и каталог установленных плагинов. * **Права доступа и безопасность (`permission.access`, `plan`, `skill`)**: пресеты прав (полный доступ, только чтение, запись в рабочую область), выполнение планов и навыки. > **О качестве перевода.** Все **10 432 ключей интерфейса (2 619 ядра + 7 813 плагинов) переведены на 100% и вычитаны вручную**. Черновой машинный перевод полностью замещён проверенными формулировками (`draft = 0`). Перевод регулярно валидируется автоматическими линтерами целостности плейсхолдеров, проверкой соблюдения глоссария (`glossary.json`) и детекторами переполнения верстки. Нашли неточность — кнопка «Сообщить о проблеме перевода» в карточке настроек создаёт готовый issue. ### 2. 🧩 Встроенный перевод 65+ плагинов экосистемы DSH (7 781 ключа) Локализация автоматически распространяется на все ключевые плагины экосистемы DeepSeek Harness: * **`dsh-session-control`** — расширенное управление сессиями: закрепление диалогов, архив по периодам, просмотр расшифровок и фильтрация шума; * **`dsh-kanban` и `task-board`** — канбан-доски задач, карточки, чек-листы, дедлайны, критерии готовности (DoD) и шлюз приёмки (Acceptance Gate); * **`dsh-cost-meter`** — учёт стоимости токенов, калькуляция расходов и тарифные сетки моделей в реальном времени; * **`dsh-goal`** — автономный целеполагающий агент с безопасным циклом и рефлексией; * **`dsh-moa`** — многоагентная архитектура Mixture-of-Agents; * **`dsh-context-lens` и `dsh-context`** — визуализатор и оптимизатор контекста, аналитика токенов и сжатие; * **`dsh-time-machine`** — снимки рабочей области и откат состояний файлов; * **`dsh-shadow-auditor`** — теневой аудит изменений и безопасность; * **`dsh-cron` и `schedule.catalog`** — планировщик периодических cron-задач; * **`dsh-clinebot` и `im-hub`** — интеграции и шлюзы для Telegram, Discord, Slack; * **`dsh-subscriptions`** — управление персональными подписками на модели; * **`dsh-voice` и `dsh-tts`** — распознавание речи и голосовое озвучивание; * **`dsh-image-gen`** — генерация изображений; * **`dsh-lanmode`** — сетевой доступ по локальной сети и генерация TLS-сертификатов; * **`dsh-model-sync`** — синхронизация моделей и эндпоинтов; * **`dsh-usage-guard` и `token-dashboard`** — контроль лимитов и аналитика расходов токенов; * **`skills-manager` и `dsh-skill-hub`** — менеджер навыков агента и витрина способностей; * **`commandcode` и `settings.commandcode`** — провайдеры команд и аккаунты; * **`better-sidebar`, `better-input`, `opencode-palette`, `context-doctor`, `plugin-store`, `autoReview`** и др. ### 3. 🔢 Русские грамматические формы числительных (Plural) Английский язык различает только `1` и `other`. Русский язык требует 3 грамматические формы числительных (`1 файл`, `2 файла`, `5 файлов` / `1 секунда`, `3 секунды`, `10 секунд`). Движок локализации автоматически подставляет правильные окончания в зависимости от числового значения. ### 4. ✍️ Интеллектуальный модуль типографики (`russian-lang.typography`) Автоматически приводит тексты сообщений и описаний к правилам русской экранной типографики: * Заменяет прямые "лапки" на правильные кавычки-«ёлочки» (а вложенные — на „лапки“); * Заменяет дефисы между словами на длинные тире (—); * Добавляет неразрывные пробелы после коротких союзов и предлогов, предотвращая висячие строки; * **Безопасность кода**: типографика строго изолирована и никогда не затрагивает блоки исходного кода, формулы LaTeX и моноширинные поля ввода. ### 5. ⌨️ Исправление ошибочной раскладки клавиатуры (Alt+L) Если вы забыли переключить раскладку и набрали текст латиницей (например, `ghjtrn d gzkmt` вместо `проект в пальто`), плагин мгновенно: * Определяет ошибочный ввод в реальном времени; * Показывает ненавязчивую плавающую подсказку над полем ввода; * При нажатии горячей клавиши Alt+L мгновенно конвертирует набранный текст в правильную кириллицу. ### 6. 🔍 Интерактивный Инспектор перевода и живые оверрайды (Alt+Click / Alt+I) Мощный встроенный инструмент для инспекции строк интерфейса и мгновенного редактирования переводов на лету: * **Точечная инспекция (Alt+Click)**: зажмите клавишу Alt и кликните по любому элементу интерфейса (кнопке, пункту меню, лейблу), чтобы открыть модальное окно инспектора. * **Постоянный режим (Alt+I)**: переключает интерфейс в интерактивный режим исследования — наведение курсора подсвечивает элементы аккуратной рамкой с бейджем источника (`Core`, `Plugin`, `DOM`, `Untranslated`), а в правом нижнем углу экрана отображается плавающий статус-виджет с кнопкой быстрого выхода. * **Модальное окно инспектора**: * Точное определение системного ключа, пространства имён и типа источника. * Быстрое копирование ключа или готового стандартизированного Markdown-сниппета для баг-репорта в 1 клик. * Поле ввода собственного перевода (оверрайда) с кнопкой **«Применить»**: мгновенно изменяет текст в DOM и сохраняет оверрайд в настройки (`russian-lang.overrides`) без перезагрузки страницы. Все аналогичные элементы интерфейса обновляются автоматически. * Кнопка **«Сбросить»** для мгновенного отката к стандартному словарному переводу. * **Управление в карточке настроек (Раздел 4.5)**: * Кнопка быстрого включения/выключения инспектора (Alt+I). * Кнопки **«Экспорт JSON»** и **«Импорт JSON»** для резервного копирования, переноса и синхронизации списка ваших оверрайдов между браузерами и рабочими профилями. ### 7. ⚡ Оптимизации производительности и архитектурная безопасность * **Пакетная обработка MutationObserver**: оптимизированный наблюдатель мутаций интерфейса с адаптивным debounce (16 мс) предотвращает лавинообразные перерисовки и перерасчёт макета (reflow) при интенсивном рендеринге списков и стриминге LLM-токенов. * **Защита HTTP-маршрутов словарей (405 Method Not Allowed)**: серверные эндпоинты `/api/dsh-russian-lang/dict/core`, `/api/dsh-russian-lang/dict/plugins`, `/api/dsh-russian-lang/dict/all` строго защищены и принимают только безопасные методы GET/HEAD. * **Клиентский бандл с запасом**: оптимизированная архитектура и компактный бутстрап обеспечивают размер клиентского скрипта 153.7 KiB (запас более 10 KiB до предельного лимита). ### 8. 🔤 Нативная интеграция в ядро Плагин нативно регистрирует пункт **«Русский»** в меню **Настройки → Общие → Язык**, переключает атрибут `` и активирует встроенный браузерный словарь проверки орфографии (`spellcheck`). --- ## Requirements - **DeepSeek Harness (DSH)**: `0.2.0-rc.2 || >=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.2.2-0 || >=0.2.2-0 <0.2.3-0` - **Node.js**: `>= 22.0.0` - **Браузеры**: Chromium 110+, Firefox 115+, Safari 16+ ## 📦 Установка ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add @goodandready/dsh-russian-lang ``` После установки откройте веб-интерфейс, перейдите в **Настройки → Общие → Язык**, выберите **«Русский»** и обновите страницу. --- ## ⚙️ Параметры конфигурации (`settings.yaml` / профиль Cordis) В актуальных версиях DSH (v0.2.0-rc.2+, v0.1.7+) конфигурация плагина управляется штатно через managed-форму в веб-интерфейсе (**Настройки → Плагины → Русская локализация**) либо в профиле/конфиге под идентификатором плагина `dsh-russian-lang` (согласно `cordis.patch.yml`). Для полной обратной совместимости с ранними версиями ядра (DSH <= 0.1.6) плагин также автоматически поддерживает чтение из легаси-пространства `russian-lang`. Схема параметров объявлена в [`lib/index.js`](lib/index.js), все поля необязательные: ```yaml # Актуальный формат (DSH v0.2.0-rc.2+ / v0.1.7+): dsh-russian-lang: enabled: true # Русский язык интерфейса (по умолчанию: true) overrides: {} # Пользовательские оверрайды ключей (по умолчанию: {}) typography: # Интеллектуальная типографика (по умолчанию: все opt-in false) enabled: false # Ёлочки, длинные тире, неразрывные пробелы yo: false # Восстановление безопасной буквы «ё» liveInput: false # Живая типографика при вводе в текстовых полях agentPrompt: false # Системная инструкция агенту отвечать по-русски (по умолчанию: false) agentPromptPreset: technical_expert # Пресет системного промпта (по умолчанию: technical_expert) slashAliases: true # Русские алиасы слэш-команд (/помощь, /очистить) (по умолчанию: true) layoutConversion: true # Детектор неверной раскладки и подсказка Alt+L (по умолчанию: true) quickSwitch: true # Быстрый переключатель RU/EN в статусной строке (по умолчанию: true) translateEngine: off # Движок перевода реплик: off, local (LibreTranslate) или google (Google) (по умолчанию: off) localApiUrl: http://localhost:5000 # URL локального инстанса LibreTranslate (по умолчанию: http://localhost:5000) # Легаси-формат (DSH <= 0.1.6, поддерживается автоматически как fallback): # russian-lang: # enabled: true # ... ``` Удобнее всего настраивать параметры визуально в интерфейсе: **Настройки → Плагины → Русская локализация**. Исправление раскладки (Alt+L) и русские алиасы слэш-команд включены по умолчанию (`true`) и могут быть индивидуально отключены в настройках (`layoutConversion: false`, `slashAliases: false`). Браузерный спелчек (`lang="ru-RU"`) активируется автоматически при выборе русской локали. --- ## 🛠 Разработка и зеркало репозитория Публичный репозиторий на GitHub является дистрибутивным зеркалом релизов `@goodandready/dsh-russian-lang`. Основная разработка, сборочный пайплайн и полный тестовый контур ведутся в основном Gitea-репозитории проекта. Pull Requests и Issues на GitHub приветствуются и обрабатываются в обычном порядке! Для внесения правок в логику клиента используйте `lib/client.template.js`. Запуск `npm test` в репозитории выполняет полную проверку (270+ модульных тестов Node.js, тесты сборщика, линтеры переводов и глоссария). --- ## 📄 Лицензия MIT © [GooDAnDReaDY](https://github.com/GooDAnDReaDY) ## Движок перевода реплик Плагин позволяет переводить ответы модели на русский язык. Для этого используется один из двух движков — по выбору пользователя в настройках. **По умолчанию оба движка выключены** (`translateEngine: off`). ### Google Translate (неофициальный) Текст ответов модели отправляется на `translate.googleapis.com/translate_a/single?client=gtx` — это **неофициальный** публичный эндпоинт Google без SLA и без гарантий доступности. В ответах модели могут содержаться фрагменты кода, пути, содержимое файлов — **всё это уходит третьей стороне**. При включении в карточке настроек отображается жёлтый бейдж. ### LibreTranslate (локальный) Плагин запускает Docker-контейнер `libretranslate/libretranslate:v1.5.3` на `127.0.0.1:5000`. Перевод выполняется полностью локально — текст **не покидает машину**. Для работы необходим установленный Docker. | Движок | Куда уходит текст | Приватность | Интернет | |---|---|---|---| | `off` (по умолчанию) | никуда | ✅ полная | не нужен | | `google` | Google (googleapis.com) | ⚠️ текст отправляется третьей стороне | нужен | | `libretranslate` | localhost:5000 (Docker) | ✅ локально | нужен только для загрузки образа | > [!NOTE] > **Ограничение системного меню Electron:** > Пункты системного меню десктопной оболочки Electron (Application, Edit, File, Quit, Undo/Redo/Cut/Copy/Paste и др.) принадлежат главному процессу Electron (`app.asar`) на уровне операционной системы и не подлежат переводу веб-плагинами DSH.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @goodandready/dsh-test-pilot

Bounded automatic test feedback after file changes, inside the same DSH turn

English • 中文说明 • Русский

⭐ If you like this plugin, please star it on GitHub — it shows me that the plugin is useful to you and motivates me to keep developing it.

🐛 If you find a bug or would like to request a feature, open a GitHub issue in any language — I will review your proposal and implement useful suggestions in a future plugin version.
--- ## Overview AI-assisted code changes need an executable signal before the agent claims completion. Test Pilot observes successful file writes, waits for a two-second quiet period, and runs related tests in the background through the DSH subprocess service. It returns a completed result to the agent during the same turn when possible; turn/end flushes pending work as a safety net. A read-only turn starts no test process. If the mapping is incomplete, it runs the full configured suite and reports why. The MVP is deliberately a verifier, not an autonomous repair agent. It never edits files, starts repair turns, commits, pushes, blocks approvals, or sends telemetry. ## Architecture ~~~mermaid graph LR A[Successful file-write tool result] --> B[Two-second quiet period] B --> C[Background related/full test run] C --> D[Attach completed result as additionalContexts] D --> E[Next tool call; turn/end flushes pending work] ~~~ ## Feature breakdown - Host lifecycle: observes successful write, edit and mutating str_replace_editor results in tools/post-execute. A two-second quiet period coalesces edits; turn/end flushes pending work as a safety net. - Change tracking: uses the current-turn `ctx.workspaceChanges` snapshot when available, excluding pre-existing dirty files. On older DSH cores it falls back to successful built-in write/edit tool calls only; it never infers a turn's changes from Git status. - Safe execution: tokenizes an executable plus arguments and rejects shell operators, command substitution and backticks. - Runner defaults: pytest, Jest, Vitest, Go, Rust/Cargo, TAP and TypeScript compiler commands are available. Pytest is the default. - Test selection: runs convention-matched tests for changed source files when the mapping is complete; otherwise runs the full suite with a reason. Manual `test_pilot_run` always runs the full configured command. - Parsers: built-in Node.js test runner summaries; normalized counts, duration, failure names/locations, exit status, timeout state and secret-shaped redaction. - Background lifecycle: later writes reset the debounce and cancel a stale run. The post-execute listener never waits for tests, observes exec.signal, and returns only an already-completed result in additionalContexts. - Automatic and manual runs are serialized per workspace, so concurrent requests cannot test the same mutable directory at the same time. - Lifecycle events publish queued/running/terminal snapshots with runId and timestamps; all existing lifecycle and report events remain available. - Agent feedback: the latest completed result is delivered to the agent once in additionalContexts, including green results. User-visible chat stays quiet on passes and no-tests; it reports an initial/new red failure composition and a red-to-green recovery once per workspace. Repeated red results with the same failed-test identities are silent. The plugin continues to emit test-pilot/report and dsh-test-pilot/report for every existing report event. - Tools: test_pilot_status returns the active-run count and latest result; optional limit includes up to 20 recent bounded summaries. test_pilot_run starts the configured full command in the current workspace or an optional cwd override. - Retention: terminal summaries are atomically stored under `$DSH_HOME/data/dsh-test-pilot/state.json`. Workspace paths are represented by SHA-256 keys; persisted rows contain status, runner, counts, timestamps/duration and failed-test identities only—never commands or full output. At most 50 workspaces and 50 history entries are retained for 30 days. Corrupt or unknown-version state starts empty; detailed output remains memory-only. ### Source modules | Module | Responsibility | | --- | --- | | lib/index.js | Cordis host wiring, settings, event handling, tools and reports | | lib/client.js | English/Chinese settings card and session-header status chip | | lib/status.js | Authenticated, session-bound status route and safe projection | | lib/command.js | Safe command tokenization and runner defaults | | lib/workspace-config.js | Workspace rules and bounded runner auto-detection | | lib/runner.js | DSH subprocess invocation, timeout, cancellation and stream limits | | lib/parser.js | Node.js built-in/Jest/Vitest/Go/Rust/TAP/tsc/Deno/npm parsing | | lib/result.js | Normalization, redaction and concise rendering | | lib/workspace.js | Session workspace and identity | | lib/turn-changes.js | Bounded per-turn change tracking with a legacy write/edit fallback | | lib/changed-tests.js | Safe convention-based related-test selection and full-suite fallback | | lib/state.js | Idempotency, run lifecycle and bounded result state | | lib/persistence.js | Versioned atomic workspace summaries and bounded retention | ## Installation The package is published on npmjs and does not require a private registry or additional credentials. Install it into the DSH web profile: ~~~bash dsh plugin --profile web add @goodandready/dsh-test-pilot ~~~ Open Settings → Plugins → Plugin settings and expand Test Pilot to edit automatic runs, runner defaults, workspace rules, run scope, timeout and output limits. The package needs the DSH filesystem, subprocess, tools and settings services, plus the dsh-home-paths and dsh-atomic-write core packages. ## Configuration Example settings: ~~~yaml enabled: true runScope: auto runner: auto command: "" workspaceRules: - path: /absolute/path/to/repo enabled: true runner: auto command: "" allowNetworkFetch: false cwd: "" timeoutMs: 120000 maxOutputBytes: 200000 ~~~ | Parameter | Type | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | enabled | boolean | true | Run after completed turns | | runScope | string | auto | auto selects related tests when safe and falls back to the full suite; full always runs the configured suite after a detected change | | runner | string | auto | auto, pytest, jest, vitest, go, rust/cargo, tap, tsc, deno or npm | | command | string | empty | Optional executable and arguments; shell syntax is rejected | | workspaceRules | array | [] | Per-workspace path, enablement, runner, optional command and package-fetch policy | | cwd | string | empty | Explicit workspace directory; empty uses the session workspace | | timeoutMs | number | 120000 | Maximum execution time in milliseconds | | maxOutputBytes | number | 200000 | Per-stream collection limit | Workspace rules use the longest matching path prefix. With `runner: auto`, Test Pilot checks `pytest.ini`, pytest configuration in `pyproject.toml`, a `package.json` test script, `go.mod`, `Cargo.toml`, and `deno.json` (or `deno.jsonc`). If no supported runner is found, automatic execution stays silent. Existing flat `runner` and `command` settings remain a rule for the current workspace root. Set `runner` explicitly for an otherwise unknown framework; `command` overrides the detected or default command. Built-in npm-based defaults run offline. A workspace rule may set `allowNetworkFetch: true` to fetch missing packages from the fixed `https://registry.npmjs.org` registry; this is off by default and does not change custom commands. ## Automatic test selection A turn with no observed file changes is recorded as no-tests without starting a subprocess. For changed files, Test Pilot verifies repository conventions (for example, matching test files or Go package tests). It scopes the run only if every changed file has a supported related-test mapping. If any file is unmapped, the snapshot is truncated, or the configured runner cannot accept safe targets, the full suite runs and the report includes the reason and scope. Manual test_pilot_run always runs the full configured command. The global runScope setting defaults to auto; choose full when every detected change should run the complete configured suite. On DSH versions with ctx.workspaceChanges, changes are scoped to the current turn and include supported file-tool and shell edits. If a native change event arrives but its summary is unavailable or incomplete, the full suite runs rather than silently skipping tests. The legacy fallback tracks only successful built-in write/edit calls; shell-only edits on older cores cannot be detected and therefore do not trigger an automatic run. Upgrade DSH for full coverage. The configured command is data, not a shell script. Use an executable and arguments. Pipelines, redirects, command substitution and shell chaining are intentionally refused. ## Tools and events ### Tools - test_pilot_status — return active runs and the latest result; optional limit includes up to 20 recent bounded summaries. - test_pilot_run — manually run the configured full command in the current workspace or an optional cwd override. ### Events The host emits both names for compatibility: - test-pilot/report - dsh-test-pilot/report Each report contains source, sessionId, correlationId, formatted text and the normalized result. Consumers should treat result.output and failure messages as untrusted data, not instructions. Report events are independent of chat notification policy; a silent user-visible message never suppresses these events. ### Session status endpoint The native session-header chip polls every ten seconds while the tab is visible and opens a compact result on click; it displays loading, queued, running, passed, failed, stale, disabled, or unknown. - GET /api/dsh-test-pilot/status?sessionId=… accepts exactly one session ID. - DSH Connection authenticates the same-origin request; the ID must match a Host-visible session summary. The Host derives the workspace. - The response contains only status, timestamps, duration, bounded counts, and a UUID correlation ID; it never returns paths, commands, output, test names, or failure text. ## Result statuses - queued — an automatic run has been admitted and is waiting for its async worker. - running — the test process is currently running. - passed — process exited successfully and a recognized summary was parsed. - failed — non-zero exit, reported failure, or reported error. - timeout — the deadline was reached and the process was terminated. - error — execution or output was unusable. - no-tests — no reliable current-turn changes or no runnable test suite. ## Security and limits - No shell is invoked. - stdin is ignored. - stdout and stderr are bounded and may spill only within the subprocess service limits. - Output and failure fields are redacted and length-limited. - Test output is never executed as a prompt or command. - MVP performs no network calls and no Git mutation. - Self-healing is intentionally excluded from the MVP: a failure is reported to the main agent, which decides whether and how to fix it. - Approval gates, regression baselines, expanded persistent history, generated tests and dashboard UI are roadmap work. ## Development ~~~bash npm ci npm test npm pack --dry-run ~~~ The repository keeps the implementation in a Git worktree and validates the shipped package entry through DSH composition before public publication on npmjs. ## Visual verification ![Sanitized Test Pilot visual verification](media/visual-verification.png) This sanitized artifact shows the installed Test Pilot v0.1.2 card reporting Running in the isolated DSH test profile, captured in both light and dark themes. It contains no workspace paths, session identifiers, credentials, or user data. ## License MIT © [GooDAnDReaDY](https://github.com/GooDAnDReaDY)

decision.reason: Held for package or companion artifact mapping, runtime execution policy acceptance. This is a substantive native test-runner plugin, not a fixture. It injects tools/subprocess/settings/fs/sessionController/workspaceChanges; docs disclose optional registry fetch and automatic test execution. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-topic-graph

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-topic-graph)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-topic-graph)
[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-topic-graph)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-topic-graph)
[![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph?style=social)](https://github.com/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph)
[![dsh-market](https://img.shields.io/badge/dsh--market-listed-4f6ef7)](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph/)

> 会话话题图谱 —— 把每个会话按轮次切开，让 AI 增量聚合成「话题 / 阶段」，一眼看清 token、工具与时间花在哪。界面支持中英双语切换。

**中文** | [English](README.en.md)

`dsh-topic-graph` 是 [dsh](https://github.com/deepseek-ai)（DeepSeek Harness）的 Web UI 插件。它监听 dsh 的会话事件流，把每个会话按**轮次（turn）**切分，再调用 DeepSeek 把轮次**增量**聚合成**话题（topic）**、把话题聚合成**阶段（stage）**，并为阶段、话题生成名字。会话里启动的**子智能体会话**也会被切分，并以分支形式直接画进同一张图。

插件在 Web UI 里以「**话题**」视图的形式停在「对话 / 轨迹」之后，包含两个视图：

- **话题 · 工作流**：左侧阶段 → 话题树，右侧是选中阶段的详情（总览统计、可展开的话题卡片、轮次明细与单轮 AI 分析）；
- **话题 · 图谱**：两种视图——「**时间线**」（X 轴轮次、Y 轴阶段，话题按时间排成彩色横线，关系用曲线连接）和「**结构图**」（阶段 → 话题树 + 右侧关系轨道），支持 Ctrl+滚轮缩放、悬停查看详情。

顶部固定显示会话统计（Token / 步骤耗时 / 工具 / 轮次 / 话题 / 阶段 / 关联 / AI 切分消耗），并可选择切分模型、手动触发切分。

插件在 dsh 的**设置**里新增一页「**Topic Graph**」：可以**启用 / 停用后端服务**（关闭后停止自动切分与 AI 分析，已有数据仍可查看），以及切换插件**界面语言（中文 / English）**。界面文案完整中英双语，AI 生成的话题 / 阶段名称与单轮分析也会跟随语言设置（切换后点「全部重切」即可让已有内容也换成新语言）。

## 界面预览

### 工作流：阶段概览与阶段内话题关系

![工作流：阶段概览](assets/screenshot-workflow.png)

*左侧阶段树（可折叠、显示 Token / 时间占比）；右侧是选中阶段的统计（Token / 总耗时 / 工具调用占比横条）、**阶段内话题关系**小图（X=轮次、圆点=话题、虚线=关系），以及可展开的话题卡片。*

### 工作流：话题与轮次

![工作流：话题与轮次](assets/screenshot-workflow-topic.png)

*话题卡片展开后是一轮一轮的明细：轮次号、用户输入摘要、总步数 / Token / 工具调用 / 耗时。*

### 工作流：轮次内详情

![工作流：轮次内详情](assets/screenshot-workflow-turn.png)

*展开某一轮：token（输入 / 输出 / 缓存读 / 缓存写）、步骤活动时间、工具调用数、总步数、模型；下方是用户输入 / AI 回复，可一键「跳转到对话」。*

### 工作流：单轮 AI 分析

![工作流：单轮 AI 分析](assets/screenshot-workflow-ai.png)

*按需把该轮的模型 / 工具轨迹写成面向人的分步说明（每一步标注覆盖步数），结果持久化缓存，可重新分析。*

### 图谱：时间线

![图谱：时间线](assets/screenshot-timeline.png)

*X 轴是轮次（时间）、Y 轴是阶段泳道，话题按轮次跨度排成彩色横线；话题之间的语义关系用淡虚线曲线连接（默认淡显，悬停 / 点击高亮），左侧大纲与右侧联动。*

### 图谱：结构图

![图谱：结构图](assets/screenshot-structure.png)

*阶段 → 话题的树状结构，右侧轨道画话题之间的关系曲线；阶段可折叠，悬停查看详情、点击打开话题详情。*

---

## 为什么做它

长会话最难回答的问题是「这件事到底做到哪了、时间花在哪了、当时那段结论在哪儿」。聊天记录是线性的，工作线索却是网状的。这个插件把线性会话折叠成一张可跳转的「工作地图」：

- 按轮次统计 **token（输入/输出/缓存读/缓存写）、工具调用、Agent 耗时**；
- 用 AI 把轮次聚成话题、把话题聚成阶段，并识别话题之间「依赖 / 延续 / 对比 / 修复 / 验证 / 回访」的关系；
- 子智能体不再藏在另一个会话里，而是作为分支挂在父话题下，token/耗时一起可比较；
- 点任意话题可以打开详情，并一键跳回该话题的首轮对话。

## 特性

### 切分与统计

- **按轮次切分**：以 `turn/start` ~ `turn/end` 为一轮，统计每轮的用户输入、AI 回复、token 用量、工具调用次数/分布/错误数、轮次耗时（各轮时间之和，而非首末轮次差）、步骤活动时间。
- **AI 话题 / 阶段**：DeepSeek 把连续轮次聚合成一条工作线（话题），把相邻话题聚合成阶段，并命名、写摘要。
- **子话题不超过 3 层**：AI 判断是否需要子话题（例如大任务下的子模块、某个错误的专项排查）；层级上限 3（根话题算第 1 层），超出的由 Host 压平。
- **增量切分**：新轮次到达后，只把「尚未切分的新轮次摘要 + 已有话题/阶段结构」发给模型；历史轮次正文不会重复输入。长会话首次导入也按批增量切分，边切边显示。
- **长会话 / 400 容错**：默认 6 轮/请求；请求失败自动把当前批**减半重试**（6→3→1），并记住可用批次大小；400 类错误自动换适配器默认推理档位重试；输出上限按话题规模动态放大，结构 JSON 被截断时自动用更大上限重试并识别截断、避免把半截结构当成完整结果；连续失败快速降级为本地兜底，不会无限重试烧钱。
- **占比统计**：每个话题 / 阶段 / 轮次都给出 token 占比、工具调用占比、Agent 耗时占比；面板顶部还有全局统计条（总轮次、总话题、阶段数、Token 总数、工具总量、步骤总耗时、总耗时、关联数、子智能体 Token）。

### 图谱与关系

- **有类型的边**：
  - `next` —— 相邻根话题的时间顺序链；
  - `belongTo` —— 话题归属阶段 / 子话题归属父话题 / 子智能体话题归属分支；
  - `has_relation` —— AI 判断的语义关系（依赖 / 延续 / 对比 / 修复 / 验证 / 回访…），带关系名；
  - `delegates` —— 父话题 → 子智能体分支的委托边。
- **按标题判断话题关系**：结构切分后，单独用「话题标题」做一次轻量关系分析（成本很低），专门识别 **「先说 A，再说 B，又回到 A」** 的回访模式；可通过 `relationMode` 关闭或改为跟随切分输出。
- **子智能体与主智能体同屏**：子智能体会话自动切分，并在图谱中以「分支框 + 内部话题树」显示；点分支头可进入子会话单独查看，点子话题节点可打开子话题详情。多层委托（子智能体的子智能体）同样支持。

### 交互

- **跟随左侧会话**：读取 shell 持久化的当前会话选择（`dsh.sessions.current`），左侧工作区/会话切换时图谱自动跟随；也可在面板下拉框里固定查看某个会话，固定子会话时不受左侧切换影响。
- **话题详情**：链式话题的 ⓘ 或图谱节点点击 → 打开详情浮层（token 明细、工具分布、耗时、关联/父子/子话题/子智能体分支）。
- **跳回首轮**：详情底部「在对话中打开首轮」→ 切到对应会话并尝试滚动定位到该话题第一轮（历史未完全加载时退化为仅打开会话）。
- **图谱操作**：Ctrl+滚轮以光标为锚点缩放、普通滚轮上下滚动、悬停 tooltip 显示完整信息；阶段 / 话题 / 子智能体分支左侧的 ▾/▸ 箭头可折叠内容，点击节点其它区域打开详情。
- **悬浮窗**：默认宽约 900px，可拖右下角继续放大到接近窗口宽度；收起成小球后仍可拖动位置，轻点展开。
- **主题与文案**：只使用 `--dsw-alias-*` 主题 token（跟随明暗主题）；界面文案注册进 dsh locale 服务（中文 / English）。

### 工程

- **零构建**：Client 半是纯 React + `h()`，由 dsh 运行时提供 React，改完刷新页面即生效；Host 半改动需重启 dsh。
- **日志是唯一事实来源**：轮次统计每次从 dsh 会话日志（`ctx.sessionQuery.readSession`）重放，实时会话通过 `session/event` 增量折叠并按 `seq` 去重；AI 只负责结构划分。
- **持久化轻量**：只持久化话题/阶段/关系结构与「已切分到第几轮」，落在 `<DSH_HOME>/data/topic-graph/<sessionId>.json`（原子写、防抖）；重启后恢复并继续增量切分。

## 安装

要求：dsh（Web profile）已能正常运行。

### 方式一（推荐）：从 dsh-market / 插件市场安装

在 dsh 的**插件市场**里搜索 `dsh-topic-graph`，点「安装」即可。插件详情页：
👉 [awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph/)

### 方式二：用 dsh CLI 从 npm 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-topic-graph
```

更新到最新版：

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-topic-graph@latest
```

### 方式三：从 GitHub 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:hagen666/dsh-topic-graph
```

### 方式四：本地开发

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hagen666/dsh-topic-graph.git
cd dsh-topic-graph
dsh plugin --profile web add file:/absolute/path/to/dsh-topic-graph
```

安装后**重启 dsh**（在运行 `dsh web` 的终端 Ctrl-C 后重新执行），刷新浏览器页面。

> 说明：本插件通过 `dsh.bundle.patch` 注册 Host 行、通过 `dsh.client` 声明 Web 启用，不需要额外构建步骤；`lib/client.js` 即浏览器 bundle。npm 包为预构建产物，安装时不会触发 `allowBuilds` 构建授权。

## 配置

配置写在 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 `config` 中（安装后也可以在你的 profile patch 层覆盖）：

| 键 | 说明 | 默认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `segmentMode` | 切分方式：`auto`（AI 优先，失败回退规则）/ `llm`（强制 AI）/ `rule`（仅规则，零成本） | `auto` |
| `provider` / `model` | 切分用的模型路由；留空则自动探测 dsh 当前配置 | `deepseek-official` / `deepseek-flash` |
| `batchTurns` | 每次请求模型的轮次数（请求失败会自动再减半） | `6` |
| `maxInputChars` | 单次请求新轮次摘要的字符上限 | `8000` |
| `debounceMs` | 轮次结束后触发切分的防抖时间（毫秒） | `2500` |
| `minGapMs` | 同一会话两次 AI 切分的最小间隔（毫秒，控成本） | `8000` |
| `autoSegment` | 新轮次到达后是否自动增量切分 | `true` |
| `showSubagents` | 会话列表是否显示子代理会话（分支始终会纳入图谱） | `false` |
| `includeSubagents` | 是否把子智能体会话纳入切分与分支展示 | `true` |
| `maxSubagentDepth` | 子智能体分支最大递归层级（1~5） | `2` |
| `maxBranches` | 单次返回的最大分支数（1~60） | `20` |
| `relationMode` | 话题关系判断：`titles`（仅标题，默认）/ `inline`（跟随切分输出）/ `off` | `titles` |
| `reasoningEffort` | 切分调用推理档位 `off/low/high/max`；400 时会自动换默认档位重试 | `off` |
| `ruleTurnsPerTopic` | 规则模式每个话题的轮次数 | `3` |
| `ruleTopicsPerStage` | 规则模式每个阶段的话题数 | `5` |

## 使用

- **链式 Tab**：阶段卡片 → 话题卡片（可展开轮次明细）；点轮次行可看 token 明细、工具分布、模型、输入/回复预览；话题下显示关联话题 chips 和子智能体分组。
- **图谱 Tab**：阶段分组框 + 话题/子话题树 + 右侧子智能体分支；Ctrl+滚轮缩放，普通滚轮滚动，悬停看完整信息，点击话题看详情。
- **话题详情**：token 明细/占比、工具分布、步骤耗时、关联/父子/子话题/子智能体分支；底部可「在对话中打开首轮」。
- **子智能体**：分支框头部点击进入子会话；子话题节点点击看详情；详情里可返回父会话。
- **会话选择**：默认跟随左侧当前会话；下拉框可固定某个会话，选「跟随左侧当前会话」恢复跟随。

## 工作原理

```
session/event ─┐
               ├─► 轮次折叠（turns）─► 增量 AI 切分 ─► topics / stages / relations
readSession  ──┘                                  └─► 子智能体分支（branches）
                                                        │
                                     webServer REST ────┴──► /plugins/topic-graph/*
                                                        │
                                          shell.overlay 悬浮窗（链式 / 图谱）
```

- **Host 半**（`lib/index.js`）：会话事件折叠、轮次统计、AI 增量切分（提示词 / 校验 / 回退 / 自适应分批）、关系边与子智能体分支、持久化、HTTP 路由。
- **Client 半**（`lib/client.js`）：注册 `conversation.view` 停靠视图（「话题」），轮询 Host 数据并渲染「话题·工作流」与「话题·图谱」（时间线 / 结构图）、详情浮层与跳转。
- AI 输出会被 Host 校验：轮次必须恰好覆盖一次、父子关系必须存在且不成环、子话题深度 ≤3、阶段归属完整；不合法的部分会被修正或回退，模型输出带截断也能容错修复 JSON。

### HTTP 接口

| 路由 | 说明 |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /plugins/topic-graph/ping` | 健康检查（返回插件版本） |
| `GET /plugins/topic-graph/sessions` | 会话列表（标题、最近活跃时间、是否有切分） |
| `GET /plugins/topic-graph/graph?sessionId=&version=` | 某会话的完整图谱数据（轮次统计 + 话题 + 阶段 + 关系边 + 子智能体分支 + AI 状态）；`version` 未变时返回 `{unchanged:true}` |
| `POST /plugins/topic-graph/segment` | 手动触发切分 `{sessionId, full}`；`full:true` 为全部重切 |

### 数据与持久化

- 轮次统计不落盘：每次从 dsh 会话日志重放，日志是唯一事实来源。
- 切分结构落盘：`<DSH_HOME>/data/topic-graph/<sessionId>.json`，只保存话题/阶段/关系结构与「已切分到第几轮」；重启后恢复并继续增量。
- 新轮次到达（`turn/end`）时后台防抖触发增量切分，即使悬浮窗收起也会继续。

## 已知限制

- 会话日志里没有 `turn/end` 的异常中断轮次会被视为「进行中」，等 dsh 日志修复补齐后才参与切分。
- 「在对话中打开首轮」的滚动定位依赖聊天区 `data-chat-turn` DOM 标记，属于尽力而为：历史未完全加载时只会打开会话，不保证精确落位。
- 跟随左侧会话读取的是 shell 的本地持久化键 `dsh.sessions.current`；如果未来 dsh 改动该实现，会自动退回 Host 的「最近活跃会话」。
- 子智能体的「挂靠话题」按启动时间落在父会话哪一轮来推断（AI 不重复读子会话正文），必要时可「全部重切」重新生成。
- 子智能体会话也会独立调用模型切分；会话/子代理很多时可通过 `includeSubagents`、`maxBranches`、`minGapMs` 控制成本。
- 极长会话的图谱数据较大（数百轮约数百 KB），前端按 `version` 跳过未变化的轮询；数据全部走本机回环。

## 开发

```bash
# 修改 lib/client.js 后：刷新浏览器页面即可（无需构建）
# 修改 lib/index.js（Host 半）后：重启 dsh 生效
```

目录：

```
lib/index.js      Host 半：事件折叠、轮次统计、AI 切分、关系/分支、持久化、REST
lib/client.js     Client 半：conversation.view 停靠视图（话题·工作流 / 话题·图谱）
cordis.patch.yml  dsh bundle 注册行与默认配置
locale/           插件显示名与说明（中 / 英）
assets/           README 截图
icon.svg          插件图标
```

## 版本记录

src/client/index.ts 里 __ModuleLoader__.load({ id }) 的 id 必须与 name 逐字一致
files —— npm publish 只发这些内容；assets/webm 是 VP9-alpha 播放素材（体积大，但不发就播不了）
