# dsh-pet-mind 🐾 桌宠 + 心智层（0.5.0）

> **非官方插件**：与 DeepSeek、DeepSeek Harness 官方无隶属关系；"DeepSeek" 等名称归其权利人所有。 > > **来源链**：`PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet` v0.3.8（MIT）→ `TuWeiZhi/dsh-pet` 0.4.4（MIT）→ 本仓库（MIT）。 > 代码许可见 [LICENSE](LICENSE)，改动与来源见 [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md)， > 素材与第三方组件见 [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)。 > > **一句话**：一只住在 DeepSeek Harness 里的桌宠，外加一层"知道你上下文还剩多少、记得你们做过什么、 > 能在你停留时给一句基于屏幕文字的建议"的心智层——**不录屏、不执行操作、不替你做事**。 --- ## 这个项目做了什么（相对上游） 上游 `dsh-pet` 是一个纯桌宠：动画、拖拽、桌面透明窗、余额、聊天。本仓库在它之上做了两类改动： ### 1）工程：恢复真正的构建链 原 fork 发布的是**构建产物快照**（`lib/*.js` 被直接改过，没有构建链，改 `src/` 不生效）。 本仓库把原 fork 的 9 个产物级补丁**回植到 TypeScript 源码**，并恢复 `tsdown` 构建： - `npm run build`：`src/client` / `src/host` / `src/standalone` → `lib/*.js`，`src/shared` → 桌面 `shared-core.js`； - `npm test`：`node:test` + 原生类型擦除，1000+ 单测； - `npm run typecheck` / ESLint / CI / 发版自检（`tools/verify-package.mjs`）。 ### 2）心智层（mind，0.5 新增） | 能力 | 它做什么 | 边界 | |---|---|---| | **上下文用量** | 从 DSH 的 `session/event` 读 `usage` 与 `contextWindow`（缺失时用 `llm.resolveModel`/配置补）；**右肩外侧环**：数据更新自动亮 10 秒 + 悬停常显 | 只覆盖 DSH 会话；窗口未知时不画；重启先显示上一轮快照（灰度） | | **工作记忆** | 到阈值把最近对话抽成 Markdown（本地抽取，零 token），写进 `memory/work/` | 抽取式，不是"完全理解"；可能漏要点 | | **陪伴记忆** | 只记称呼/偏好/约定，写进 `memory/companion/` | 启发式触发，可能误记/漏记 | | **记忆注入** | 把 `INDEX.md` 注入系统提示词，新会话/子支线能续上 | 有长度上限；会占用一点上下文 | | **专注建议** | 进入新页面 30 秒 → 本地 OCR → 文字交给**你的文本模型** → 一句话建议 | 每页只一次、每天 6 条、失败重试一次；**只建议，不操作** | | **待机** | 人不在（空闲 ≥5 分钟且屏幕未变化）→ 只播待机、碎碎念静音 | Windows 专用；误判可能发生 | | **隐私闸门** | 微信/支付宝/网银/密码管理器/远程桌面 + 标题兜底 + 识别不出即拒绝 | 不是万无一失，见 [PRIVACY](docs/PRIVACY.md) | ### 这个版本做了什么 - 把上游的产物级改动回植到 TypeScript，恢复 `npm run build` / `npm test` / CI 与发版自检； - 新增心智层：上下文环（右肩外侧，数据变化自动亮 10 秒/悬停常显，重启先显示上一轮快照）、 双轨本地记忆、OCR 专注建议（30 秒/每页一次/每天 6 条/失败重试一次/120 字）、待机、隐私闸门； - 发布材料：README、PRIVACY、LIMITATIONS、LEGAL、TESTING、SECURITY、CONTRIBUTING 与素材声明； - 当前版本实测记录见 [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md)（1054 tests / 1053 pass）。 ## 做不到什么（先看这里） - **不能真正"读懂"你在干什么。** OCR 只把屏幕上的**文字**读出来；它不理解图片、图表、视频、 软件界面结构，也不知道你的意图。建议来自"这段文字 + 应用名"，模型可能理解偏、甚至编造。 - **不能"看着你"做出判断。** 默认是 OCR 模式：只在停留到期时截**一帧**（内存）， 立即转文字后丢弃；没有持续画面、没有视觉理解。可设 `vision.enabled=false` 完全关掉。 - **不能执行任何操作。** 不点鼠标、不敲键盘、不调工具、不改文件；提示词里明确要求"只做建议"。 - **不能识别密码框。** 外部程序无法可靠判断别的应用里是否在输入密码；只能靠应用名单 + 窗口标题 + 手动暂停（"隐私暂停"）。提权窗口读不到标题 → 直接不采。 - **不是监控软件。** 不做录屏、不留副本、不做人脸/身份识别、不上传画面；不适合用于员工监控、 取证或任何需要留证的场景。 - **记忆不等于理解。** 摘要是抽取式的，可能丢掉关键结论；注入的记忆也可能与新情况冲突。 - **平台限制**：桌面感知与 OCR 仅 Windows；多屏只截光标所在那块屏；OCR 依赖系统语言包， 排版复杂/字体过小/深色背景下可能读不出字。 完整清单见 [docs/LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md)。 ## 已知问题（不粉饰） - **重启后要等一轮回复才有实时数字**：计量只吃实时事件，不回放历史；会先显示上一轮快照（灰度）顶一下； - **环不是所有时候都在**：默认"数据变化亮 10 秒 + 悬停常显"，避免一直挡视线；想让常驻可以提 issue； - **建议可能不来**：没字/敏感应用/夜间免打扰/当天 6 条用完，都会静默； - **OCR 质量依赖系统**：远程桌面、深色主题、小字号、游戏/视频可能读不出； - **模型可能编**：建议只是一句话参考，不要当结论。 ## 运行要求 | 项 | 要求 | |---|---| | 宿主 | DeepSeek Harness（桌面 Electron 版或 `dsh web`）；插件用到的宿主服务：`webServer`、`agentDefaultModel`、`credentials`、`llm`、`commands`、`connection` | | 系统 | 桌面感知/OCR **仅 Windows 10/11**；其他平台桌宠可用，心智层的感知部分自动降级 | | OCR | Windows 自带 OCR 需安装**中文语言包**（设置 → 时间和语言 → 语言 → 中文 → 可选功能） | | 模型 | 需要 DSH 里已配置可用的对话模型；建议使用你在用的文本模型（`suggestion.model` 留空 = 跟随对话模型） | | 权限 | 不需要管理员权限；提权窗口读不到标题，会直接不采集 | | 构建 | Node ≥ 22.12（仅从源码构建时需要；装 tgz 不需要） | ## 安装 **没有发布到 npm**。用本地 tgz（[Releases](../../releases) 或 `npm pack` 产物）： **直接安装：** 1）安装前要先卸载之前版本，重新启动dsh软件。 2）直接安装，在dsh软件直接用本地 tgz 安装,在插件页面输入"路径\dsh-pet-mind-0.5.0.tgz"点击安装。

```bat :: 1) 旧插件与本插件共用 entry id dsh-pet，先卸旧的 "...\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop remove @tuweizhi/dsh-pet :: 2) 装本包 "...\dsh.cmd" plugin --profile desktop add "路径\dsh-pet-mind-0.5.0.tgz" :: 3) 完全退出 DSH 再启动（不要在运行中热装后指望立即生效） ``` `dsh web` 用户把 `--profile desktop` 换成 `--profile web`，然后重启 `dsh web`。 详细步骤、配置片段、排查与回滚见 [docs/INSTALL-LOCAL.md](docs/INSTALL-LOCAL.md)。 **独立模式**（不打开 DSH，仅桌宠）： ```sh npm install && npm run build node lib/standalone.js --check node lib/standalone.js ``` ## 开箱默认（不需要手写配置） 装好即用，心智层默认已开启：本地 OCR 建议（画面不出本机）、进入新页面 30 秒后建议一次、 每天最多 6 条、失败重试一次、23:00–08:00 免打扰、文案上限 120 字、上下文窗口自动识别。 **不要往 `main-config.jsonc` 里贴任何 `mind` 配置**；只有想改节奏/关掉采集时才需要动 [`assets/config.jsonc`](assets/config.jsonc) 里的带注释字段（高级用法）。 ## 隐私与数据流（摘要） | 数据 | 在哪 | 是否离开本机 | |---|---|---| | 屏幕帧（默认开启，仅停留到期截一帧） | Helper 内存 → 本地 OCR → 丢弃 | **不离开**（`mode:"ocr"`） | | OCR 文字 + 前台应用名 | 内存 → 交给**你配置的**文本模型 | **会**，只发给你选的服务商 | | 窗口标题 | 内存，仅用于隐私判定 | 不落盘、不发网络 | | 记忆 `memory/*.md` | `$DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/memory/` | 不离开，除非你把它提交/同步 | | 配置 | `main-config.jsonc` | 不离开 | 控制手段：`mind.enabled=false` 整层关闭；`vision.enabled=false` 完全不碰像素； 设置页「隐私暂停」或 `mind.privacy.paused=true` 立即停采；删除 `memory/` 即清空记忆。 完整说明（含法律依据与保留期）见 [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md)。 ## 法律与合规（要点） - **代码**：MIT。允许修改、发布、商用，但必须保留版权与许可声明、注明改动、不得用原作者名义背书。 - **素材**：`assets/webm`、`assets/memes`、`assets/fonts`、`assets/logo.png` 来自上游，**不因代码 MIT 而自动可商用**。 表情包多为网络梗图、字体有独立授权——**公开分发前请自行确认或替换**。 - **名称**：本项目是非官方 fork，未使用 DeepSeek 官方标识暗示背书；"DeepSeek Harness" 名称归其权利人。 - **个人信息**：OCR 文字属于可能含个人信息的屏幕内容。请仅在**你有权处理的设备与内容**上使用； 在工作场所或他人设备上使用，需遵守当地劳动法/个人信息保护法（如中国《个人信息保护法》的告知同意、 最小必要原则），并取得相关人员同意。**本项目不构成法律意见。** - **模型服务**：文字会发给你配置的模型服务商，适用其服务条款与数据政策；请勿把涉密/受限材料送入云端模型。 完整说明见 [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md)。 ## 文档 - [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)：目录、构建、**与 DSH 的连接点**、IntelliJ 打开与调试、扩展指南 - [docs/MIND.md](docs/MIND.md)：心智层设计、OCR 链路、策略与隐私 - [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md)：0.5.0 实测记录（上下文/记忆/OCR/待机/隐私）与未覆盖项 - [docs/PRIVACY.md](docs/PRIVACY.md)：数据清单、出网边界、保留期、法律依据、用户控制 - [docs/LIMITATIONS.md](docs/LIMITATIONS.md)：做不到什么（能力边界） - [docs/LEGAL.md](docs/LEGAL.md)：许可、素材、商标、个人信息与免责 - [docs/INSTALL-LOCAL.md](docs/INSTALL-LOCAL.md)：本地安装、配置、排查、回滚 - [docs/PUBLISH.md](docs/PUBLISH.md)：改名、GitHub/Gitee、npm、发布前 checklist - [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)：逐版本改动 ## 开发 ```sh npm install npm run typecheck npm test npm run build node tools/verify-package.mjs ``` 贡献方式见 [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)，安全问题见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。 ## 来源与致谢 - 上游：`PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet`（桌宠本体、动画流水线、桌面 Electron 外壳） - 增强 fork：`TuWeiZhi/dsh-pet`（碎碎念本地化、气泡可收起、夹框、边距等） - 灵感：`dsh-vision-router`（"把画面转成文本再交给纯文本模型"的思路；本仓库**未**把它作为依赖打包） ## 许可 [MIT](LICENSE)。素材版权独立于代码，详见 [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)。

# 记忆星图 · memory-nebula

[![CI](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-memory-nebula.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-memory-nebula)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/npm/l/dsh-memory-nebula.svg)](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/blob/main/LICENSE)

[English](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/blob/main/README.en.md) · [在线示例](https://hanhan9999999999999999999.github.io/dsh-memory-nebula/demo.html?lang=en) · [官网](https://hanhan9999999999999999999.github.io/dsh-memory-nebula/) · 在 DSH 里把散落在各个工作区、各个记忆插件里的记忆抽出来，算成一张**带证据的关联星云**，再从这张图上做「神经元式」的连带检索——以及，让别的插件注入了什么，星图就顺着连接补上它没注的那一半。

![记忆星图：三种视图、左栏筛选、证据链与详情](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/preview.png)

第一次打开、库里还没有记忆时，页面不会留一块空白——它给三条接入路径，也可以先进示例星系看看：

![空态：三条接入路径](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/empty.jpg)

![示例星系：64 条虚构记忆，只读，不碰真实库](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/demo.jpg)

![英文界面：顶栏、左栏、看板与详情一起切换](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/i18n-en.jpg)

![首访三步：搜一个词、看一条证据、走一条链](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/onboard.jpg)

看完之后，可以把整张星图（含正文）导出成一个自包含 HTML，双击离线打开，搜索和证据链都还能用：

![单文件快照：离线只读](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/main/docs/assets/snapshot.jpg)

- 左侧栏一个图标 → 打开就是整片星云（Deep Space 风格，可缩放、可筛选、可搜索）。
- 不改任何别的插件的记忆库：所有记忆库都以 `readOnly` 打开，只写自己的目录 `$DSH_HOME/memory-nebula/`。
- 星图不只是一张画：宿主侧注册了 **9 个工具** + 一段每轮注入的提示，让会话里的 AI 在检索记忆时能**顺着连接把别的项目里的那一半一起读出来**。
- 记忆从哪来是**可插拔**的：meow-memory 的 SQLite、任意笔记目录、任意 SQLite 表、远端服务推来的 JSONL，都走同一套适配器契约。

```
   ┌─────────────── 记忆来源（全部只读）───────────────┐
   │ meow-memory  <ws>/.dsh-meow/memory.db + sessions/ │
   │ notes        任意 .md/.jsonl/.txt 目录（frontmatter）│
   │ sqlite       任意库，列名自动猜，写操作直接拒       │
   │ ingest       $DSH_HOME/memory-nebula/ingest/*.jsonl│
   └───────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                           │ adapters/index.js 发现 + 扫描
                           ▼
  text.js 分词/实体 ──▶ graph.js 建图（6 类边 + 打分 + 剪枝）
                           │
                   nebula.js 门面（索引 / 缓存 / 巡检）
                           │
        ┌──────────────────┼────────────────────┬──────────────┐
        ▼                  ▼                    ▼              ▼
   http.js 页面      index.js 9 个工具    systemPrompt     bridge.js 补充包
   （iframe）         nebula_*            每轮邻域注入      ledger.js 注入账本
```

## 能做什么

| 能力 | 入口 |
| --- | --- |
| 看整片星云 / 星系 / 时间螺旋 | 左侧栏图标；`1` `2` `3` 切换三档 |
| 顺着连接检索（跨工作区） | `nebula_recall`、搜索框 `/` |
| 查一条记忆的全文、出处、同会话邻居、谁提到过它 | 点任意节点 |
| 证据链：两条记忆到底怎么连上的 | 选中后 `Shift` 点另一条 |
| **跨插件补充包**：别的插件注入了什么，就补它强相关却没读的邻居 | `nebula_bridge`、每轮注入（可配预算） |
| **接入新的记忆库**：SQLite / 笔记目录 / JSONL 推送 | `nebula_sources`、`sources.json` |
| **远端记忆服务推进来**（hindsight / openviking 之类） | `nebula_ingest`、`POST /ingest` |
| 导出整张图：给人看的 MD 报告 / 给 AI 看的 JSON | `GET /export?format=md\|json`、顶栏「导出」 |
| 纠错：把算错的关联按掉 | 详情里邻居右侧 `×`，或 `nebula_link(action="mute")` |
| 记忆体检（六类失效模式） | 左侧「记忆体检」、看板 `B`、`nebula_hygiene` |
| 导出当前视图 PNG / 可见子图 JSON | 顶栏「导出」 |
| **第一次打开**：空库给三条接入路径，或直接进示例星系 | 空态卡片「看示例」、`?demo=1` |
| **单文件快照**：整张星图（含正文）打包成一个 HTML，离线可看 | 顶栏「导出 → 整张星图 · 单文件 HTML」、`GET /share` |
| **范围分享**：只导出一个工作区 / 一个项目 / 选中节点 2 跳 | 导出菜单另两项、`GET /share?scope=ws:<工作区>` |
| **命令行快照**：CI / 定时归档不启端口，直接写 HTML | `node lib/standalone.mjs --share <file> [--scope …]` |
| **隐私过滤**：导出前整区隐去日记 / 按层级 / 项目 / 状态排除 | 导出菜单「隐去日记」、`GET /share?hide=ws:日记` |
| **中英双语**：界面与离线快照都可切英文，未翻译处回退中文 | 顶栏语言按钮、`?lang=en` |
| **一键诊断**：复制版本/环境/图规模/最近错误，不含正文与路径 | `?` →「复制诊断」、`GET /diagnostics`、`--diagnose` |
| **首访引导**：搜一个词 → 看一条证据 → 走一条链，三步可跳过 | 首次打开自动出现，`?` 里可重看 |
| **两万条级打开**：20,000 条 / 156,993 条连接，建图 2.53s、快照首屏 762ms | 无需切换；大图自动跳过生长动画，基准见 `docs/benchmarks.md` |
| 时间回放（只看某天及之前） | 时间视图底部时间轴 |
| **纯键盘 / 读屏**：方向键在星星之间按方向走、`[` `]` 沿连接走、`+` `-` 缩放、`Home` 跳枢纽 | 点一下画面（或 Tab 进星图）就能用；`?` 看全表 |
| 快捷键一览 | `?` 或顶栏「?」 |

## 快速开始

已经装好的机器上（`profiles/desktop`），只要打开「记忆星图」页面就有一张图；页面每 12 秒比一次 `sig`，别的会话写了新记忆会自动长出新星点。库里还没有记忆时，页面会给三条接入路径，也可以先点「看示例」；`…/memory-nebula/?demo=1` 可直达示例星系，逛完退出不会动真实库。

精选目录已收录（推荐）：[awesome-dsh-plugin 目录页](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/p/hanhan9999999999999999999/dsh-memory-nebula/)。

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-memory-nebula
```

也可以在 DSH 的「插件 → 发现」里添加索引
`https://unpkg.com/dsh-memory-nebula@1.7.0/market/index.json`，搜索「记忆星图」安装。
装完按下面的 2.5 跑一次 doctor。

想先看看，不装进 DSH：

```powershell
npx -y -p dsh-memory-nebula memory-nebula --demo
```

打开它打印的 `http://127.0.0.1:7891/api/memory-nebula/?demo=1`，看到的是内置示例库，不读也不写你的真实记忆。

也可以从仓库装到 DSH：

```powershell
# 1) 装进 profile（二选一）
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "<profile>\node_modules\dsh-memory-nebula" -Target "<plugin>"
npm install <path>\dsh-memory-nebula-1.7.0.tgz --prefix <profile>

# 2) profile 的 package.json 里加依赖与 bundles（只加 dependencies 不会重组）
#    dependencies:         "dsh-memory-nebula": "file:../../plugins/dsh-memory-nebula"
#    dsh.profile.bundles:  "dsh-memory-nebula"

# 2.5) 装完先体检：只读检查 Node/依赖/bundles/文件，fail 才退出 1
node "<profile>\node_modules\dsh-memory-nebula\scripts\doctor.mjs" --profile "<profile>"

# 3) 重启 DSH，打开侧栏「记忆星图」
```

不想重启 DSH，或宿主里跑的还是旧模块：

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File sidecar.ps1 start   # Windows，默认 7890，自动找 node
node lib/standalone.mjs --port 7890                          # 其它系统，默认扫当前目录
```

`sidecar.ps1` 还接受 `-Port`、`-Root <额外扫描目录>`、`-Node <node.exe>`；`status` / `stop` 只作用于指定端口。

不启动端口，直接从命令行写一份快照：

```powershell
node lib/standalone.mjs --demo --share .\snapshot.html
node lib/standalone.mjs --share .\work.html --scope ws:星港产品 --hide level:lesson

# 报告也能带走：md 或 json，范围语义与快照一致
node lib/standalone.mjs --export .
ebula.json --scope project:memory-nebula
node lib/standalone.mjs --export .
ebula.md --format md
```

`--share` / `--export` 都只建一次图就退出：`--scope` 支持 `all` / `ws:<工作区>` /
`project:<项目>` / `focus:<节点 id>`，`--hops` 控制 focus 的跳数（1–5，默认 2），
`--hide` 可逗号分隔多条规则（仅 `--share`）。

页面会并行探宿主与独立引擎的 `/ping`，自动选 `build` 较新的那条；宿主缺接口时顶部有横幅说明。

自检三条命令：

```bash
npm test        # 126 项单元测试
npm run verify  # 单测 + 发布静态检查（npm pack 的 prepack 会自动再跑）
node scripts/smoke.mjs   # 63 项接口契约（对运行中的实例）
```

### 接入一个新的记忆库（三步）

1. 问 AI：「用 `nebula_sources` 看看现在接了哪些来源，然后把 `<你的记忆在哪>` 接进来。」
2. AI 会读 [docs/integration-guide.md](docs/integration-guide.md)，判断属于哪种情况：
   - **落盘的 SQLite / 笔记目录** → 往 `sources.json` 加一条 source，重启页面即可（热载）。
   - **只有 API 的远端服务** → 让那个插件在写入后 `POST /api/memory-nebula/ingest`，或调 `nebula_ingest`。
   - **只想临时补上下文** → 直接 `nebula_bridge(memory_ids=[…])`，不用接来源。
3. `GET /sources` 或 `nebula_sources(verbose=true)` 确认新来源「读到了 N 条、没有读取失败」。

适配器契约、列名猜测规则、`sources.json` 全字段见 [docs/adapters.md](docs/adapters.md)。

装卸（junction + `dsh.profile.bundles`）、热载边界、sidecar 过渡通道见 [docs/operations.md](docs/operations.md)。

## 目录结构

```
lib/
  index.js            插件入口：注册 9 个工具、注入提示、挂 /api/memory-nebula
  client.js           左侧栏入口
  host/               引擎（只读取数、建图、检索、体检、转写解析）
    nebula.js         门面：索引 / 缓存 / 巡检 / publicGraph / detail / bridge
    graph.js          建图、打分、剪枝、auditHygiene
    recall.js         seed + 扩散激活
    bridge.js         补充包：ids → 扩散 → 排除已读 → 预算内挑几条
    ledger.js         注入账本：谁什么时候注入过什么（跨插件共用）
    adapters/         来源适配器（meow / notes / sqlite / ingest）+ 发现与配置
    live.js           引擎热载（递归枚举 lib/host，按 mtime 复制再 import）
    http.js           路由（启动时静态加载）
  web/                前端（每次请求从磁盘读，改完刷新即生效）
    app.js            状态、面板、筛选、命令面板、导出、时间轴
    render.js         2D 星云：力导向 + 区块点亮 + Path2D 批处理
    space3d.js        3D 星系 / 时间螺旋：WebGL 光点
scripts/smoke.mjs     只读契约自查（63 项）
scripts/release-check.mjs  发布静态检查
scripts/bench.mjs     10k 性能基准（建图 / 检索 / 体检 / 快照 / 内存）
test/                 node:test 单元测试（124 项）
sidecar.ps1           Windows 独立引擎开关
```

## 隐私与安全

- 只读：所有记忆库以 `readOnly` 打开；写入只落在 `$DSH_HOME/memory-nebula/`。
- 只连本机：独立引擎绑定 `127.0.0.1`；跨站读拿不到 CORS、跨站写 403；页面带 CSP。
- 独立引擎可加 `--token <至少 12 字符>` 开本机口令；不传时保持本地即开即用，宿主内走 DSH 的 Host/认证围栏。开启后浏览器直接打开页面会看到输口令的登录页，口令错误不会放行。
- 全文细节与威胁模型见 [docs/security.md](docs/security.md)。
- 性能预算与 10k 实测见 [docs/benchmarks.md](docs/benchmarks.md)。

## 支持与反馈

- 先跑 `node scripts/doctor.mjs`，再对照 [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md)；多数空白页/空图/3D 问题能在那里解决。
- 提 issue 请用仓库里的模板，附 `doctor` 输出、DSH/Node/系统版本、复现步骤；**不要贴记忆正文、token、`.npmrc` 或私有路径**。
- 安全漏洞走私密 advisory，见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。完整支持边界见 [SUPPORT.md](SUPPORT.md)。

## 版本与许可

- 当前版本 `1.7.0`，MIT。
- 打包内容：`lib/`、`scripts/`、`docs/`、`cordis.patch.yml`、`README.md` / `README.en.md`、`CHANGELOG.md`、`LICENSE`、`sidecar.ps1`（`test/` 与 `dev/` 不进包）。
- 前端改动刷新页面即生效；`lib/host/` 下所有引擎文件（含 `adapters/`、`bridge.js`、`ledger.js`）由 LiveEngine 热载，`http.js` / `index.js` / `live.js` 改动要重启 DSH 或走独立引擎。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-remote-connect

DSH 插件：**手机浏览器操作电脑上的 DSH**，以及**两台电脑之间同步插件 / 技能 / 规则 / 配置 / 会话**。

装好之后在 **DSH → 设置 → 远程互联** 里操作，五个页签：概览 / 连接 / 同步 / 手机通道 / 诊断。

## 装

```bash
# 从市场索引装（DSH → 设置 → 插件 → 发现，加索引源后点安装）
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh/main/index.json

# 或者直接钉版本装
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh.git#v1.0.56&path:/plugins/dsh-remote-connect"

# 或者拷到 profile 的 plugins 目录，再跑一次自带安装器
node scripts/install.mjs --profile <profile 名>      # --dry-run 先看要写什么
```

`npm` 装不了 git 子目录（会报 `ENOENT … package.json`），用 `pnpm`，或上面的拷贝方式。

## 两件事

| 能力 | 用法 | 前提 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 📱 手机通道 | 手机扫码连上这台电脑的 DSH，浏览器里直接对话 | 本机有一份 `phone-bridge` 目录 |
| 💻 电脑互联 | 两台电脑配对后互相同步插件 / 技能 / 规则 / 配置 / 会话 | 两台都装本插件，同网段或能直连 |

手机通道的桥接目录按这个顺序找，都不用手动配：

```
config.bridgeDir  >  config.dir  >  环境变量 DSH_PHONE_BRIDGE_DIR
  >  自动探测 $DSH_HOME/phone-bridge、./phone-bridge、~/phone-bridge
  >  第一个候选目录
```

自动探测只认里面真有 `ensure-running.ps1` 或 `server.mjs` 的目录；一个都没有时页签会显示
「本机还没装手机通道」并告诉你它在找哪儿，不会甩一个 ENOENT 给你。细节见 [docs/PHONE.md](docs/PHONE.md)。

## 接口

本机路由挂在 `/dsh-remote-connect-api/*` 下共 30 条，手机通道另有 `/dsh-phone-api/*` 5 条；
两台电脑之间走 `/dsh-link/v1/*`（health / hello / inventory / export / apply / rollback / bye）。
完整清单在 [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)，`test/docs-guard.mjs` 会拿运行时注册的路由
去对文档，改了代码忘了改文档会红。

## 安全

- 配对走 scrypt + 挑战应答 + HKDF + HMAC 签名，帧用 AES-256-GCM；会话 12 小时，nonce 防重放。
- 同一 IP 连续失败 10 次锁 10 分钟。
- 同步默认排除依赖、缓存、日志、密钥、凭据；插件自身的数据目录永久排除。
- 威胁模型与边界见 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)。

## 开发

```bash
node test/run-all.mjs     # 全量：client-smoke / inventory-guard / deps / bridge-dir / docs-guard / plugin-smoke / e2e
```

零第三方依赖，`node >= 20`。MIT，作者 茄茄子。

# dsh-remote-connect

[![test](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh/actions/workflows/test.yml)

> DSH 插件：**用手机远程操作电脑上的 DSH**，以及**两台电脑之间互相同步**插件 / 技能 / 规则 / 配置 / 会话。

装在 DSH 里之后，设置页会多出一个 **「远程互联」** 分区，两个能力都在里面。

| 能力 | 做什么 | 入口 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 📱 **手机通道** | 手机浏览器直接打开电脑上的 DSH：二维码配对、局域网直连，或走你自己的公网域名 | 设置 → 远程互联 → 手机通道 |
| 💻 **电脑互联** | 两台电脑互扫配对，同步插件 / 技能 / 规则 / 配置 / 会话，随时可回滚 | 设置 → 远程互联 → 互联 |

- 插件名：`dsh-remote-connect`
- 版本：1.0.56
- 许可证：MIT
- 需要的 DSH：带 `webServer` 服务、客户端支持 `settings.section` 插槽的版本

---

## 安装

### 方式一：从市场索引装（推荐）

DSH → 插件市场 → 索引源，填：

```
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh/main/index.json
```

这条是**主地址**：推完一般几十秒就能看到新版本。

国内网络打不开 raw 时，可以换 jsDelivr 镜像：

```
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh@main/index.json
```

> ⚠ **jsDelivr 是镜像，会滞后。** 我们对它实测过：`s-maxage=43200`（12 小时）加上不同边缘节点各存各的，
> 同一时刻不同人看到的可能是 1.0.0 / 1.0.2 / 最新版三种。刚发完版就换索引源、又恰好命中旧节点，
> 就会以为「怎么装到的还是旧版」。要「现在就是最新」，用上面的 raw 地址；要「永远是某一版」，
> 用下面的 git 直装并钉标签或 40 位 SHA。

索引里只有这一个插件，版本 `1.0.56`，来源是本仓库的 `plugins/dsh-remote-connect` 子目录。

### 方式二：用 git 直装

插件在 monorepo 子目录里，`npm` 装不了（它不支持 git 子目录），用 pnpm：

```powershell
# 用发行标签装（推荐，标签指向这一版的发布提交）
pnpm add "git+https://github.com/hanhan9999999999999999999/remote-connect-dsh.git#v1.0.56&path:/plugins/dsh-remote-connect"
```

想钉死某个 commit 也可以，把 `#v1.0.56` 换成 40 位 SHA；`index.json` 里钉的就是同一版的具体
commit（社区市场要求 40 位 SHA），两者由发版流程一起更新，见 `RELEASING.md` 第 5 节。

### 方式三：手动放进 profile

```powershell
# 把仓库里的插件目录拷进当前 profile 的 node_modules
Copy-Item -Recurse .\plugins\dsh-remote-connect "$env:DSH_HOME\profiles\desktop\node_modules\dsh-remote-connect"
```

包内自带 `scripts/install.mjs`，也可以用：

```powershell
node .\plugins\dsh-remote-connect\scripts\install.mjs --dry-run   # 先看要写什么，不落盘
node .\plugins\dsh-remote-connect\scripts\install.mjs             # 真装
node .\plugins\dsh-remote-connect\scripts\install.mjs --purge     # 连插件文件一起卸掉
node .\plugins\dsh-remote-connect\scripts\install.mjs --help      # 全部参数
```

它只改 `$DSH_HOME\plugins\` 与 profile 的 `package.json`（改前留 `.bak-<时间戳>`），**不会重启 DSH**。

装完重启 DSH，进 设置 → 远程互联。

---

## 手机通道怎么用

1. 电脑上装好本插件，DSH 开着；
2. 设置 → 远程互联 → **手机通道** → 点「启动」，拿到二维码 / 配对码；
3. 手机连同一个 Wi-Fi，浏览器扫码打开；不在同一网段就走公网域名（见下）。

**手机通道需要有 `phone-bridge/` 目录**——它是每台机器自己的运行态（路径、端口、域名、私钥都绑在这上面），插件不打包它。目录里至少要有 `ensure-running.ps1` 或 `server.mjs`。

路径优先级：

```
config.bridgeDir  >  config.dir  >  环境变量 DSH_PHONE_BRIDGE_DIR
                  >  自动探测（$DSH_HOME/phone-bridge、./phone-bridge、~/phone-bridge）
                  >  第一个候选目录（找不到就显示「还没装手机通道」，不报 ENOENT）
```

自动探测只认真的装好的目录（里面有 `ensure-running.ps1` 或 `server.mjs`），所以把 `phone-bridge/` 放在 DSH 数据目录或启动目录旁边就不用配了。

配置写在 DSH 插件配置里：

```yaml
dsh-remote-connect:
  bridgeDir: '/path/to/phone-bridge'
```

没装 `phone-bridge` 时不会报错，面板显示「本机还没装手机通道」并给出当前找的路径。

细节（接口、状态字段、停用方式）：[plugins/dsh-remote-connect/docs/PHONE.md](plugins/dsh-remote-connect/docs/PHONE.md)

---

## 电脑互联怎么用

1. 两台电脑都装本插件，各自在 设置 → 远程互联 里设设备名和密码；
2. A 点「发现」或直接填 B 的地址 → 配对；
3. 配对后在 A 上勾选要同步的类别（插件 / 技能 / 规则 / 配置 / 会话），点「推送」或「拉取」；
4. 每次同步都有记录，`回滚` 可以退回上一份。

同步走的接口一览（前缀 `/dsh-remote-connect-api`）：

| 方法 | 路径 | 说明 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/status` | 本机互联状态、设备名、端口 |
| GET | `/diagnostics` | 诊断信息 |
| GET | `/logs` | 最近 300 行日志 |
| POST | `/config` | 改配置 |
| GET | `/deps` · POST `/deps/install` | 依赖检查 / 安装 |
| POST | `/device/name` | 改设备名 |
| POST | `/password/set` · `/password/rotate` | 设密码 / 换密码 |
| POST | `/server/start` · `/server/stop` | 起停互联服务 |
| POST | `/discover` · `/connect` | 发现对端 / 配对连接 |
| POST | `/peer/disconnect` · `/peer/forget` · `/peer/rename` · `/peer/probe` | 对端管理 |
| POST | `/inventory` · `/sync` | 列出可同步内容 / 开始同步 |
| POST | `/task/status` · `/task/cancel` | 同步任务进度 / 取消 |
| POST | `/local/syncs` · `/local/rollback` | 本机同步记录 / 回滚 |
| POST | `/remote/syncs` · `/remote/rollback` | 对端同步记录 / 回滚 |
| GET | `/phone/status` | 手机通道状态（同进程直连，不走回环） |
| POST | `/phone/start` · `/phone/stop` · `/phone/port` · `/phone/paircode` | 手机通道启停、换端口、改配对码；参数放请求体（`{port}` / `{code}`） |

手机通道自身还注册了一组 `/dsh-phone-api/*`（`status` / `start` / `stop` / `port` / `paircode`）。

**为什么面板走 `/dsh-remote-connect-api/phone/*` 而不是 `127.0.0.1`**：回环请求没有 renderer token，会被浏览器访问策略挡成 403，所以面板和桥接在同一进程里直连函数。

---

## 目录结构

```
plugins/dsh-remote-connect/
├── index.js              Host 半：注册 /dsh-remote-connect-api/*，挂载手机通道
├── client.js             客户端半：设置页「远程互联」分区（slots/设置/locale）
├── host/
│   ├── service.mjs       互联服务：配对、同步、回滚（编排）
│   ├── tasks.mjs         同步任务表（内存、上限 40 条、按开始时间淘汰）
│   ├── peer.mjs/peers.mjs 对端握手、探测、对端表
│   ├── discovery.mjs     局域网发现
│   ├── inventory.mjs     可同步内容清点
│   ├── pack.mjs/tar.mjs 打包与解包
│   ├── crypto.mjs        配对码 / 密码派生
│   ├── frames.mjs        传输分帧
│   ├── phone.mjs         手机通道：启停编排、状态、配对码
│   ├── port-scan.mjs     端口窥探：解析 netstat、认领桥接进程、挑空端口
│   ├── server.mjs        互联 HTTP 服务
│   ├── guard.mjs         连接守卫：IP 提取、设备字段清洗、失败锁定、签名窗口
│   ├── apply.mjs/config.mjs/deps.mjs/util.mjs  装配、配置、依赖、常量
├── locale/{zh,en}.json   文案（分区名「远程互联」/ Remote Connect）
├── docs/{PHONE,ARCHITECTURE}.md
├── cordis.patch.yml      插件清单补丁
└── test/                 客户端冒烟、清单守卫、依赖、路由、端到端
```

---

## 开发与测试

```powershell
cd plugins/dsh-remote-connect
node test/run-all.mjs          # 插件全套（约 10 秒）
node ../../tools/validate-index.mjs   # 市场索引校验（无依赖）
node ../../tools/pin-index.mjs --version x.y.z --commit <SHA>   # 钉版本（固定缩进 + LF）
```

包含：客户端冒烟（插槽/文案/顺序）、清单守卫（`files` 与实际文件一致）、依赖声明、路由（35 条断言 + 手机通道 5 条）、端到端（health / pull / push / rollback）。全部用临时目录，不碰你真机的数据。

CI 在 `.github/workflows/test.yml`：ubuntu + windows × node 20/22，克隆下来就能看到结果；索引校验与插件测试都会跑。

改完插件后的发版流程（改版本 → 提代码 → 拿 SHA → 更新 `index.json` → 校验 → 实装验证 → 社区市场提 PR）写在 [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md)。

---

## 安全边界

- 连接是**配对码 + 密码**双要素，配对后对端才会出现在列表里；
- 同步内容由你自己勾选，默认不包含任何密钥文件；
- 局域网 HTTP 是明文，信任模型写在 [plugins/dsh-remote-connect/SECURITY.md](plugins/dsh-remote-connect/SECURITY.md)；
- 走公网域名时用的是你自己的隧道和证书，别把私钥提交进仓库（本仓库 `.gitignore` 已排除 `runtime/`）。

---

## 相关

- [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) — 发版与上架手册
- [index.json](index.json) — DSH 插件市场索引（format 1）
- [LICENSE](LICENSE) — MIT

ruff](https://img.shields.io/badge/lint-ruff-D7FF64.svg)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![Ask DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/badge.svg)](https://deepwiki.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard) | ![HOL whole dark logo](https://hol.org/brand/Logo_Whole_Dark.png) | **Stop risky AI actions before they compromise your machine.** HOL Guard is a local-first security layer for AI agents, tools, plugins, skills, MCP servers, and package installs.

[Install HOL Guard](https://hol.org/guard/activate)
[Read the documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/blob/main/docs/guard/get-started.md)
[PyPI Package (`hol-guard`)](https://pypi.org/project/hol-guard/)
[Report an Issue](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/issues) | | :--- | :--- | HOL Guard reviews agent actions before they run: shell commands, file access, package installs, and MCP tool calls. It detects secret exposure, destructive operations, prompt injection, and supply-chain risks, then allows, blocks, or requests approval according to your policy. Run it locally without an account. Use the CLI and local dashboard to manage protection, resolve approvals, and inspect decision history. Optional [Guard Cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) adds shared history, team policy, and fleet management. [Get started](#install-hol-guard) · [Supported agents](#supported-ai-agents) · [Plugin scanner](#plugin-scanner) · [Documentation](#documentation) · [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) · [Contribute an adapter](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md) · [Development](#development) ### Sponsors #### Gold sponsors

#### Bronze sponsors

   

Thank you to our sponsors for supporting HOL Guard. Some sponsor links are referral links.
Sponsorship does not change Guard's security decisions or coverage.

## Install HOL Guard Requires Python 3.10 or newer, [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/stable/installation/), and a matching native runtime. Check the [platform support and Windows ARM64 setup notes](docs/guard/get-started.md#platform-support) before installing. ```bash pipx install hol-guard hol-guard init ``` The first-run wizard discovers supported agents and walks you through protection setup. It asks before each setup change, including opening the dashboard, installing agent integrations, and connecting optional cloud services. Check your installation: ```bash hol-guard --version hol-guard status ``` To update an existing installation: ```bash hol-guard update ``` For manual setup, see the [installation guide](docs/guard/get-started.md). Annotated release notes with upgrade context live at [hol.org/guard/releases](https://hol.org/guard/releases); raw releases and prereleases are on the [GitHub releases page](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-guard/releases). ## What HOL Guard Protects | Surface | Protection | | :--- | :--- | | **Shell commands and file access** | Reviews destructive operations, sensitive file access, credential exposure, and suspicious outbound commands. | | **Package installs** | Evaluates supported package-manager operations against supply-chain intelligence before installation. | | **Plugins, skills, and agent configuration** | Inventories local artifacts and reviews new or changed tools before launch. | | **MCP servers and tools** | Inspects server configuration and reviews tool calls through supported hooks and managed proxies. | | **Prompts and tool results** | Screens supported events for prompt injection and sensitive content. | | **Approvals and evidence** | Routes decisions to native prompts or the approval center, and records local receipts for review. | Guard connects through native agent hooks, managed MCP proxies, and launch integrations. Coverage depends on the events each agent exposes; the [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) documents enforcement, approval delivery, and failure behavior per integration. ## Supported AI Agents Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Cursor, Cline, Gemini CLI, Grok, Hermes, Kimi Code, Pi, oh-my-pi, OpenClaw, OpenCode, Antigravity, ZCode, and Devin. [Paseo](docs/guard/paseo.md) is supported through these native provider integrations, with per-provider coverage. For example, to set up Codex explicitly: ```bash hol-guard install codex hol-guard run codex --dry-run hol-guard run codex ``` The dry run records the current artifact state before launch. For Codex, Guard installs native pre-tool hooks and refuses a managed launch if those hooks are missing or disabled. [Agent support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) · [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) ## Everyday Use | Task | Command | | :--- | :--- | | Check protection status | `hol-guard status` | | Diagnose an agent integration | `hol-guard doctor codex` | | Inspect changes before launch | `hol-guard diff codex` | | Review pending approvals | `hol-guard approvals` | | Approve or deny a request | `hol-guard approvals approve ` / `hol-guard approvals deny ` | | Read decision history | `hol-guard receipts` | | List tracked artifacts | `hol-guard inventory` | | Export an AI bill of materials | `hol-guard abom --format json` | | Scan workspace dependencies | `hol-guard supply-chain scan` | | Connect optional cloud sync | `hol-guard connect` | ### Understand a paused command Inspect the command's classification and matching rules: ```bash hol-guard command test 'rm -rf ./build' hol-guard command explain 'git clean -ndx' hol-guard command extensions command.git --json ``` `command test` and `command explain` inspect the command without executing it or creating an approval. Use `hol-guard approvals` to resolve a pending request and `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. The [Extension directory](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) lists command coverage generated from the Rust-compiled catalog. External contributions require explicit opt-in; required core protections remain enabled. To add coverage, follow the [Extension contribution guide](docs/guard/extensions/contributing.md). ### Check a package ```bash hol-guard supply-chain sync hol-guard supply-chain scan hol-guard supply-chain explain minimist@1.2.5 --ecosystem npm ``` The package verdict includes the available advisory evidence and ecosystem coverage. See the [get-started guide](docs/guard/get-started.md) for package-manager interception and the [remediation guide](docs/guard/remediation.md) for handling false positives. ## Plugin Scanner This repository also ships `plugin-scanner`, a CLI for maintainers who want security and quality checks before publishing agent plugins, skills, and MCP integrations. ```bash pipx install plugin-scanner plugin-scanner scan . plugin-scanner lint . plugin-scanner verify . ``` | Command | Purpose | | :--- | :--- | | `scan` | Security findings and a quality report across detected package surfaces. | | `lint` | Rule-level authoring feedback. | | `verify` | Install-surface and runtime readiness checks. | | `submit` | A submission artifact for one plugin package. | | `doctor` | Component diagnostics and troubleshooting bundles. | The scanner detects Codex, Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, Gemini CLI, Kimi Code, and OpenCode package formats. Use `plugin-scanner --list-ecosystems` to list them or `--ecosystem` to select one. At a Codex marketplace root, it discovers local plugin entries automatically. Checks cover manifests, secrets, MCP transport and command configuration, approval defaults, skills, dependency lockfiles, and GitHub Actions permissions. Optional Cisco integrations add skill and MCP analysis. Reports support text, JSON, Markdown, and SARIF. ```bash plugin-scanner scan . --format sarif --output plugin-scanner.sarif plugin-scanner scan . --fail-on-severity high ``` Quality grades use the checks applicable to each package. Trust scoring has separate provenance and weights; see the [skill](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md), [MCP](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md), and [plugin](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) scoring references. ### Package a plugin for every runtime `hol-guard plugin` is the Plugin Kit. Point it at one plugin source, such as a Claude Code plugin, Codex plugin, Gemini CLI extension, MCP Registry `server.json` or a folder of skills, and it checks the source and writes a ready-to-load copy for each agent runtime that can use it. It runs locally, reads only the folder you name and makes no network calls. ```bash hol-guard plugin check # what marketplaces and runtime loaders would reject hol-guard plugin package # writes dist/hol-plugin// for each runtime hol-guard plugin convert --to agent-plugins # Agent Plugins 1.0 package, checked against the spec hol-guard plugin links # install commands per runtime, plus listing links hol-guard plugin card # draft .well-known plugin card as JSON hol-guard plugin init --name my-plugin # scaffold a new plugin in an empty folder ``` Runtimes: `claude-code`, `codex`, `gemini-cli`, `cursor`, `vscode`, `opencode`, `mcp-registry`, `agent-skills` and `agent-plugins`. See [the Plugin Kit guide](docs/guard/plugin-kit.md). ### GitHub Actions Add the scanner to a plugin repository: ```yaml name: Plugin security on: [push, pull_request] permissions: contents: read jobs: scan: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6 - uses: hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action@fdb49f9d85321a2ced2933301b395dd3c1ce9c8f # v1.2.631 with: plugin_dir: "." min_score: 80 fail_on_severity: high ``` See the [action documentation](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/ai-plugin-scanner-action) for SARIF uploads, submission workflows, and machine-readable outputs. The action source is maintained in [`action/`](action/). ### Optional Cisco analysis The baseline packages work without Cisco dependencies. To add Cisco skill scanning, use Python 3.11 through 3.14 and install the extra in an isolated environment: ```bash pipx install 'plugin-scanner[cisco]' ``` For Cisco MCP analysis, use the repository's [Docker image](Dockerfile) or the `cisco-mcp` dependency group: ```bash uv sync --extra dev --extra cisco --group cisco-mcp --python 3.13 uv run plugin-scanner scan . --cisco-skill-scan on --cisco-mcp-scan on ``` The published `cisco` extra provides skill scanning; the separate `cisco-mcp` group supplies the MCP scanner. Dependency versions and Python constraints are maintained in [`pyproject.toml`](pyproject.toml). ## Ecosystem Support | Ecosystem | Detection surfaces | | :--- | :--- | | Codex | `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `marketplace.json`, `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | | Claude Code | `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | | DeepSeek Harness | `package.json` with `dsh.bundle`, declared patches, and Cordis `apply(ctx)` exports, or `dsh.bundle.mode` set to `"patch"` for patch-only bundles | | Gemini CLI | `gemini-extension.json`, `commands/**/*.toml` | | Kimi Code | `kimi.plugin.json`, `.kimi-plugin/plugin.json`, declared skills, agents, commands, prompts, and MCP servers | | OpenCode | `opencode.json`, `opencode.jsonc`, `.opencode/commands`, `.opencode/plugins` | Use `--ecosystem auto` to detect supported packages in a repository, or select an ecosystem explicitly: ```bash plugin-scanner scan ./plugins-repo --ecosystem claude plugin-scanner scan ./dsh-plugin --ecosystem deepseek-harness ``` ## What The Scanner Checks | Category | Coverage | | :--- | :--- | | Manifest validation | Required fields, versions, declared paths, interface metadata, links, and assets. | | Security | Hardcoded secrets, unsafe MCP commands and transports, and risky approval defaults. | | Operational security | GitHub Actions permissions and pinned dependencies, privileged checkout patterns, Dependabot, and lockfiles. | | Plugin packaging | README and license files, skill frontmatter, ignore rules, and accidentally committed environment files. | | Marketplace | Manifest validity, local package discovery, and safe source paths. | | Skill and MCP analysis | Analyzer availability, findings, and analyzability from optional Cisco integrations. | | Code quality | Dynamic code execution and shell-injection patterns. | ## How Trust Scoring Works Plugin Scanner reports a quality grade alongside trust provenance. Quality scores are normalized across applicable checks, so optional surfaces do not inflate a package's grade. Skill trust uses the HCS-28 baseline adapter IDs, weights, and denominator rules. MCP and Codex plugin trust use explicit adapters, weights, and contribution modes documented in the local specifications: - [Skill Trust Local Draft](docs/trust/skill-trust-local.md) - [MCP Trust Draft](docs/trust/mcp-trust-draft.md) - [Codex Plugin Trust Draft](docs/trust/plugin-trust-draft.md) ## CLI Usage ```bash # Structured security report plugin-scanner scan ./my-plugin --format json --profile public-marketplace # Inspect authoring rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --list-rules plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --explain README_MISSING # Apply supported mechanical fixes plugin-scanner lint ./my-plugin --fix --profile strict-security # Verify package readiness; --online permits live probes plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --format json plugin-scanner verify ./my-plugin --online --format text # Generate a submission artifact for one plugin plugin-scanner submit ./my-plugin --profile public-marketplace --attest dist/plugin-quality.json # Collect component diagnostics plugin-scanner doctor ./my-plugin --component mcp --bundle dist/doctor.zip ``` For a repository marketplace, `scan`, `lint`, `verify`, and `doctor` can target the root. `submit` targets one plugin package. ## Codex Spec Alignment The scanner recognizes Codex plugin manifests, interface metadata, declared assets, and marketplace packages: - Local manifest paths use `./` prefixes; `lint --fix` preserves or adds them. - `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the preferred marketplace location, with root `marketplace.json` supported for compatibility. - Interface validation checks declared links and assets without requiring an undocumented `type` field. - `verify --online` checks HTTP remote reachability. Its source lives in [`action/`](action/), and the [publication workflow](.github/workflows/publish-action-repo.yml) distributes the action bundle. The legacy [HOL Codex Plugin Scanner Action](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/hol-codex-plugin-scanner-action) remains available for existing workflows. ### Plugin Author Submission Flow Use `submission_enabled: true` to open or reuse a submission issue when a plugin meets the configured threshold. `submission_token` must have permission to create issues in the target submission repository. The action emits submission status and issue URLs as outputs. See the [action's input reference](action/action.yml) for `submission_score_threshold`, `submission_token`, and the target repository options. ### Registry Payload For Plugin Ecosystem Automation Set `registry_payload_output` to write a machine-readable payload for a registry or badge pipeline. The action also exposes `score`, `grade`, `grade_label`, `max_severity`, and `findings_total` outputs and can write a job summary. The [HOL Registry Broker plugin](https://github.com/hashgraph-online/registry-broker-codex-plugin) is an example of an agent plugin in the [HOL Plugin Registry](https://hol.org/registry/plugins). Its [registry listing](https://hol.org/registry/plugins/hol%2Fregistry-broker-codex-plugin) provides current trust information. ## Why HOL Guard AI agents can run commands, install dependencies, read files, and call external tools within one session. HOL Guard reviews those actions at supported execution points and keeps the policy decision, approval request, and receipt together. Use it for AI agent security on a developer machine, MCP security around connected tools, and supply-chain checks for packages and plugins. Teams can add Guard Cloud for shared approvals and policy management while retaining local protection. ## Frequently Asked Questions ### What is HOL Guard? HOL Guard is open-source antivirus and runtime protection for AI agents. It reviews supported tool calls, shell commands, file access, and package operations for risks such as secret exposure, prompt injection, destructive actions, and malicious dependencies. ### Does HOL Guard work without a cloud account? Yes. Local protection, CLI commands, approvals, and receipts work without signing in. Guard Cloud is optional and adds synchronized evidence, team controls, and fleet visibility. The [support matrix](docs/guard/harness-support.md) explains which events and enforcement paths each adapter supports. ### What is the difference between HOL Guard and Plugin Scanner? Install `hol-guard` to protect agent activity on your machine. Install `plugin-scanner` to inspect plugin packages and enforce security and quality checks in CI. This repository builds and publishes both distributions. ### How does HOL Guard protect MCP servers? Guard inspects MCP server configuration and reviews supported MCP tool calls through agent hooks and managed proxies. Plugin Scanner checks MCP configuration and HTTP remote reachability; optional Cisco MCP analysis adds static security findings. ### Why did Guard pause my command? The action may need approval under your active policy, or its tools or artifacts may have changed. Start with `hol-guard approvals`, inspect the command with `hol-guard command explain ''`, and use `hol-guard receipts` to review the recorded decision. ## Documentation For enrollment or stale native authority errors, see [extension-control recovery](docs/guard/extension-control-recovery.md). | Guide | Contents | | :--- | :--- | | [Get started](docs/guard/get-started.md) | Installation, manual setup, package protection, and common commands. | | [Agent support](docs/guard/harness-support.md) | Integration coverage and approval behavior. | | [Architecture](docs/guard/architecture.md) | Runtime components and decision flow. | | [Policy specification](spec/guard-policy/v1alpha1/README.md) | GuardPolicy document format. | | [Policy recipes](docs/guard/policy-recipes.md) | Configuration examples for common workflows. | | [Extensions](docs/guard/extensions/README.md) | Built-in command rules and contribution guidance. | | [Native extension authoring](docs/guard/extension-builder/README.md) | Canonical JSON sources, the Rust compiler, portable fixtures, and review kits. | | [Contribute an extension](#contribute-a-new-extension) | Generate, review, integrate, and test a new extension with the CLI. | | [Local vs. cloud](docs/guard/local-vs-cloud.md) | Local capabilities and optional cloud services. | | [Troubleshooting](docs/guard/troubleshooting.md) | Diagnosis and recovery. | | [Security](SECURITY.md) | Vulnerability reporting and disclosure policy. | ## Contribute a New Extension To integrate a new AI coding agent or IDE, use the separate [harness adapter contribution guide](docs/guard/adapter-contributions.md). # dsh-agent-herald

Herald, the sovereign release agent: a publisher that earns its keep
releasing files whose decryption is earned through ownership — hold a
DataDAO community's token and its corpus opens for you.

## The definition

| File | Prompt section | Order | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `soul.md` | `agent:soul` | -500 | Who Herald is: goal, community covenant, money ethics, custody |
| `process.md` | `agent:process` | -400 | What Herald does: release pipeline, gate selection, money loop, community ops |
| `workflow.md` | `agent:workflow` | -350 | Stage manual: source→ingest→analyze→seal→upload→sync→cleanup, all harness-native |
| `reference/aol-protocol.md` | `agent:aol-protocol` | -300 | Haven-AOL v1/v3/v4 mechanics: derivation, epochs, market-cap math, errors |

`apply()` reads the four docs and registers each as a system-prompt
section (the tool-bash pattern). Sections render before the deployment
persona prefix (identity first, then deployment instructions, then
first-party guidance). No config — the docs are the config. A missing
or empty doc throws at apply: an agent never boots without its soul.

Token cost is fixed per deployment (the docs are static, prefix-stable
for KV cache); edits to any doc change every subsequent prompt.

## Money loop

Release tokens launched with the agent as fee recipient earn
mint/burn royalties; venue fees accumulate in routers and sweep on
cadence; v4 drips tie unlocks to market cap so community buying
drives both unlocks and royalties. `process.md` §3 is the procedure.

## Sealing is harness-native

`aol_seal` (v1/v3/v4) seals in-container under the canister-fetched
verification key. Herald seals its own releases, verifies the
binding (`aol_gate_info`), and trial-decrypts before announcing.

## Note: the dead `persona` key (2026-09)

`dsh-persona/cordis.patch.yml` and `docker/profile.patch.yml` set
`system-prompt.config.persona`, which the installed
`dsh-system-prompt` (0.1.7-rc.2 and 0.2.1-alpha.1 alike) never reads — its schema declares
`personaPrefix`/`personaSuffix` (`Config({persona: ...})` parses but
the constructor ignores the key). Until this package, the deployment
ran with an empty persona. Herald's sections are the live identity
now; those `persona` rows are inert documentation. If they are ever
migrated to `personaPrefix`, that text will render *after* these
sections (order 0) — keep it short or fold it here.

# dsh-web3

## Quickstart

One-shot get-started (builds latest `02ca906` stack, tests, starts `xmtp-prod`, spits QR + wallet):

```sh
bash quickstart.sh
# or: MUSE_SPARK_API_KEY=<your-key> bash quickstart.sh
```

Spits `Invite URL: https://popup.convos.org/v2?i=...` + ANSI QR (`qrencode -t ANSIUTF8`) and wallet `0xa85dD3FbD8C2c831Ef156036F14638CcFf03b44e` (dynamic `wallet_info`→`ctx.wallet.address`). Also available: `./show-convos-qr.sh` / `./show-xmtp-qr.sh` for QR-only.


Reimplementation of the sovereign web3 agent harness using DeepSeek harness as core, where everything is a plug-in. Replaces https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-core and https://github.com/Haven-hvn/haven-adapters

There is deliberately **no aggregate bundle**: people may want one capability
and not another, so each package ships its own `dsh.bundle.patch` →
`cordis.patch.yml` inserting only its own rows, and installs independently:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-haven/<package>
```

## The packages

| Package | Haven concept | dsh seam it lands on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`dsh-wallet`](./dsh-wallet) | `WalletIdentity` custody ("the key never leaves this boundary") + the `CryptoAdapter` contract | `ctx.wallet` service; credentials resolved through `ctx.credentials` per operation — configuration carries *references*, never keys |
| [`dsh-wallet-ethereum`](./dsh-wallet-ethereum) | `EthereumCryptoAdapter` → OWS migration plan | provider plugin registering a `CryptoAdapter` per chain family, backed by `@open-wallet-standard/core` (sign-only; the standard handles all chain families) |
| [`dsh-treasury`](./dsh-treasury) | `Treasury` machine: balances, expenses, FUNDED/LOW/CRITICAL/DEPLETED survival gradient | storage-domain tables + derived state; a policy plugin short-circuits `agent/request` and `tools/pre-execute`, metered off `llm/token-meter` |
| [`dsh-channel-xmtp`](./dsh-channel-xmtp) | `XmtpChannel` direct agent↔user messaging | one dsh agent per conversation (`ctx.agents`), inbound via `agent.followup`, replies via `sendText`; EOA identity signs through `ctx.wallet` |
| [`dsh-storage-synapse`](./dsh-storage-synapse) | `SynapseStorageAdapter` + `StorageBackend` pinning | `ctx.synapse` + `synapse_pin` / `synapse_pin_status` agent tools; every node request wallet-signed per operation |
| [`dsh-wallet-tools`](./dsh-wallet-tools) | wallet address/balance exposure (replaces hard-coded persona) | `wallet_info` tool via `ctx.tools` + `ctx.wallet.address()` live (no hard-coded `0x...`) |
| [`dsh-persona`](./dsh-persona) | Haven persona / system instructions | `agent/request` composition; generic instruction to call `wallet_info` when address/balance/funding asked |
| [`dsh-tool-prowlarr`](./dsh-tool-prowlarr) | Prowlarr indexer search bridge (use-case agnostic) | `prowlarr_indexers` / `prowlarr_search` read-only tools via `ctx.tools`; no wallet seam |
| [`dsh-tool-acquisition`](./dsh-tool-acquisition) | Download/acquisition arm (Haven `acquisition/` port, torrent clients outsourced) | `acquire_submit` / `acquire_status` tools via `ctx.tools`; qBittorrent → Transmission failover, no wallet seam |

## Composition

`dsh-wallet` is the custody root; the other packages build on it:

```
dsh-wallet  ←  dsh-wallet-ethereum   (registers the evm CryptoAdapter)
    ↑
    ├── dsh-channel-xmtp             (signs XMTP identity per signature)
    ├── dsh-storage-synapse          (signs node requests per request)
    └── dsh-wallet-tools             (exposes wallet_info via ctx.tools → ctx.wallet)
dsh-persona                           (composes agent/request; calls wallet_info, no hard-coded address)
dsh-treasury                          (independent; needs the storage stack)
```

A typical full install:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-wallet-ethereum \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-treasury \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-channel-xmtp \
  /path/to/dsh-haven/dsh-storage-synapse \
  @open-wallet-standard/core @xmtp/node-sdk
```

The two SDKs are optional peers: every package loads, mounts, and tests
without them (lazy imports with actionable errors; tests substitute
`internals.*` seams).

## Prerequisites

- **Storage stack** (`dsh-treasury` only): the profile must mount `storage`,
  `storage-json`/`storage-sqlite`, and `storage-domain` rows (present in
  `dsh-web-app`; absent in `dsh-base`). The treasury patch does NOT insert
  them — a row id inserted by two layers mounts the plugin twice.
- **Agent stack** (`dsh-channel-xmtp` only): agents/sessions/llm, present in
  any agent-running profile.
- Plugins with unmet `inject` lists stay dormant instead of failing, so
  install order is free.

## Design decision: isolated bundles, coupled seams

Web3 plugins are **isolated as code, coupled at the seam** — a direct consequence of
how the DeepSeek harness composes.

* **Isolated** — every package is a standalone Cordis plugin (`export const name`,
  `export const inject`, `export function apply(ctx, config)`) with its own
  `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`. There is no aggregate bundle; `dsh plugin add`
  installs one capability at a time and `inject` ordering is free (unmet `inject` stays
  dormant). This is why `dsh-wallet`, `dsh-channel-xmtp`, `dsh-storage-synapse`,
  `dsh-treasury`, and `dsh-wallet-tools` each build via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`) and test
  without the others (`internals.*` seams).

* **Coupled at the seam** — isolation would break without declared contracts:
  `ctx.wallet` (custody), `ctx.tools` (model-facing tools), `ctx.agents`/`ctx.sessions`
  (per-conversation agents), `ctx.synapse`/`ctx.treasury` (storage). Plugins declare
  this with `inject` — e.g. `inject = ['wallet','tools']` in `dsh-wallet-tools` and
  `dsh-storage-synapse` — so they mount only when the seam exists, and call it
  per-operation (`ctx.wallet.address()`, `ctx.wallet.signMessage()`, `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`).

Harness limitations that force this shape:

1. **Singleton tool runtime.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` exposes one scheduler (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare`). If two instances are deduped incorrectly the `Symbol` mismatches and every `tool/call` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`. Bundles therefore depend on `dsh-tools` as a **peer** (`0.2.1-alpha.1`, exact — dsh also rejects a bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not match the running CLI) and `link:` installs must dedupe to one copy.

2. **Wallet custody is per-operation.** Configuration carries only `keyRef`/`wallet` names; `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs inside `signMessage`/`address` and is dropped. Consumers (XMTP identity in `dsh-channel-xmtp`, per-request `x-synapse-*` headers in `dsh-storage-synapse`, `wallet_info` in `dsh-wallet-tools`) see only addresses/signatures. Hard-coding an address in persona (`When asked for address, answer with 0x...`) breaks rotation and wallet-agnostic installs — the correct seam is a tool that resolves `ctx.wallet.address(config.wallet)` live.

3. **Channel is per-conversation, not per-process.** `dsh-channel-xmtp` creates one `ctx.agents` session per XMTP conversation (`SessionId` derived from `conversationId`), handles `conversations.sync()` before `getConversationById`, reconnect/consent sweep, and dedup. The channel owns transport; the agent owns the turn.

Result: add `dsh-wallet` once, then compose any subset. `dsh-wallet-tools` (`wallet_info` tool, `presentCall: {kind:'read'}`) makes the EVM address model-reachable without persona shortcuts; `dsh-channel-xmtp` makes it XMTP-reachable; `dsh-storage-synapse` makes it storage-reachable — all through `ctx.wallet`, none by sharing key material.

## Custody model (the through-line)

Haven's rule — *the private key never leaves its layer; everything else
requests signatures* — maps to one dsh pattern used everywhere here:

1. Configuration carries **names and credential references** (`keyRef`,
   `dbEncryptionKeyRef`). A pasted raw key fails loud at plugin load because
   key material cannot syntactically be a `CredentialRef`.
2. Secrets exist only **inside one operation**: `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs
   per call, the provider signs, every reference is dropped. Rotation reaches
   the very next operation without restart.
3. Consumers (XMTP signer, Synapse requests, future channels) see only
   **addresses and signatures** through `ctx.wallet`.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install       # workspace of five packages
pnpm vitest        # specs live in <package>/tests/**
```

Each package builds self-contained via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`), so git or
path installs work without monorepo context. Money figures are integer µUSD
(USD × 1e6) throughout, matching haven-core.

# dsh-channel-xmtp

XMTP channel for DeepSeek Harness: direct agent↔user messaging over the XMTP
network, ported from Haven's `XmtpChannel` (haven-adapters).

Inbound XMTP text reaches a dsh agent; assistant output is sent back to the
same conversation — both replies to inbound and output of turns the channel
did not start (background-job completion wakes, subagent returns,
schedules). Identity is an Ethereum EOA signed through `dsh-wallet` — this
channel never holds key material.

## Transport model

The channel is a session **observer** (the `dsh-acp` bridge pattern), not a
turn caller:

- **Inbound only enqueues.** `agent.followup` (or `agent.steer` with
  `busyInbound: steer`), never awaiting a turn. An inbound that arrives
  while the agent is mid-turn gets one busy ack per running interval and
  runs as its own turn afterwards.
- **One outbound path for every turn.** Committed session events drive a
  per-conversation send tail that reads forward from a persisted cursor.
  Turns an inbound started (correlated through `agent/inbox/claimed`) are
  `reply` sends; every other turn is `proactive`. A turn with no assistant
  output sends nothing.
- **Exactly-once across restarts** with `outboxPath`: the inbound outbox
  stops redelivered messages re-entering the agent; the outbound cursor
  makes a restart send committed-but-unsent output and never re-send.

Pair it with `tool-jobs.maxConsecutiveWakes` in the profile so a
self-waking job chain cannot spam the chat.

## Concept transfer

| Haven `XmtpChannel` | Here |
| --- | --- |
| `walletAddress` + `signMessage` callback config | the `ctx.wallet` seam: each XMTP signature runs dsh-wallet's resolve → load → sign → drop pipeline |
| `InboundMessage` → MessageBus → AgentLoop session per `sessionKey(channel, chatId)` | one dsh agent per conversation (`ctx.agents.create`, session id `<channelName>-<conversationId>`), inbound via `agent.followup`, output via a `session/event` observer → `conversation.sendText` |
| Disconnected/Connecting/Connected/Reconnecting machine | reconnect loop with the same policy (attempt cap 10, delay 5000ms), reported as `xmtp/status` events |
| `dbEncryptionKey` (raw hex in config) | `dbEncryptionKeyRef` — a `ctx.credentials` reference resolved at each connect |
| `setActiveGroupId()` runtime setter | `activeConversationId` config |
| text-only / own-message / dedup filters, consent auto-allow sweep (15s), dedup cap 5000 → prune to half | preserved verbatim |

Not ported: the installation-limit auto-revocation recovery (deep SDK surface;
revoke stale installations with XMTP tooling if `Client.create` reports the
limit).

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-wallet /path/to/dsh-wallet-ethereum /path/to/dsh-channel-xmtp @xmtp/node-sdk
```

All bundles are independent; each inserts only its own row. `@xmtp/node-sdk`
is an optional peer — the package loads, mounts, and tests without it (lazy
import with an actionable error; tests substitute `internals.sdk`). The
channel requires the agent stack (agents/sessions/llm) present in any
agent-running profile.

## Configuration

```yaml
- id: channel-xmtp
  name: 'dsh-channel-xmtp'
  config:
    wallet: agent              # dsh-wallet entry (EVM — XMTP identity is an Ethereum EOA)
    env: production            # production | dev | local
    channelName: xmtp          # session-id prefix; distinguishes parallel mounts
    # dbPath: /var/lib/dsh/xmtp.db3
    # dbEncryptionKeyRef: XMTP_DB_KEY   # credential REFERENCE, never a key value
    # activeConversationId: <id>        # restrict to one conversation
    # maxReconnectAttempts: 10
    # reconnectDelayMs: 5000
    # outboxPath: /var/lib/dsh/xmtp-outbox.json  # inbound outbox + outbound cursors
    # replyMode: turn          # turn: one reply per turn | message: every assistant message live
    # busyInbound: queue       # queue: own turn after the running one | steer: joins the running turn
    # busyAck: "Still working on the previous request — I'll get to this next."  # '' disables

```

## Events

- `xmtp/inbound` `{ messageId, conversationId, senderInboxId, sentAtMs }` —
  one accepted inbound message (post-filter, pre-agent). Never carries content.
- `xmtp/outbound` `{ conversationId, kind, turn?, inboundMessageId? }` — one
  successful send; `kind` is `reply`, `proactive`, or `ack`. Never carries content.
- `xmtp/status` `{ status, reason }` — connection lifecycle

## Custody

The signer's `signMessage` is one `ctx.wallet.signMessage` operation per XMTP
signature request: the wallet credential resolves inside that call and is
dropped on return. Configuration carries wallet *names* and credential
*references* only.

without them (lazy imports with actionable errors; tests substitute

  `dsh-web-app`; absent in `dsh-base`). The treasury patch does NOT insert
  them — a row id inserted by two layers mounts the plugin twice.
- **Agent stack** (`dsh-channel-xmtp` only): agents/sessions/llm, present in
  any agent-running profile.
- Plugins with unmet `inject` lists stay dormant instead of failing, so
  install order is free.

## Design decision: isolated bundles, coupled seams

Web3 plugins are **isolated as code, coupled at the seam** — a direct consequence of
how the DeepSeek harness composes.

* **Isolated** — every package is a standalone Cordis plugin (`export const name`,
  `export const inject`, `export function apply(ctx, config)`) with its own
  `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`. There is no aggregate bundle; `dsh plugin add`
  installs one capability at a time and `inject` ordering is free (unmet `inject` stays
  dormant). This is why `dsh-wallet`, `dsh-channel-xmtp`, `dsh-storage-synapse`,
  `dsh-treasury`, and `dsh-wallet-tools` each build via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`) and test
  without the others (`internals.*` seams).

* **Coupled at the seam** — isolation would break without declared contracts:
  `ctx.wallet` (custody), `ctx.tools` (model-facing tools), `ctx.agents`/`ctx.sessions`
  (per-conversation agents), `ctx.synapse`/`ctx.treasury` (storage). Plugins declare
  this with `inject` — e.g. `inject = ['wallet','tools']` in `dsh-wallet-tools` and
  `dsh-storage-synapse` — so they mount only when the seam exists, and call it
  per-operation (`ctx.wallet.address()`, `ctx.wallet.signMessage()`, `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`).

Harness limitations that force this shape:

1. **Singleton tool runtime.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` exposes one scheduler (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare`). If two instances are deduped incorrectly the `Symbol` mismatches and every `tool/call` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`. Bundles therefore depend on `dsh-tools` as a **peer** (`0.2.1-alpha.1`, exact — dsh also rejects a bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not match the running CLI) and `link:` installs must dedupe to one copy.

2. **Wallet custody is per-operation.** Configuration carries only `keyRef`/`wallet` names; `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs inside `signMessage`/`address` and is dropped. Consumers (XMTP identity in `dsh-channel-xmtp`, per-request `x-synapse-*` headers in `dsh-storage-synapse`, `wallet_info` in `dsh-wallet-tools`) see only addresses/signatures. Hard-coding an address in persona (`When asked for address, answer with 0x...`) breaks rotation and wallet-agnostic installs — the correct seam is a tool that resolves `ctx.wallet.address(config.wallet)` live.

3. **Channel is per-conversation, not per-process.** `dsh-channel-xmtp` creates one `ctx.agents` session per XMTP conversation (`SessionId` derived from `conversationId`), handles `conversations.sync()` before `getConversationById`, reconnect/consent sweep, and dedup. The channel owns transport; the agent owns the turn.

Result: add `dsh-wallet` once, then compose any subset. `dsh-wallet-tools` (`wallet_info` tool, `presentCall: {kind:'read'}`) makes the EVM address model-reachable without persona shortcuts; `dsh-channel-xmtp` makes it XMTP-reachable; `dsh-storage-synapse` makes it storage-reachable — all through `ctx.wallet`, none by sharing key material.

## Custody model (the through-line)

Haven's rule — *the private key never leaves its layer; everything else
requests signatures* — maps to one dsh pattern used everywhere here:

1. Configuration carries **names and credential references** (`keyRef`,
   `dbEncryptionKeyRef`). A pasted raw key fails loud at plugin load because
   key material cannot syntactically be a `CredentialRef`.
2. Secrets exist only **inside one operation**: `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs
   per call, the provider signs, every reference is dropped. Rotation reaches
   the very next operation without restart.
3. Consumers (XMTP signer, Synapse requests, future channels) see only
   **addresses and signatures** through `ctx.wallet`.

## Development

```sh
pnpm install       # workspace of five packages
pnpm vitest        # specs live in <package>/tests/**
```

path installs work without monorepo context. Money figures are integer µUSD
(USD × 1e6) throughout, matching haven-core.

# dsh-exactly-once

Transparent exactly-once guard for DeepSeek Harness write tools. A
`tools/execute` wrapper (the timeout-policy shape) that needs no model
cooperation and adds no tools or parameters:

- **Redelivery dedup by call identity.** One model call block carries one
  `callId`, so a redelivered call shares `(agent, rootCallId, callId)` and
  a model retry does not. Repeats of an in-flight call attach to it;
  repeats of a settled call replay the recorded result. The body runs
  once.
- **Session-ledger repeat evidence.** Canonical values are deliberately
  omitted from durable events and the harness never re-dispatches a
  settled callId after restart (repair closes dangling calls with
  synthetic errors), so the cold path reads last-outcome evidence from
  the `exactlyOnce` session projection — an incremental fold of
  `tool/call` + `tool/result` events, checkpointed with the session —
  instead of replaying successes. A human `user/message` clears the
  evidence inside the fold, matching the `agent/pre-step` reset.
- **Repeat-after-ambiguous checks.** An exact repeat (same agent, tool,
  canonical arguments) following a non-success consults that tool's
  read-back hook when one is registered through
  `ctx.exactlyOnce.registerCheck`; without a hook the call dispatches
  and the attempt is recorded. Ambiguous errors (timeout, abort,
  unclassified throws) carry an attempt trailer; classified failures
  (`INVALID_ARGS`, treasury denials) pass through byte-identical.

Reads and unlisted tools pass through with zero tracking.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add /path/to/dsh-exactly-once
```

`inject = ['tools', 'sessionProjections']` — the projection registry is
required (present in any agent profile via `dsh-base`). The
`agent/pre-step` repeat reset rides the context event without a service
dependency.

## Config

```yaml
- id: exactly-once
  name: 'dsh-exactly-once'
  config:
    writes: ['synapse_pin', '*_submit', 'erc8004_register']  # *-wildcards; default covers the stack writes
    exempt: []  # exempt wins over writes
```

## Tests


## Design decision: isolated bundles, coupled seams

Web3 plugins are **isolated as code, coupled at the seam** — a direct consequence of
how the DeepSeek harness composes.

* **Isolated** — every package is a standalone Cordis plugin (`export const name`,
  `export const inject`, `export function apply(ctx, config)`) with its own
  `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`. There is no aggregate bundle; `dsh plugin add`
  installs one capability at a time and `inject` ordering is free (unmet `inject` stays
  dormant). This is why `dsh-wallet`, `dsh-channel-xmtp`, `dsh-storage-synapse`,
  `dsh-treasury`, and `dsh-wallet-tools` each build via `prepare` (tsdown → `lib/`) and test
  without the others (`internals.*` seams).

* **Coupled at the seam** — isolation would break without declared contracts:
  `ctx.wallet` (custody), `ctx.tools` (model-facing tools), `ctx.agents`/`ctx.sessions`
  (per-conversation agents), `ctx.synapse`/`ctx.treasury` (storage). Plugins declare
  this with `inject` — e.g. `inject = ['wallet','tools']` in `dsh-wallet-tools` and
  `dsh-storage-synapse` — so they mount only when the seam exists, and call it
  per-operation (`ctx.wallet.address()`, `ctx.wallet.signMessage()`, `ctx.tools.register(defineTool(...))`).

Harness limitations that force this shape:

1. **Singleton tool runtime.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` exposes one scheduler (`ctx.tools[TOOL_RUNTIME_SCHEDULER].prepare`). If two instances are deduped incorrectly the `Symbol` mismatches and every `tool/call` fails with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'prepare')`. Bundles therefore depend on `dsh-tools` as a **peer** (`0.2.1-alpha.1`, exact — dsh also rejects a bundle whose `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peers do not match the running CLI) and `link:` installs must dedupe to one copy.

2. **Wallet custody is per-operation.** Configuration carries only `keyRef`/`wallet` names; `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs inside `signMessage`/`address` and is dropped. Consumers (XMTP identity in `dsh-channel-xmtp`, per-request `x-synapse-*` headers in `dsh-storage-synapse`, `wallet_info` in `dsh-wallet-tools`) see only addresses/signatures. Hard-coding an address in persona (`When asked for address, answer with 0x...`) breaks rotation and wallet-agnostic installs — the correct seam is a tool that resolves `ctx.wallet.address(config.wallet)` live.

3. **Channel is per-conversation, not per-process.** `dsh-channel-xmtp` creates one `ctx.agents` session per XMTP conversation (`SessionId` derived from `conversationId`), handles `conversations.sync()` before `getConversationById`, reconnect/consent sweep, and dedup. The channel owns transport; the agent owns the turn.

Result: add `dsh-wallet` once, then compose any subset. `dsh-wallet-tools` (`wallet_info` tool, `presentCall: {kind:'read'}`) makes the EVM address model-reachable without persona shortcuts; `dsh-channel-xmtp` makes it XMTP-reachable; `dsh-storage-synapse` makes it storage-reachable — all through `ctx.wallet`, none by sharing key material.

## Custody model (the through-line)

Haven's rule — *the private key never leaves its layer; everything else
requests signatures* — maps to one dsh pattern used everywhere here:

1. Configuration carries **names and credential references** (`keyRef`,
   `dbEncryptionKeyRef`). A pasted raw key fails loud at plugin load because
   key material cannot syntactically be a `CredentialRef`.
2. Secrets exist only **inside one operation**: `ctx.credentials.resolve` runs
   per call, the provider signs, every reference is dropped. Rotation reaches
   the very next operation without restart.
3. Consumers (XMTP signer, Synapse requests, future channels) see only

# dsh-haven-aol

Haven-AOL token-gated seal/decrypt/attest for DeepSeek Harness: `ctx.aol` plus six model-facing tools over the `haven-aol` TypeScript SDK and the ICP backend canister (mainnet `gny6k-fqaaa-aaaab-ag3ra-cai`).

> TEMP: `haven-aol` is not on npm despite its README claim, so `package.json`
> uses `file:../../haven-aol/packages/typescript` (requires `npm install` +
> `npm run build` there first for `dist/`). This breaks isolated-bundle
> installs elsewhere — publish `haven-aol` to npm and revert to `"=0.1.0"`.

## Tools

| Tool | Kind | Versions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aol_gate_info` | read | v1/v3/v4 | Pure metadata parse. v4 includes Bond-pin pre-check. |
| `aol_epoch` | read | — | Current 30-day epoch + rollover (advisory). |
| `aol_market_cap` | read | v4 | Live cap in whole reserve units (300s canister burst cache). Fails closed client-side on non-Bond oracles. |
| `aol_decrypt` | execute | v1/v3/v4 | Full gated decrypt; dispatches on metadata version. Keys never leave the call. |
| `aol_seal` | execute | v1/v3/v4 | Harness-native encrypt: AES-GCM key (shared per epoch bucket for v3, fresh per seal for v1/v4, fresh IV always) + IBE wrap under the canister-fetched DPK. No wallet, no signature. |
| `aol_attest_holding` | execute | — | Canister-signed holding attestation (`payload.attn`, haven-cli single shape bound to the record `sha256_ct`). One signature + one canister call per record; denials surface as tool errors. |

Gate denials (`InsufficientBalance`, `MarketCapNotReached {required, actual}` in whole reserve units, `InvalidSignature`, `InvalidEpoch`, `InvalidOracle`) surface as tool errors the model can report verbatim.

## Sourcing rules

- Pure protocol (derivation preimages, epoch math, metadata build/parse, EIP-712 typed-data builders) is imported from the `haven-aol` SDK verbatim — fixture-pinned across Motoko/Python/TS, never re-derived here.
- v1 canister calls use the SDK's own `canister.ts` wrappers.
- v3/v4 canister calls (`requestDecryptionKeyV3/V4`, `getMarketCap`) are vendored in `src/aol.ts` following the SDK's IDL-factory pattern; record shapes copied from `src/backend/backend.did`. Upstream them to the SDK when convenient.

## The EIP-712 signing spike (resolved via raw-key provider)

The EIP-712 gate signature is the only signing operation. `ctx.wallet.signMessage` is **EIP-191** (personal prefix); the canister verifies `ecrecover` over the **raw EIP-712 digest** (`\x19\x01‖domain‖structHash`). A personal-prefixed signature is rejected with `#InvalidSignature`, and OWS exposes no `signDigest`/`signTypedData` through its Node wrapper (see `spike-ows-eip712.mjs`).

Resolution: skip OWS for the signing wallet — `dsh-wallet-ethereum` with `provider: raw` signs the digest raw via `ctx.wallet.signDigest`, which this plugin already prefers (`runtimeForCall`). No code changes were needed here:

```yaml
- id: wallet
  config:
    wallets:
      agent: { chain: evm, wallet: agent, keyRef: PRIVATE_KEY }
- id: wallet-ethereum
  config: { chains: [evm], provider: raw }
- id: haven-aol
  config:
    wallet: agent
    canisterId: gny6k-fqaaa-aaaab-ag3ra-cai
    icpHost: https://icp-api.io
    fetchRootKey: false
```

Without a wired `signDigest` (default OWS path), the `signGate` seam stays **unset and every gated call throws `AolSigningError`** — fail-loud, no silently-invalid signature ever produced. Reads (`aol_gate_info`, `aol_epoch`) and client-side `aol_market_cap` Bond-pin rejection work without any signer.

## Config

```yaml
- id: haven-aol
  config:
    wallet: agent
    canisterId: gny6k-fqaaa-aaaab-ag3ra-cai
    icpHost: https://icp-api.io
    fetchRootKey: false   # local replica only — never mainnet
    keyStorePath: /data/haven-aol/keys.json  # optional; unset = memory-only
```

`inject = ['wallet', 'tools']`. `ctx.synapse` is best-effort via `ctx.get()` — `aol_decrypt {cid}` needs `dsh-storage-synapse` mounted, otherwise pass `path`.

## Deferred (deliberately absent)

- `attestHolding` — no wrapper exists in any SDK yet (TS, Python, or here).

Sealing (`aol_seal`) is harness-native: v3/v4 metadata builders and derivation inputs stay SDK-verbatim, the v1 builder is ported from Python `core.py`, file bytes ship in haven-cli's framed chunk layout (`[12-byte base IV][u32LE index][u32LE length][ciphertext+tag]*`, 1 MiB chunks — players refuse unframed payloads over 32 MiB), and the IBE wrap runs against `@icp-sdk/vetkeys` under the **canister-fetched** verification key. Seal here, upload the sealed bytes plus `gateMetadataJson` via the storage tools. Decrypt dispatches on framing, so pre-framing legacy rows stay open.

## Key reuse (epoch buckets)

Upstream Bugs 4–6 fixed in the port: v3 is one key per epoch, not one per file.

- **Seal side** (`EpochAesKeyCache`): one AES key + wrapped blob per `(chain, token, threshold, epoch)` bucket. Every file sealed in the epoch carries the same `encryptedAesKey`; `keySha256` is the bucket commitment. v1 (per-file) and v4 (per-rung — sharing across rungs would let one unlock open later files) still mint per seal. IVs are fresh per seal in all versions, so every seal's bytes stay unique.
- **Decrypt side** (`VetKeyCache`): one signed canister round-trip per bucket, then local unwraps for every file in it. Lookups key off the derivation input from the gate metadata epoch — never the wall clock.
- **Custody**: both caches are memory-first with an optional durable store. The keys are tiny (32-byte AES, 48-byte vetKeys) and append-only, so a configured `keyStorePath` (e.g. `/data/haven-aol/keys.json`) keeps them across restarts in versioned JSON (0600, atomic tmp+rename, merge-on-save across runtimes — the xmtp outbox convention); unset keeps memory-only. Either way there is deliberately no revocation within an epoch (a member who held a bucket key could have saved the unwrapped file keys anyway). Gate denials are never cached.
