# dsh-lead-agent-only-leads

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DeepSeek Harness bundle that adds a **Lead agent only leads** preset: a Team Lead
that hands every job to teammates and stays available to the user. By default it
cannot run shell commands, cannot read or search the workspace, cannot view
images, cannot write files, and cannot wait for a teammate to finish — but it keeps
every tool it needs to start a teammate, steer it, present the result, and answer:

| | Standard Lead | Lead agent only leads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell (`bash`), file writes (`write`, `edit`) | yes | **no** |
| Reading and search (`read`, `read_image`, `glob`, `grep`) | yes | **no** |
| Jobs, scheduling, web, `subagent_fork`, workflow | yes | **no** |
| `ask_user_question`, `todo_write` | yes | yes |
| Plan mode (`exit_plan_mode`) | yes | yes — the tool stays enabled; the contract neither mentions nor encourages planning |
| `present` (file and image cards) | yes | yes |
| `subagent` (starts a teammate), `send_message`, `list_agents`, `interrupt_agent`, task board | yes | yes |
| `wait_agent` | yes | listed; **refused** by default |
| `subagent_fork`, `list_subagent_models` | yes | **hidden** by default |
| Teammates | standard | **standard** |

In the current DSH the Team tools and the delegation tool are ordinary **global**
tools: the base bundle mounts `tool-agent-team` and `tool-subagent-control` in the
Host composition, and a teammate is started with `subagent` — `spawn_teammate` no
longer exists. `tools.restrict()` reaches every one of them, so a plain keep list
would hide the Lead's whole coordination surface. The catalog therefore treats
them as `guard` rows: `constrain()` always names every guard row this scope
mounts in the allow list, so each stays on the Lead's list, and a row that is OFF
is **refused at execution** by the guard instead of disappearing. `wait_agent` is
an OFF-by-default guard row, so it stays listed and its refusal names the
replacement (`send_message` / ending the turn); `subagent` is an ON-by-default
guard row, because handing work out is the Lead's entire job.

The Lead's **prompt contract is generated from the resolved policy**, so its
refusal sentence names only the tools actually denied, its shell, writer, and
reading claims follow the resolved allow list, and its closing claim sentence
names the Lead's **actual preset tools** — derived from that same allow list, with
the Team tools and the delegation tool kept as a generic phrase — so the text
cannot go stale when the catalog changes. It never contradicts the permissions
the Lead really has. `exit_plan_mode` stays an enabled tool — making a plan is
allowed — but the contract never mentions plan mode or planning; it only names
the tool inside the resolved list. `subagent_fork` and `list_subagent_models`
stay ordinary `whitelist` rows hidden by default, and `list_subagent_models` is
registered only when a preset mounts the delegation tool with
`modelDiscovery: true`, so a profile whose delegation row omits it has no such
tool.

Teammates are ordinary agents: they may block, they may wait on each other, and
they do the writing. The restriction and the guard apply to the Lead's own Agent
scope only, so nothing else in the profile changes.

## Install

The bundle is a normal workspace plugin. Point the installer at the directory:

```
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-lead-agent-only-leads" })
```

That registers the bundle in the profile, links the package, and appends its
patch. Restart the Host so the new patch is loaded, then pick **Lead agent only
leads** when starting a session in the Web UI.

**Upgrading an installed profile.** The Web editor writes a full
`preset-lead-agent-only-leads` row (its `config.plugins` list included) into the
profile's own `cordis.patch.yml`, and that user layer overrides the bundle row by
id. A row saved under an earlier bundle revision keeps the retired
`tool-subagent-list-agents` row and the old `modelSelectionSettings` config, so
delete that row from the profile patch (or re-save the preset in the Web editor)
after upgrading. The bundle patch itself already carries the current `standard`
rows and configs.

Beyond a local checkout, the bundle travels by tarball or Git: `npm pack` in this directory
produces a tarball that installs by absolute path (or an `https:` URL), and a clone installs by Git with a
subdirectory selector, because this repository has no root `package.json`. Only the path/`link:` route is
registry-free, because the Host supplies the dependency; a tarball or Git install also resolves its one
declared dependency, `@deepseek-ai/schemastery@3.19.0`, from the registry, so it needs a reachable
registry, or that dependency already present on the host:

```sh
npm pack    # -> dsh-<name>-<version>.tgz (local only; nothing is published)
```

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/dsh-<name>-<version>.tgz" })
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "git+https://github.com/jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins.git#<commit>&path:/dsh-<name>" })
```

Nothing here is published to an npm registry.

## Use

Start a new session and choose the `Lead agent only leads` preset (the composer's preset
seat lists it as *Lead agent only leads*). The shared task board exists only while the root
Session has Team mode on, so the plugin turns it on when it constrains a Lead — the same
selection as **Use Agent Teams** in the model and reasoning menu. Switch it off mid-session
and that Lead keeps the board off until the plugin constrains it again (a new session, or a
re-preset). The delegation, messaging, and `list_agents` controls work either way. The Lead
will delegate: give it a task, and it briefs a teammate and comes straight back to
you. Teammate reports arrive as new turns, so you can keep talking while work is in
flight.

Because the Lead cannot read, search, or list the repository, it may not know a
brief's exact files or checks up front. Its contract therefore folds reconnaissance
into the brief bullet: to know those files or checks it **may create a reconnaissance
task** — one teammate on a **read-only task**, recorded on the shared board like any
other task, that states the question and asks for the facts (where the code lives,
which files a change touches, how the result should be verified). The Lead then ends
its turn: the report arrives as its next turn, and it splits and briefs the real work
from what that report establishes. Nothing blocks: the Lead never waits on the scout.

## How a Lead is identified

Two live facts decide whether an Agent gets the contract: the preset its session
runs **right now**, and whether it is a Team Lead. The preset is read from the Host's
live preset projection for the session (`presetForSession`), not from the
session's creation header. The header records what the session was created under
and is never re-stamped, so a session created as `standard` and later resumed or
re-presetted under **Lead agent only leads** still carries `standard` in its
header for its whole life even though every turn runs under the Lead
composition. Trusting that header is what once let such a Lead run unrestricted
for an entire session; restarting DSH did not heal it, it merely started a
different session whose header named the Lead preset.

Those lookups rely on Host services that can start after this plugin does, so the
plugin resolves them lazily, re-checks every Agent when they appear, and
re-reconciles whenever a session switches preset. While the authoritative preset
cannot be read it fails closed rather than guessing: "cannot tell yet" is never
treated as "not this preset", a Lead that is already constrained is not released
because a lookup was temporarily unavailable, and an Agent that could be the
Lead is kept constrained and re-checked instead of being left unrestricted. If
the preset then turns out to be another one, that Agent is released. The Team side asks
the roster when the mounted Team service exposes a membership probe; the current
Agent Teams service does not, so the plugin falls back to the root Session — the
Lead by construction, because every teammate is its descendant. That hold
applies only where the composition could still provide the preset: a Host that
never mounts the preset registry (the headless bundle) has no preset to enforce,
so its Agents are left alone rather than held restricted, while the Web profile,
which does mount it, keeps the first-turn guarantee. Once the decision lands, the
next step's tool list reflects it — no Host restart needed. (A step already in
flight finishes first.)

## Settings page

The bundle ships a **Lead agent only leads** page under Settings (section id
`lead-agent-only-leads-tools`), driven by the Host's `configForms` namespace for the
`lead-agent-only-leads` row. It lists the whole tool universe grouped by mechanism, with a
per-row description and its default, and writes one dictionary key per toggle:

- **Whitelist** (35) — preset/global-layer tools; ON keeps the tool, OFF hides
  it. Defaults ON: `ask_user_question`, `todo_write`, `exit_plan_mode`,
  `present`; every other row — the four reading tools (`read`, `read_image`,
  `glob`, `grep`) included — defaults OFF.
- **Guard** (9) — the delegation tool and the eight Team tools. They stay on the
  Lead's list, and OFF refuses them through the guard instead of hiding them.
  Defaults ON: `subagent` and the seven steered Team controls. Defaults OFF:
  `wait_agent`.
- **No effect** (6) — `/goal`, `/plan`, `/compact` (commands, not tools),
  `plugin_manager`, `plugin_market` (not mounted in this profile), and
  `structured_output` (only appears inside a delegated child). Shown disabled,
  with a *not toggleable* badge where the switch would be. These rows no longer
  render a `default on/off` line: that label was inert, because the plugin
  ignores `none` entries entirely, so only togglable rows show their default.

The page **leads with the Lead contract prompt the current selection produces**, shown as a
quote above the groups: it is the text `constrain()` hands the Lead's system prompt, so the
page can be read as "this is what the Lead will be told". `client.js` mirrors the host's
`leadContract()` and the same keep/deny resolution (catalog toggles, or a legacy
`leadTools`/`denyTools` array wholesale — the quote follows that override too, because the
toggles stop driving policy then), and `verify.mjs` compares the two builders byte for byte for
the catalog default, an `ask_user_question`-off selection, a `bash`-on selection, a `grep`-only
selection (which pins the `readersHidden` branch), and a legacy
override. Honest limit: the client derives the three capability claims and the named tool list
from this page's catalog plus the toggles and cannot read the host's live `reachable` scope, so
a tool the profile does not mount still appears in the preview, where the live prompt drops it.
The quote updates with every toggle, because it is computed from the same live snapshot the rows
render.

Toggles are **volatile**: an edit is committed into the running config without
remounting the plugin, so it applies to **Leads constrained afterwards**; a Lead
that is already constrained keeps the surface it was constrained with. The first
install needs one Host restart for the client half to be discovered; later
`client.js` edits hot-reload.

The bundle ships **no `node_modules`**. `index.js` resolves the config-schema
library (`@deepseek-ai/schemastery`) from the Host that loaded it: a normal
import first (a marketplace install that fetched dependencies), then the running
process entry, then `$DSH_HARNESS_CHECKOUT` through the workspace's hoisted store.
Offline and restart-safe. If none resolves, the plugin still enforces the catalog
defaults; only the settings page is absent, because no config namespace exists.

Turning every whitelist toggle off hides every preset tool: the restriction still
runs and the Lead keeps exactly the guard rows (its delegation and Team tools) —
never the whole surface. A toggle list whose tools are not mounted in this scope
(everything off except `pwsh`, say, on Linux) behaves the same way, and the
warning names the tools that are not mounted. The only path that leaves the
preset surface intact is an explicit legacy `leadTools` row config whose names
are all absent from the scope. An explicitly configured legacy
`leadTools`/`denyTools` array still wins wholesale over the catalog for its own
list — a legacy `leadTools` list also drops the always-kept guard rows, so write
one only if you mean it — and the page shows a notice while one is set.

## Files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Two host rows: the plugin, and the preset declaration. |
| `index.js` | The plugin: per-Agent restriction, denial guard, prompt contract, catalog, `Config`. |
| `client.js` | Client half: the `Lead agent only leads` settings page and the mirrored `LEAD_TOOL_CATALOG`. |
| `locale/*.json` | Marketplace metadata (title/description). |
| `verify.mjs` | Offline check suite — `node verify.mjs`. |
| `CONTRACT.md` | Frozen interface, invariants, non-goals. |
| `package.json` | Bundle manifest (`dsh.bundle.patch`, `dsh.client`). |

## Configure

Row config, in the profile patch. The settings page writes `tools`; these keys
are the manual equivalent:

```yaml
- id: lead-agent-only-leads
  config:
    preset: lead-agent-only-leads     # which preset gets the contract
    tools:                            # per-tool toggles; absent key = catalog default
      bash: true
    leadTools: [ask_user_question, todo_write]   # legacy: explicit keep list, wins wholesale
    denyTools: []                     # legacy: explicit deny list; [] removes the guard
```

`tools` and the two legacy keys are volatile, so an edit reaches Leads created
afterwards without a plugin remount. Every `leadTools` name the scope cannot
restrict is pruned rather than fatal; an explicit empty `leadTools` keeps
**nothing** (the "all off" intent), and `denyTools: []` removes the guard.

## Verify

```
node verify.mjs
```

Fifty-nine checks on a checkout whose `js-yaml` is reachable: the pure helpers,
the `Config` schema shape, the catalog and its defaults (the reading tools off,
`exit_plan_mode` and `present` on, in catalog order), the config-aware contract text
(the frozen no-argument bytes and hash, the no-plan-mode invariant, the merged
reconnaissance bullet asserted byte for byte, the resolved-tool-list sentence and its
1/2/many/empty renderings, an empty deny list, a `subagent`-only deny, the gated
shell/writer/reading claims, and the text the plugin
actually registers under a delegation opt-in override shape), the plugin's
behaviour against a model of the inherited surface (the preset rows plus the base
bundle's global Team rows, including a scope that does not mount `exit_plan_mode`), the
toggle→keep/deny mapping including the all-off and unknown-names cases, the
classification contract (the creation header never decides, the Session
projection does, a registry that activates after apply re-reconciles and releases
a genuine non-Lead, the selection payload and `session/event` both re-reconcile,
a selection observed before the Agent is published applies at creation and its
memory is bounded — consumed once, evicted oldest-first past 64 entries, dropped
on disposal — with a one-shot unresolved warning re-armed by a resolved decision,
and fail-closed follows composition capability so a registry-less Host is not
over-restricted), a
deep-parse of the patch that also proves this preset mounts exactly the shipped
`standard` rows and configs, and a real load of `client.js` through a stubbed
module loader
that deep-compares the host and client catalogs. The suite needs no live Host; it
reads the harness checkout for `js-yaml` and `standard.patch.yml`, and the one
aggregate deep-parse check is skipped when the checkout is unreachable.

## Why it is built this way

The preset deliberately duplicates the `standard` plugin list instead of being
narrow. A teammate inherits the Lead's preset generation, so a narrow preset
would make the teammates non-standard too; the reduction has to happen per Agent
scope at runtime. `CONTRACT.md` explains the seam, what it can and cannot do, and
why the catalog refuses `wait_agent` with a guard while keeping `subagent` and
`list_subagent_models` as ordinary whitelist rows hidden by the restriction.

# deepseek-harness-plugins

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Five standalone DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin bundles.
Each one installs into a DSH host as a profile bundle, carries its own English and Simplified Chinese
README, and ships a hermetic verification suite that runs without a live Host.

| Bundle | What it does | Where it appears | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dsh-backend-restart` | Adds a **Restart backend** action: asks the Host to replace itself over the `/backend-restart` RPC channel, then reloads the page once the successor answers. | Settings → **General**, in a row above the version line | [English](dsh-backend-restart/README.md) · [中文](dsh-backend-restart/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-compaction-tuner` | One page that owns the full eleven-key `compaction-basic` policy and pushes the tune into every agent preset in the active profile. | Settings → **Compaction tuner** (last nav row) | [English](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.md) · [中文](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` | Adds the **Lead agent only leads** preset — a Team Lead that delegates every job and never waits on a teammate — plus the host plugin that enforces the tool restrictions. | Session preset picker; Settings → **Lead agent only leads** for the tool toggles | [English](dsh-lead-agent-only-leads/README.md) · [中文](dsh-lead-agent-only-leads/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-llm-api-call-tuning` | One Settings page that tunes the model-request retry policy of every active provider route — retry mode, max retries, backoff delays, jitter, and retryable failure codes — plus the per-route provider timeouts (stream idle, SDK request, Files API) and the two process-wide HTTP fetch timeouts shared by every provider, web search, and HTTP MCP server. | Settings → **LLM API call tuning** (last nav row) | [English](dsh-llm-api-call-tuning/README.md) · [中文](dsh-llm-api-call-tuning/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-use-repo-tmp` | Prompt-only guidance that sends scratch files to `<workspace>/tmp` instead of `/tmp`, as one static system-prompt section plus a runtime-context line. | No UI | [English](dsh-use-repo-tmp/README.md) · [中文](dsh-use-repo-tmp/README.zh.md) |

## Requirements

- **DSH `^0.2.2-rc.3`** — declared as `engines.dsh` in every manifest, so a DSH host outside that range
  refuses the install.
- These packages declare no separate Node.js version. Their verification scripts are plain ESM and run
  with the `node` binary you already use for DSH.

## Installation

A bundle is an npm package whose `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`; installing it adds that patch
layer to the active DSH profile. Three routes work today. Only the path/`link:` route is registry-free: a
tarball or Git install of `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` also resolves its one declared dependency,
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery@3.19.0`, from the registry, so that route needs a reachable registry, or that
dependency already present on the host.

### From a local checkout (absolute path)

From this repository's root, with the installed DSH CLI on `PATH`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:"$PWD/dsh-backend-restart"
```

From a DSH source checkout instead, run its own script with an absolute bundle path:
`pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add link:/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-backend-restart`.

Or from a running GUI session, with the `plugin_manager` tool:

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-backend-restart" })
```

The installer links the package into the profile and records the bundle row; the plugin loads on the next
full page load.

### From a tarball

`npm pack` inside a bundle directory produces a local tarball that installs by absolute path (or by an
`https:` URL):

```sh
cd dsh-backend-restart
npm pack    # -> dsh-backend-restart-0.2.2-rc.3.tgz
```

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/dsh-backend-restart-0.2.2-rc.3.tgz" })
```

### From Git (subdirectory selector)

There is no root `package.json`, so a bare `github:jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins` install cannot
resolve a package. Address one bundle with a `path:` selector instead:

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "git+https://github.com/jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins.git#<commit>&path:/dsh-backend-restart" })
```

Pin a commit for `<commit>`; the same spec form works for the other four bundles with their own
`path:/dsh-<name>`.

## Nothing is published to npm

These bundles are **not published**: no version of these packages exists on npm. Their manifests set
`"private": false` and carry publish metadata, so a release is possible later, but nothing has been
published to any registry.

## Notes

- `dsh-compaction-tuner` writes its tune into the profile's preset rows on the first boot; uninstalling it
  does not revert that. See *Install behaviour change* in its [README](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.md).
- The preset added by `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` is identified from the preset a session currently runs,
  not from its creation header: a session switched or resumed under **Lead agent only leads** is
  constrained without a restart. Installing the bundle itself still needs one Host restart to load its
  patch.

## Verification

Each bundle ships a self-contained `verify.mjs`; no network, no server, and no live Host. Set
`DSH_HARNESS_CHECKOUT` to a DSH source checkout — it is required for a green run: the compaction tuner
fails loudly without it, and the other suites resolve the checkout's libraries through it.

```sh
export DSH_HARNESS_CHECKOUT=/path/to/deepseek-harness

node dsh-backend-restart/verify.mjs          # 13 checks passed
node dsh-compaction-tuner/verify.mjs         # 99 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (99 checks)
node dsh-lead-agent-only-leads/verify.mjs    # 59/59 checks passed
node dsh-llm-api-call-tuning/verify.mjs      # 164 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (164 checks)
node dsh-use-repo-tmp/verify.mjs             # 14 checks passed
```

# `dsh-llm-api-call-tuning`

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A DSH plugin that puts **one** Settings page behind the model-request retry policy of **every active
model provider route**. DSH resolves one retry policy per route — retry mode, max retries, retryable
failure codes, and a bounded exponential backoff with jitter (`packages/llm/llm/src/retry-policy.ts`) —
but each provider owns its own copy (`llm-deepseek` and `llm-deepseek-account` under `retryPolicy`,
`llm-pi-ai` under `providers.<id>.retryPolicy`) and DSH has no global knob, CLI flag, environment
variable, or GUI-core page for them. Tuning them by hand means editing every provider row and keeping
five numbers in sync.

The page is organised in **two tiers**:

- **Global settings card (first)** — one card holding every global knob in two labeled sub-groups:
  - **Retries** — the six retry values stored once in this plugin's own settings namespace
    (`llm-api-call-tuning`) as a **preset**. Saving them changes **no provider**.
  - **Fetch timeouts** — the two process-wide HTTP timers `headersTimeoutMs` and `bodyTimeoutMs`, applied
    by the Host to the fetch dispatcher that every provider route, web search, and HTTP MCP server shares.
    Both are `unset` by default, so a fresh install changes no behavior; `0` explicitly disables a timer
    and a positive integer sets it in milliseconds.
  One **Save global settings** writes the six retry leaves and the two fetch leaves in a single write;
  **Reset to system defaults** clears only the two fetch timers.
- **Per-route overrides (below)** — one route section with a native **route picker** above the list, then
  **one merged card per DEVIATING provider route**, carrying that route's retry policy and its
  application-layer timeouts as two sub-groups (**Retry policy** / **Timeouts**). Retry and timeout are
  no longer separate sections. A route appears when its **effective stored retry policy differs in at
  least one leaf** from the global retry values, or when the route **stores any timeout leaf
  explicitly**; an entry stored equal to the global values is hidden. A route card writes leaf-path
  operations **directly into that provider's own settings namespace**, and nothing is written until you
  edit a field.

**The extended retry codes are opt-in and off by default.** In `normal` mode the code checklist offers
**ten** failure codes, but exactly the **five upstream codes** are selected by default, on a fresh
install and for every stored policy that does not already name an extra: `EMPTY_RESPONSE`,
`RATE_LIMIT`, `SERVER`, `TIMEOUT`, `TRANSPORT`. The five extras — `STREAM_CLOSED`,
`MALFORMED_RESPONSE`, `PI_AI_ERROR`, `HTTP_408`, `HTTP_409` — change nothing until you tick one and
save, so upgrading shows five additional **unchecked** checkboxes and nothing else changes. Saving an
untouched or default route writes **no `retryableCodes` change at all**: route saves now write only the
leaves you actually touched. The global card's preset (and therefore **Apply defaults to all** when you
have not ticked an extra there) remains exactly the five.

The listing rule is deliberately asymmetric: retry deviation is **value-based** (compared with the
global retry values), while timeout deviation is **presence-based**, because the global fetch timers are
undici **transport** timers and a route's `streamIdleTimeoutMs` / `timeoutMs` / `filesApiTimeoutMs` are
application-layer **watchdogs** — different knobs, with no global counterpart to compare against. These
are **provider routes, never models**: DSH resolves retry and timeout policy once per route.

The provider routes are authoritative; the global retry values are copied only when you explicitly ask
(**Use defaults** on a route card, or **Apply defaults to all active providers**). The two fetch timers
are a separate, **process-wide** side effect: they are not part of the retry preset and are never copied
onto a provider route. The wire format is frozen in [CONTRACT.md](CONTRACT.md).

## Install

The plugin is a profile bundle, not a workspace package. Install it from the DSH checkout (so the
`pnpm dsh` entry point resolves), pointing the `link:` at the bundle directory — use your own checkout
and plugins-workspace paths:

```sh
cd /abs/path/to/deepseek-harness
plugins=/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add link:"$plugins/dsh-llm-api-call-tuning"
```

Or, from the plugins workspace (the parent of this bundle) with the `dsh` CLI on `PATH`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:"$PWD/dsh-llm-api-call-tuning"
```

In a running GUI session the same step is the `plugin_manager` tool with
`action: "install_bundle"` and the absolute directory path as `target`:

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-llm-api-call-tuning" })
```

`application: "applied"` means the profile changed. Then **reload the page**; a first install may also
need a backend restart before the bundle patch is read. The bundle ships no dependencies (it resolves
the Host's own `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` at load time), and nothing here is published to an npm
registry: installing from this checkout, an absolute path, or `npm pack` is the supported route.

## Use

Open **Settings** (the account menu at the bottom of the sidebar) and choose **LLM API call tuning**,
the last nav row (section order 45). The page renders exactly two tiers:

1. **Global settings** — one card, first, with two labeled sub-groups and one **Save global settings**:
   - **Retries** — one control for each of the six retry fields in the table below. These values are
     stored in `llm-api-call-tuning` and are a **preset**: saving them does not touch a provider.
   - **Fetch timeouts** — the two process-wide HTTP timers, plus **Reset to system defaults**.
   The card also carries **Apply defaults to all active providers**.
2. **Per-route overrides** — a native **route picker** and an **Add** button above the list, then **one
   merged card per deviating route**. A card carries its **Retry policy** and **Timeouts** sub-groups,
   one **Save**, one **Reset to global**, one **Reset**, and **Use defaults** (retry half). Only routes
   that deviate are listed; the picker offers the remaining routes and excludes the ones already
   listed. Picking a route
   materializes its card locally from the effective values and **writes nothing** until you edit a field
   and save. Editing a retry leaf back to its global value (or clearing a timeout) removes that override,
   so the card disappears once the route no longer deviates. An empty list says "No provider route
   deviates from the global settings.", and "Every editable route is already listed." appears when the
   picker has nothing left to offer.

A route is listed when its **effective stored retry policy differs in at least one leaf** from the
global retry values, **or** when the route **stores any timeout leaf** it owns. The two halves are
deliberately asymmetric: the global fetch timers are undici transport timers, while a route's
`streamIdleTimeoutMs` / `timeoutMs` / `filesApiTimeoutMs` are application-layer watchdogs, so there is no
global value to compare a route timeout against — presence is the only meaningful test there. A route
that stores a timeout equal to the package default is therefore still listed.

Routes that are declared but dormant, that declare no settings namespace, or whose namespace this
deployment does not serve are **not listed and not pickable**: without a live config form their deviation
cannot be proven, and writing a timeout leaf would materialize a partial provider profile and could
activate a dormant route.

Outside these two settings tiers the plugin also adds a **retry bar above the composer** for failures the
automatic policy declined ([Manual retry](#manual-retry)); it is a separate host/client feature, not a
third settings page.

The retry field table (same values the Host's `Config` and the upstream retry resolver use) applies to
the global card's **Retries** sub-group and to every route card; the two process-wide fetch fields
follow:

| Field | Meaning | Accepts | Code default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | Retry mode. `normal` retries only the selected codes up to the retry limit; `always` retries **every** model-request failure — including permanent ones such as AUTH, INVALID_REQUEST, or QUOTA — with no retry limit, until success, cancellation, or disposal, and ignores the code list. | `'normal'` or `'always'` | `'normal'` |
| `maxRetries` | Eligible retries after the first request in `normal` mode; `0` disables retries. | integer 0..9007199254740991 | `5` |
| `initialDelayMs` | First locally scheduled retry delay, in milliseconds. | finite and > 0, at most 2147483647; must not exceed maxDelayMs | `500` |
| `maxDelayMs` | Cap on a locally scheduled or accepted provider delay, in milliseconds. | finite and > 0, at most 2147483647; must not be below initialDelayMs | `10000` |
| `jitterRatio` | Symmetric random multiplier around each local delay: `0` disables jitter, `1` allows up to double. | number in [0, 1] | `0.1` |
| `retryableCodes` | Failure codes `normal` mode retries. The five upstream codes are selected by default; the five added provider/HTTP codes are opt-in and stay inactive until ticked. | non-empty array of unique codes from the ten offered codes; defaults to the five upstream codes | `'EMPTY_RESPONSE', 'RATE_LIMIT', 'SERVER', 'TIMEOUT', 'TRANSPORT'` |
| `headersTimeoutMs` | Process-wide HTTP response-headers timeout, in milliseconds, applied by the Host to the fetch dispatcher that every provider route, web search, and HTTP MCP server shares. | `unset` (leave the system/DSH default untouched), or integer 0..2147483647; `0` disables the timer | `unset` |
| `bodyTimeoutMs` | Process-wide HTTP response-body (chunk) timeout, in milliseconds, on that same fetch dispatcher. | `unset` (leave the system/DSH default untouched), or integer 0..2147483647; `0` disables the timer | `unset` |

The **Code default** column for the retry rows is the upstream resolution fallback
(`retry-policy.ts:15-25`), also what an unconfigured provider route runs. The bundle seeds nothing, so
the page starts on those values. For the two fetch rows the code default is **`unset`**, not a number:
the schema deliberately has no `.default()`, so a fresh install materializes no timer and the Host's own
dispatcher defaults apply. `unset` means no behavior change; `0` is a real value that disables that one
timer; a positive integer sets it.

### Retryable codes (opt-in extras)

`normal` mode offers ten checkboxes. Five are the upstream code defaults and start selected; the other
five are additions this page offers but never enables on its own:

| Code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `STREAM_CLOSED` | The stream ended before a terminal event — a dropped or truncated connection mid-response. |
| `MALFORMED_RESPONSE` | A garbled or invalid stream frame (for example invalid JSON, or invalid tool arguments). |
| `PI_AI_ERROR` | An `llm-pi-ai` failure the adapter could not classify into a more specific code. |
| `HTTP_408` | The status-shaped fallback the DeepSeek transport produces for HTTP 408. |
| `HTTP_409` | The status-shaped fallback the DeepSeek transport produces for HTTP 409. |

**Opt-in semantics.** An unchecked extra is not part of the policy. The page remembers an extra only
after you tick it and save, and a stored list that already names an extra stays ticked. If a stored list
is empty or contains no code this page recognizes, it falls back to the five defaults — never to the
ten. An untouched list is never rewritten by a route card, so a save cannot silently activate a code.

**Upstream is not limited to five.** The retry schema is
`retryableCodes: z.array(z.union([...RETRY_CODE_CHOICES.map(code => z.const(code)), z.string().min(1)])).min(1)`
(`packages/llm/llm/src/retry-policy.ts:95-96`): the const branches publish the built-in choices to forms
while the string branch admits any non-empty provider-specific code, and `.min(1)` rejects an empty array;
the resolver additionally rejects empty strings and duplicates (`retry-policy.ts:176-184`) — no layer
checks membership. The executor compares exact code strings
(`packages/llm/llm-retry/src/index.ts:212`). The five-code default is this plugin's own policy, not an
upstream limit; the ten-code list is what this page offers, and a hand-stored code outside it is dropped
from the draft only when the code list is actually rewritten (a route card writes only touched leaves; the
global card's Save always rewrites its six default leaves, so it normalizes the plugin's own preset).

**Never add `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` or `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED`.** In `normal` mode a listed code is
retried **before** the executor delegates to `next()`, so the failure never reaches the handlers that
actually fix those cases — `compaction-basic`
(`packages/compaction/compaction-basic/src/index.ts:213,217`) and `compaction-image-offload`
(`packages/compaction/compaction-image-offload/src/index.ts:27,28`). Retrying them would burn attempts
instead of compacting or offloading; they are deliberately not offered.

### Saving the global card

**Save global settings** validates the six retry fields and the two fetch timers locally first (the retry
rules are in *Saving a route card* below), then writes **one atomic op list at one revision fence**: the
six retry `set` leaves followed by the two fetch leaves, where an empty fetch field emits an `unset` and
a typed value — including `0` — emits a `set`. Nothing is projected onto a provider: the retry values are
a preset, and the fetch leaves are a process-wide side effect. **Reset to system defaults** clears only
the two fetch leaves, so the Host's system defaults apply again; the six retry defaults keep their stored
values.

### Saving a route card

**Save** validates both drafts locally first — a fractional retry limit, a delay of `0` or above
`2147483647`, an initial delay above the maximum, a jitter outside `[0, 1]`, an empty/unknown/duplicate
code list, or a timeout outside blank/`1..2147483647` is refused with a localized message and **no Host
call** — then submits **one atomic write of leaf operations at one revision fence**, carrying that
route's retry leaves and its changed timeout leaves together.

The retry half is written **relative to the global retry values** and **only for the leaves you
actually touched**: an untouched leaf produces no operation at all, a touched leaf whose draft differs
from the global value is `set`, and a touched leaf turned back to the global value is `unset` only when
that global value is the **code default** and the user layer actually stores it (except `mode`, see
below). An `unset` falls back to the provider schema's code defaults, never to this plugin's saved
preset, so matching a **non-default** global value is written as a `set` — which is what keeps **Save**
stable after a **Reset to global**. That is also what keeps the opt-in code list safe: an untouched
`retryableCodes` list is never written, so a default route cannot be given an extra code by pressing
Save. When the retry half's list is non-empty and every op in it is an `unset`, the page collapses it
into the single `unset [...settingsPath, 'retryPolicy']`. `retryPolicy.mode` is exempt from the leaf
`unset` rule: both arms of the provider schema's retry-policy union require `mode`, so a touched mode is
persisted with `set` whenever it is part of a mixed save — including when it reverts to the global
value — and a pure revert (no other dirty retry leaf) emits the single whole-node
`unset [...settingsPath, 'retryPolicy']`. In `normal` mode the touched leaves can be
`retryPolicy.mode`, `retryPolicy.maxRetries`, `retryPolicy.retryableCodes` and the three
`retryPolicy.backoff.*` leaves. In `always` mode the code checklist is **hidden**, the maximum-retries
input stays visible and typable but is **ignored and not validated**, and a save sets `retryPolicy.mode` and
**clears** any stored `retryPolicy.maxRetries` and `retryPolicy.retryableCodes`, because the upstream
`always` shape has no retry limit and no code list. Always mode retries **every** model-request failure
with no cap — permanent ones included (`AUTH`, `INVALID_REQUEST`, `QUOTA`,
`CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED`, `IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED`) — until success, cancellation, or disposal. A whole
`retryPolicy` object is never *set*, so sibling configuration (base URL, credentials reference, models)
is left alone.

The timeout half writes only the leaves whose draft changed: a blank field that was seeded from a stored
value emits its `unset`, a typed value emits its `set`, and an untouched field emits nothing. A picked
card that stores nothing yet has nothing to save (its **Save** stays disabled), and **Save** is also
disabled while either draft is invalid or nothing changed.

**Reset to global** copies the **saved** global retry preset onto the route in one write: all six retry
leaves, at the same leaf paths **Save** uses, carrying the global code list (the saved section, never
the global card's unsaved draft). It then clears this family's timeout overrides, because timeouts have
no per-provider global counterpart — inheriting the package/SDK default **is** their global-effective
state. It covers every retry setting (nothing is hardcoded or skipped) and it writes even on a picked
card that stores no override yet, unlike **Reset**. The provider rows stay the source of truth, so the
global values are written explicitly; a route that ends up equal to the saved preset no longer deviates
and closes.

**Reset** is the inherit-style reset: it removes everything the card stores for the route in one write —
the whole `retryPolicy` plus this family's timeout leaves — so the provider falls back to its own schema
defaults. On a picked card that stores no override yet, **Reset** closes the card locally with **no
write at all**. **Use defaults** copies the validated global retry defaults into the retry draft;
nothing is written until **Save**.

A write is attempted only when the route's form reports `ready`, is not read-only, and carries a numeric
revision; that same read is the revision fence, so the page never sends an unconditional write. A route
that fails the gate stays disabled (and is **skipped** by "Apply defaults to all" instead of written).

If the Host refuses the write, `mutate` resolves `false` — that is **every** Host refusal, including
one caused by a home patch or `--patch` overlay owning the row, because the settings form API does not
surface the reason. The page shows the **generic refusal copy** and re-seeds every field from whatever
the Host reports next; if the refusal was a superseded revision and the recovery read moved it, the
write is retried **once** at the fresh revision. The page keeps a separate "managed elsewhere" copy for
a **direct `RemoteError` carrying `settings/rejected`**, but that classification is defensive only and
is not reachable through the settings form API: a home-patch-owned row shows the generic copy.

**Apply defaults to all active providers** copies the validated global retry defaults into every
editable route (active, with a settings namespace and a live form), one provider at a time, each at its
own freshly read revision. It re-checks each row immediately before its write: a row whose form is still
loading, read-only, or missing a numeric revision is **skipped** (the section-level summary still
reports it as `skipped`). It is **not a transaction**: a provider that refuses keeps its policy, the ones
already written stay written, and the per-row outcome says which is which. It never writes timeout leaves
or the two fetch timers onto a provider: those are per-route and process-wide settings, not the retry
preset.

### Timeouts (route card sub-group)

The **Timeouts** sub-group of each merged route card edits the application-layer timeouts that live in
each **provider's own** namespace, the same cross-namespace write the Retry policy sub-group performs.
Defaults are the upstream package/SDK values; a blank field writes nothing, so the route keeps them.

| Field | Applies to | Namespace / path | Default | Accepts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | every active route | `llm-pi-ai` → `providers.<route>.streamIdleTimeoutMs`; `llm-deepseek` / `llm-deepseek-account` → `streamIdleTimeoutMs` | `300000` ms (5 min) | blank (package default) or integer 1..2147483647; `0` is refused |
| `timeoutMs` | `llm-pi-ai` routes only | `llm-pi-ai` → `providers.<route>.timeoutMs` | unset = SDK default (about `600000` ms) | blank (SDK default) or integer 1..2147483647; `0` is refused |
| `filesApiTimeoutMs` | `llm-deepseek` and `llm-deepseek-account` only | `llm-deepseek` / `llm-deepseek-account` namespace root → `filesApiTimeoutMs` | `20000` ms (20 s) | blank (package default) or integer 1..2147483647; `0` is refused |

Why `0` is refused and there is no off switch: the DeepSeek and stream-idle schemas require a strictly
positive value (the load-time asserts reject `<= 0`), and a zero SDK request timeout would abort every
request immediately. The schemas have no "disabled" state, so the **Unlimited** preset writes the
maximum `2147483647` ms (about 24.8 days) instead — a limit, not an off switch. A direct
`settings.mutate` (or a hand-edited profile patch) can still persist `0`; for the two watchdogs that
fails the provider's load-time assert and the route then fails to resolve, which is exactly what the
page prevents.

Interplay with the other two timeout surfaces: for SSE routes the SDK request timeout bounds the wait
for **response headers**, while `streamIdleTimeoutMs` bounds silence **between** streamed chunks, and the
process-wide fetch `bodyTimeoutMs` bounds the transport between chunks. When the idle window is raised
above the default `600000` ms SDK request timeout, the card warns (non-blocking) if `timeoutMs` is
shorter, or if the fetch body timeout is set below the idle window. Raising only the idle window is not
enough if a shorter SDK or transport deadline still fires.

Diagnosis pointer: an `llm-pi-ai` failure reported as a **stream idle timeout after 300000 ms** is the
default idle watchdog aborting a slow first token (TTFT stall), not a transport failure. Raise
`streamIdleTimeoutMs` on the route card (and match `timeoutMs` and the fetch `bodyTimeoutMs` if they are
shorter) instead of editing the profile patch by hand.

`connectTimeoutMs` is **out of scope**: undici has no per-request connect timeout in versions 6, 7, or 8,
and only a fragile agent rebuild could express one. A proper transport connect limit belongs upstream in
`packages/util/http-proxy/src/install.ts` (the proxy-aware dispatcher install), not in this page.

### Fetch timeouts (process-wide)

The **Fetch timeouts** sub-group of the global card edits the two top-level leaves of this plugin's own
namespace. The tri-state contract is:

- **Empty input = `unset`** — the fresh-install state. Saving an empty field emits
  `{ op: 'unset', path: ['<key>'] }`, so no timer of this plugin's is applied and the Host/system default
  is left untouched. A fresh install changes no behavior.
- **`0` = disabled** — a real write (`{ op: 'set', path: ['<key>'], value: 0 }`). It is visually
  distinct from empty and means "disable this timer", not "unset".
- **Positive integer = custom milliseconds**, at most `2147483647`.

The effect is **process-wide**: the Host wraps the current global undici dispatcher and fills
`headersTimeout`/`bodyTimeout` only on requests that do not set their own value, so every provider
route, web search, and HTTP MCP server in the process shares it. A per-request timeout always wins. The
wrapper is installed lazily, only while at least one of the two values is a number; clearing the last
value restores the dispatcher the Host had (only while that wrapper is still the current dispatcher),
and a later live save re-installs it. This is a **stopgap** on top of an upstream design: it is adapted
from the MIT-licensed `dsh-fetch-timeouts` project (© 2026 Dev Mehra), whose attribution lives in the
repository's [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](../THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md). It is not a DSH-native setting, so a
future DSH release may supersede it.

### Live and persisted semantics

- The save travels the shared settings form API — the same `settings.mutate` path the Models page uses —
  and the settings service persists it into the active profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (the profile's own
  patch next to its `package.json`). The plugin stores nothing itself.
- A retry-policy change is meant for the **next model request**, with **no backend restart**: every
  route's policy is captured at **registration** (`packages/llm/llm/src/index.ts:435-470`), and each
  provider re-registers its routes when the loader reports a changed volatile value (after a settings
  save). `llm-deepseek`/`llm-deepseek-account` do that in `llm-deepseek/src/host.ts:82-90`;
  `llm-pi-ai` includes `retryPolicy` in its registration facts and re-registers on
  `loader/volatile-update` (`llm-pi-ai/src/index.ts:108-120,289-319`).
- A request already in flight keeps the policy it started with.
- A route-card timeout change is persisted in the provider's namespace and is picked up by the next
  request/route registration, with no backend restart; a route that is dormant or whose namespace is not
  served is not listed here, so it cannot be written.
- A fetch-timer change is picked up on the **next HTTP dispatch** (the wrapper re-reads the live values on
  every request) with **no backend restart**. The values persist in this plugin's settings namespace like
  any other Host setting; clearing them (or Reset) restores the system-default state.
- Picking a route writes nothing. The deviating list and the picker recompute whenever any provider form
  snapshot changes (a write from another page included), while the provider **directory** itself is read
  once per mount.
- The page only needs a reload to appear after install/upgrade (and a first install may need a backend
  restart). A value change does not need either.

### The two halves

`index.js` (Host) owns the global-defaults `Config` — six `.volatile()` retry fields plus the two
process-wide fetch fields — plus `DEFAULT_TUNE`/`TUNE_OPTIONS`, `DEFAULT_FETCH`/`FETCH_KEYS`/
`FETCH_OPTIONS`, `PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_FIELDS`/`PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_KEYS`/`PROVIDER_TIMEOUT_OPTIONS` (frozen
metadata for the route cards; NOT `Config` fields), `validateTune()` (the cross-field guard for the
retry rules the schema cannot express), and `apply(ctx, config)`. `apply()` has three jobs: it registers
the documented `auto: false` page policy for this namespace (future-proofing: no shipped DSH client
builds pages from a namespace schema yet), installs the opt-in fetch-timeout dispatcher wrapper
described above, and runs the **manual same-turn retry** (the `agent/request-error` listener plus the
authenticated `state`/`decide` route). It never projects any value onto a provider. `client.js`
(browser) is the page — one **Global settings** card followed by one **Per-route overrides** tier — plus
the **Retry bar** above the composer. The page reads the provider directory from the Client Remote `llm`
namespace, paints each route's effective policy and stored timeout leaves from that route's config form,
writes leaf-path operations back through the same form, and never owns a copy of a route's state. The
provider routes are the source of truth; `DEFAULT_TUNE` is the preset the page offers, not a fallback
layer, and the fetch timers are a process-wide side effect rather than a fallback for any provider.

## Manual retry

A second feature, independent of the settings page: when a model request fails and the automatic retry
policy has already declined (no eligible code, retries exhausted, or recovery declined), a **Retry bar**
appears above the composer in the session that owns the failure. It shows the failure code, the
provider, the message, **Retry** / **Dismiss**, and a muted **`Attempt n/5`** indicator. It appears only
for an open, browser-watched session (`normal` mode, or a route with no stored policy; `always` already
retries every failure, so it never asks).

**Retry** re-issues that model request in the **same turn and step**. It is a re-dispatch, not a new
turn: the user message is not re-sent as a new message, `step/start` is not duplicated, and earlier
steps' tool results stay in the history. Each attempt re-runs request preparation and `llm.prepareCall()`, so the call is fresh and its
retry policy is re-captured; a tuning save made while the bar is up therefore applies to the retried
request (the global-defaults card is still only a preset — it does not rewrite a route by itself).

The manual decision **bypasses the retry-policy budget**: `maxRetries` and `retryableCodes` are not
consulted and no `llm/retry` event is logged. The only stops are the **5 manual retries per turn** and
**one click per attempt** (each new failure prompts once).

**Dismiss** ends the turn with the normal error row. So do the 90-second decision timeout, canceling the
turn, disposing the plugin, and closing the page (the last one after the timeout: the bar needs a page
polling the Host). While the bar is up the turn is still running, so the composer is disabled; **Cancel**
is the escape hatch. Only the first valid decision counts — a stale tab cannot settle a newer prompt.
The bar is host-authenticated and reachable only through the plugin's own `POST`+JSON route; headless or
CLI runs and crash-closed turns never see it and fall back to the old behavior. A retried call may repeat
side effects if the model re-issues the same tool calls, and the bar shows the provider, not the model
(the failure payload carries no model field).

## Troubleshooting

- **The nav row is missing.** The bundle is not loaded into the active pr

# `dsh-use-repo-tmp`

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Prompt guidance that tells the model to put scratch files, temporary downloads, and generated
artifacts under `tmp/` at the root of the workspace — the current working directory — instead
of `/tmp`, and resolves that directory for the session in the runtime-context snapshot.

It is **guidance only**. It registers one static system-prompt section and one runtime context.
It does not intercept tool calls, does not guard or rewrite any tool, does not swap the file or
shell provider, and installs nothing outside the active profile.

## The problem it addresses

`/tmp` does not mean the same directory to every surface of a sandboxed DSH session:

- **A confined shell command gets a private, ephemeral `/tmp`.** On the Linux bwrap runner, a
  `workspace-write` command runs with `--tmpfs /tmp` plus a writable bind of the workspace
  (`packages/sandbox/sandbox-local/src/profiles.ts`). The tmpfs is created for that one command
  and discarded when it exits, so a file written to `/tmp` by `bash` is gone by the next
  command. A persistent terminal session is one long-lived bwrap process, so its tmpfs lasts for
  that session — it is still not the host `/tmp` and it disappears with the session.
- **The file tools write the host `/tmp`.** `read`, `write`, and `edit` run in-process behind the
  file-effect fence, whose `workspace-write` allow-list is the workspace root, the host `/tmp`,
  and `os.tmpdir()` (`packages/sandbox/sandbox/src/roots.ts`).

The two surfaces therefore never share `/tmp` under that runner: a shell-written file is
invisible to the file tools (and dies with the command), and a file-tool-written file is
invisible to the next shell command. `tmp/` inside the workspace is the one directory every
surface can share and that survives the turn.

This asymmetry is **runner-dependent**, and the injected text says so: it scopes the durability
claim to bwrap-sandboxed runners and never claims that the host `/tmp` is wiped or deleted. Under
the Landlock runner `/tmp` is granted read-write and is the real host `/tmp`, so there the advice
is a convention about durability and consistency, not a workaround for a missing directory. On
every runner, keeping intermediates inside the workspace is still the safer habit: it is the one
location the workspace-write policy promises, and it makes a task's artifacts inspectable and
disposable after the fact.

## What is injected

Both registrations live in the plugin's own Cordis layer, so one `apply()` covers every Agent in
the composition — the Lead, subagents, and teammates.

| Seam | Name | Order | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| System-prompt section | `repo-tmp:policy` | `950` | Static text, `interpolate: false`. |
| Runtime context | `repo-tmp:root` | `111` | `Durable scratch directory for this session: "<workspace>/tmp".`, `interpolate: false`. |

Order `950` places the section between `FILE_REFERENCE` (900) and `TOOL_BASH` (1000), so the
general policy is read before the tool-specific shell guidance. Order `111` is one past
`SANDBOX_POLICY` (110), so the resolved directory renders directly beside the "Current DSH file
policy" line. Both orders are written as literals because a custom section or context name is
not part of `getSectionOrder`/`getContextOrder`'s typed placement union.

The section is deliberately **cache-stable**: it carries no session-dependent path, no
interpolation variables, and no per-session value, so every session and every cached prompt
prefix shares one text. The only absolute path in it is the literal `/tmp` being contrasted.

The context is dynamic and value-bearing. It resolves the workspace root as
`ctx.get('workingDirectory')?.get(session) ?? session.header?.cwd` — the optional lookup keeps
the bundle loadable in a profile that does not mount the working-directory service — and
contributes an empty string (which renders nothing) when no Agent is being assembled. The path
is quoted with `JSON.stringify`, so a directory containing spaces or unusual characters cannot
break the sentence.

Injected policy text:

```text
Put scratch files, temporary downloads, and generated artifacts under `tmp/` at the root of the workspace — the current working directory — instead of `/tmp`.

`/tmp` is not durable on a bwrap-sandboxed runner: a confined shell there gets its own empty `/tmp` that is not the host `/tmp` the file tools read, so anything written there can vanish or stay invisible to other tools.

Run `mkdir -p tmp` before the first use, then address the files by workspace-relative path (`tmp/out.log`) or by absolute path inside the workspace. Keep intermediates there while a task needs them; do not put tracked deliverables in `tmp/`.
```

## Install

The bundle is a normal profile plugin, not a workspace package. Capture its path in this plugins
workspace, then install it with the DSH CLI:

```sh
# in this plugins workspace
PLUGIN="$(pwd)/dsh-use-repo-tmp"

# with the DSH CLI
dsh plugin --profile web add link:"$PLUGIN"
```

The plugin then loads on the next full page load; no build step is needed, because the bundle is
plain ESM loaded from source. In a running GUI session the same step is the `plugin_manager`
tool with `action: install_bundle` and `target: "$PLUGIN"`.

Beyond a local checkout, the bundle is distributable without a registry: `npm pack` in this directory
produces a tarball that installs by absolute path (or an `https:` URL), and a clone installs by Git with a
subdirectory selector, because this repository has no root `package.json`:

```sh
npm pack    # -> dsh-<name>-<version>.tgz (local only; nothing is published)
```

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/dsh-<name>-<version>.tgz" })
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "git+https://github.com/jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins.git#<commit>&path:/dsh-<name>" })
```

Nothing here is published to an npm registry.

## Verify

```sh
# from this plugin directory
node --check index.js && node verify.mjs

# from the plugins workspace root
node dsh-use-repo-tmp/verify.mjs
```

`verify.mjs` is hermetic: no network, no model, no filesystem write. It checks the manifest and
the bundle patch (deep-parsed with the js-yaml of a reachable DSH checkout — the checkout of the
`DSH_HARNESS_CHECKOUT` override or the sibling `deepseek-harness` directory; when neither is
reachable the deep parse prints an explicit `SKIP` naming the reason and the strict text fallback
still runs), drives `apply()` against a fake Cordis context, and asserts the section's name,
order, cache-stability (no variables, no session-dependent path, only the fixed `/tmp` token),
and the context's resolution order — service first, Session header as the fallback, `''` and no
throw when neither exists. It also compares the policy block quoted above byte-for-byte with the
text `apply()` registers. It passes from the plugin directory and from the plugins workspace
root.

Repositories that adopt this convention should ignore the directory:

```gitignore
/tmp/
```

## Alternatives considered and rejected

- **Deny `/tmp` at the file tools** (`PreToolDecision` / `tools.guard`). A guard sees the call,
  but a pre-tool decision can only allow, deny, cancel, or ask
  (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`), so denying produces a failed call and a retry, not a
  file at a usable path. It is also the wrong claim about policy: the host `/tmp` really is
  writable through the file tools.
- **Swap or wrap the file/shell provider** to remap `/tmp` into the workspace. That widens the
  sandbox's trust boundary to save the model one path segment, and it would silently change the
  meaning of every command that legitimately means the host `/tmp`.
- **Rewrite tool arguments** before dispatch. DSH has no such seam by design: "Input rewriting
  is excluded because arguments are already logged and presented"
  (`packages/core/tools/src/index.ts`). The guidance goes into the prompt because the prompt is
  where behaviour can be changed without lying about what the tools did.

## What it cannot do

- It cannot enforce anything. A model that ignores the section can still write to `/tmp`, and
  the plugin has no opinion about the result.
- It cannot make a shell's `/tmp` and the file tools' `/tmp` agree; only the sandbox runner and
  the tools own that.
- It changes no permission. Under `workspace-write`, `tmp/` inside the workspace is writable;
  under `read-only` nothing is, and this plugin does not widen that.
- It does not add, hide, or reorder tools. It contributes one cache-stable prompt section and
  one runtime-context line, and it persists nothing between sessions.
- It assumes the workspace root is where the task's files belong. A session whose
  working directory is intentionally outside the project (for example a scratch directory the
  user chose) gets that directory named, which is the honest answer for that session.

## Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | The static policy section, the dynamic scratch-directory context, `apply()`. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch: one top-level insert so every Agent receives the guidance. |
| `locale/*.json` | Plugin-list display metadata: the English and Chinese titles. |
| `verify.mjs` | Hermetic self-check of the manifest, the patch, and both registrations. |
| `README.md` | This document. |
| `CONTRACT.md` | The frozen surface of the bundle. |

The bundles in this repository are licensed under **GPL-3.0-or-later**. The canonical GNU GPL v3 text
ships with the package as [LICENSE](LICENSE); the "or later" grant lives in the `license` field of
`package.json` and in this notice, not in the unchanged license text.

`npm pack` tarball, or a Git URL pointing at this repository.

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Five standalone DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin bundles.
Each one installs into a DSH host as a profile bundle, carries its own English and Simplified Chinese
README, and ships a hermetic verification suite that runs without a live Host.

| `dsh-compaction-tuner` | One page that owns the full eleven-key `compaction-basic` policy and pushes the tune into every agent preset in the active profile. | Settings → **Compaction tuner** (last nav row) | [English](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.md) · [中文](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` | Adds the **Lead agent only leads** preset — a Team Lead that delegates every job and never waits on a teammate — plus the host plugin that enforces the tool restrictions. | Session preset picker; Settings → **Lead agent only leads** for the tool toggles | [English](dsh-lead-agent-only-leads/README.md) · [中文](dsh-lead-agent-only-leads/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-llm-api-call-tuning` | One Settings page that tunes the model-request retry policy of every active provider route — retry mode, max retries, backoff delays, jitter, and retryable failure codes — plus the per-route provider timeouts (stream idle, SDK request, Files API) and the two process-wide HTTP fetch timeouts shared by every provider, web search, and HTTP MCP server. | Settings → **LLM API call tuning** (last nav row) | [English](dsh-llm-api-call-tuning/README.md) · [中文](dsh-llm-api-call-tuning/README.zh.md) |
| `dsh-use-repo-tmp` | Prompt-only guidance that sends scratch files to `<workspace>/tmp` instead of `/tmp`, as one static system-prompt section plus a runtime-context line. | No UI | [English](dsh-use-repo-tmp/README.md) · [中文](dsh-use-repo-tmp/README.zh.md) |

## Requirements

- **DSH `^0.2.2-rc.3`** — declared as `engines.dsh` in every manifest, so a DSH host outside that range
  refuses the install.
- These packages declare no separate Node.js version. Their verification scripts are plain ESM and run
  with the `node` binary you already use for DSH.

## Installation

A bundle is an npm package whose `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`; installing it adds that patch
layer to the active DSH profile. Three routes work today. Only the path/`link:` route is registry-free: a
tarball or Git install of `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` also resolves its one declared dependency,
`@deepseek-ai/schemastery@3.19.0`, from the registry, so that route needs a reachable registry, or that
dependency already present on the host.

### From a local checkout (absolute path)

From this repository's root, with the installed DSH CLI on `PATH`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add link:"$PWD/dsh-backend-restart"
```

From a DSH source checkout instead, run its own script with an absolute bundle path:
`pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add link:/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-backend-restart`.

Or from a running GUI session, with the `plugin_manager` tool:

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/to/deepseek-harness-plugins/dsh-backend-restart" })
```

The installer links the package into the profile and records the bundle row; the plugin loads on the next
full page load.

### From a tarball

`npm pack` inside a bundle directory produces a local tarball that installs by absolute path (or by an
`https:` URL):

```sh
cd dsh-backend-restart
npm pack    # -> dsh-backend-restart-0.2.2-rc.3.tgz
```

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "/abs/path/dsh-backend-restart-0.2.2-rc.3.tgz" })
```

### From Git (subdirectory selector)

There is no root `package.json`, so a bare `github:jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins` install cannot
resolve a package. Address one bundle with a `path:` selector instead:

```js
plugin_manager({ action: "install_bundle", target: "git+https://github.com/jinluchang/deepseek-harness-plugins.git#<commit>&path:/dsh-backend-restart" })
```

Pin a commit for `<commit>`; the same spec form works for the other four bundles with their own
`path:/dsh-<name>`.

## Nothing is published to npm

These bundles are **not published**: no version of these packages exists on npm. Their manifests set
`"private": false` and carry publish metadata, so a release is possible later, but nothing has been
published to any registry.

## Notes

- `dsh-compaction-tuner` writes its tune into the profile's preset rows on the first boot; uninstalling it
  does not revert that. See *Install behaviour change* in its [README](dsh-compaction-tuner/README.md).
- The preset added by `dsh-lead-agent-only-leads` is identified from the preset a session currently runs,
  not from its creation header: a session switched or resumed under **Lead agent only leads** is
  constrained without a restart. Installing the bundle itself still needs one Host restart to load its

## Verification

Each bundle ships a self-contained `verify.mjs`; no network, no server, and no live Host. Set
`DSH_HARNESS_CHECKOUT` to a DSH source checkout — it is required for a green run: the compaction tuner
fails loudly without it, and the other suites resolve the checkout's libraries through it.

```sh

node dsh-backend-restart/verify.mjs          # 13 checks passed
```
